records.title: Director of Quality, Regulatory & Improvement
records.description:
***Title:*** ***Director of Quality, Regulatory and Improvement***

**Job Summary:**
----------------

This senior leadership role leads the quality departments for all Deringer-Ney locations globally. The Director implements best practices and metrics to coordinate all teams under a unified Quality Management System and is responsible for ensuring that the company's products, services, and manufacturing processes comply with strict government laws, industry standards, and internal quality systems. The role plans, coordinates, and directs the activities of the quality assurance and compliance programs to ensure the production of consistent, reliable products that meet or exceed established standards, and leads the continuous improvement team to support, train, and execute the DNIOS system.

***Supervisory Responsibilities:****Yes*

**Duties/Responsibilities:**
----------------------------

* Manage all quality departments by formulating, developing, and overseeing global goals, objectives, policies, procedures, systems, and outcomes pertaining to quality controls, assessments, and audits.
* Quality Management Systems (QMS): Build, maintain, and continuously improve QMS frameworks (such as ISO 13485 and ISO 9001).
* Develop a high-performance team by acquiring, developing, training, coaching, cultivating, and managing talented Quality Control personnel.
* Maintain and improve the quality system through routine system audits and corrective actions, and ensure that corrective actions, whether internal or external, are handled in a timely manner.
* Risk & Lifecycle Management: Oversee design controls, validation packages, complaint handling, and post-market surveillance (such as Automotive Reporting).
* Manage and maintain quality inspection and product release programs for raw materials, work in process (WIP), and finished goods.
* Regulatory Compliance & Filings: Lead product submissions and act as the primary liaison during agency audits.
* Disseminate quality awareness, adherence, and developments to global stakeholders by scheduling and performing regional quality audits and by ensuring that ISO systems are managed and maintained.
* Serve as an active member of the DNI Leadership Team, sharing the function's progress toward its goals while setting, and driving toward, an aspirational vision for a best-in-class quality department.
* Create a Cost of Poor Quality metric for the organization and set specific goals to improve quality performance across the company.
* Lead the development of the Annual Strategic Planning (P.D.C.A.) Cycle to include the Improvement Process.
* Lead the organization in attaining key metrics based on Balanced Scorecard (BSC) Objectives. Understand the department's key performance indicators and leading and lagging indicators, and contribute to achieving these goals, both individually and as a team.
* With the CIP Team, perform systematic audits designed to confirm that process standards are being utilized and met (BSC One-Page Reports).
* Interact with and make recommendations and presentations to the Executive Leadership Group via standardized checks: weekly, monthly, quarterly, and year-end. Maintain the PDCA Cycle while focusing on BSC Objectives.

**Required Skills/Abilities:**
------------------------------

* Strong background in ISO 9000 system management, including training and auditing.
* Strong background in ISO 13485 system management and thorough knowledge of FDA requirements and other international standards that regulate the medical device industry.
* Knowledge of automated inspection equipment, including vision systems and coordinate measuring devices.
* Adept at delegating and managing multiple tasks with various levels of priority.
* Excellent communication skills; must be able to present ideas, results, and requirements effectively throughout the organization and to the customer on a timely basis.
* Expert skill set in applied statistics, reliability, design of experiments, MSA, GR&R, and project management.
* Fluency with various software packages commonly used in project management, database, SPC, word processing, and data acquisition.
* Analytical, problem-solving, project management, facilitation, and decision-making skills are essential.
* Strong leadership skills with the ability to motivate, coach, resolve conflict, and promote teamwork.
* Ability to see and hear the facts from several viewpoints while promoting success through interactive problem solving and teamwork.

**Experience & Education Requirements:**
----------------------------------------

* Technical degree (BS, BSE, or BSME) with a minimum of 10 years' experience in quality engineering or quality management.
* Strong preference for relevant industry experience in a metals or electrical connectors company or similar.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in Quality Assurance, Quality Control, or Regulatory Affairs within a regulated field such as medical devices, automotive, or defense.
* Preferred certifications: Regulatory Affairs Certification (RAC), Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), or Certified Quality Engineer (CQE).
* Demonstrated project management skills in the areas of process control, SPC, automotive PPAP submission, and statistical analysis.
* Lean Green Belt or Black Belt certification, Six Sigma, and DMAIC process experience.
* Actively continuing training through courses and seminars.

***Physical Requirements:***

* Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
* Must be able to lift 15 pounds at times.
* Must be able to access and navigate each department at the organization’s facilities.
* Travel to other locations as required.

The role plans, coordinates, and directs the activities of the quality assurance and compliance programs to ensure the production of consistent, reliable products that meet or exceed established standards, and leads the continuous improvement team to support, train, and execute the DNIOS system.

records.title: Director, Quality Engineering
records.description:
HHAeXchange is the leading technology platform for home and community-based care. Founded in 2008, HHAeXchange was born out of an idea to create a fully comprehensive end-to-end homecare solution to help people who are aging or have disabilities thrive in their homes and communities. Our employees are passionate about transforming the healthcare space by building the only homecare ecosystem that fully connects patients, personal care providers, managed care organizations, and states.

The Director, Quality Engineering will lead the enterprise-wide quality strategy and Quality Assurance (QA) program across HHAeXchange. This role is responsible for standardizing testing processes and tools, driving test automation, and ensuring our products meet high standards for reliability, performance, security, and accessibility. The Director, Quality Engineering will oversee functional and non-functional testing practices, including accessibility (WCAG) and security-related validation, and will own processes that support customer User Acceptance Testing (UAT).

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential job duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**This is a fully remote opportunity for candidates located in the EST or CST time zones within the US only.**

### **Essential Job Duties**

* **Enterprise Quality Leadership:** Develop, implement, and lead the overall quality strategy and QA operating model across the organization.
* **Standardize Testing Processes:** Define and enforce consistent testing approaches including test planning, test cases, regression strategy, and release readiness criteria.
* **Tooling Ownership:** Select, implement, and manage enterprise testing tools for test management, automation, performance, accessibility, and security validation.
* **Automation Strategy:** Drive increased automated test coverage across UI, API, mobile, and services, reducing reliance on manual regression testing.
* **Compliance, Accessibility & VPAT Reporting:**
 + Lead accessibility testing programs aligned to WCAG 2.1+
 + Oversee creation and maintenance of Voluntary Product Accessibility Templates (VPATs) and Accessibility Conformance Reports
 + Partner with Product, Legal, and Compliance to respond to customer accessibility requirements and audits
* **Security & Compliance Testing Support:** Coordinate with Security teams on SAST/DAST, vulnerability validation, and remediation tracking.
* **Customer UAT Support:**
 + Define and support customer UAT strategies and environments
 + Provide test plans, data guidance, and defect triage support during customer acceptance testing cycles
 + Ensure feedback from UAT informs release decisions and product quality improvements
* **Quality Metrics & Reporting:** Establish KPIs to measure product quality, defect escape rate, automation coverage, UAT outcomes, and release readiness; communicate results to leadership.
* **Shift-Left Quality Practices:** Embed quality earlier in the development lifecycle through collaboration on requirements, acceptance criteria, and CI/CD integration.
* **Incident & Defect Management:** Oversee defect triage for high-priority production and pre-production issues and ensure timely resolution and root-cause prevention.
* **Cross-Functional Collaboration:** Work closely with Product Management, Engineering, DevOps, Security, and Compliance to ensure alignment of quality practices across releases.
* **Organizational Leadership**: Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing team of QA engineers, SDETs, automation engineers, and accessibility/compliance testers.
* **Continuous Improvement:** Identify quality gaps and drive process improvements that improve product reliability, reduce rework, and increase delivery confidence.
* **Release Governance:** Participate in release readiness reviews and serve as a key stakeholder in go/no-go decisions.
* **Coding agent advocacy:** **Help onboard team members to AI development tools. Share techniques, prompt patterns, and review practices that make AI-augmented development effective and safe in a regulated environment.**

### **Other Job Duties**

* Other duties as assigned by supervisor or HHAeXchange leader.

### **Travel Requirements**

* Travel up to 10%, including overnight travel

### **Required Education, Experience, Certifications and Skills**

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field required.
* 10+ years of experience in software engineering within a software product company, with a focus on developing scalable, high-performance systems.
* 4+ years leading QA organizations or enterprise quality programs.
* Proven experience designing and implementing standardized QA processes and test automation strategies in SaaS environments.
* Hands-on experience implementing automated testing frameworks integrated into CI/CD pipelines.
* Experience with accessibility testing and standards such as WCAG 2.1+ and authoring VPATs/ACRs.
* Experience supporting security testing practices such as vulnerability scanning, SAST/DAST, and penetration test remediation validation.
* Experience supporting or running customer UAT processes.
* Strong understanding of quality metrics (defect rates, coverage, MTTR, escape rate, etc.) and how to operationalize them.
* Background working in cloud-based architectures and microservices environments.
* Demonstrated success collaborating across engineering, product, and security teams in a fast-paced environment.
* Strong leadership skills with experience managing and developing QA and automation teams.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex topics to technical and non-technical partners.
* **AI/ML fundamentals:** Familiarity with LLM APIs, prompt engineering, and how generative AI can be applied in a product context. Direct project experience preferred.

The base salary range for this US-based, full-time, and exempt position is $175,000-195,000/yr, not including variable compensation. An employee’s exact starting salary will be based on various factors including but not limited to experience, education, training, merit, location, and the ability to exemplify the HHAeXchange core values.

This is a benefits-eligible position. HHAeXchange offers competitive health plans, paid time-off, company paid holidays, 401K retirement program with a Company elected match, including other company sponsored programs.

HHAeXchange is an equal-opportunity employer. The Company offers employment opportunities to all applicants and employees without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, medical condition, marital status, veteran status, citizenship, genetic information, hairstyles, or any other status protected by local or federal law.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

records.title: VP Distribution Operations
records.description:
**Meet Vestis®:** For the People Who Make It All Work
 
At Vestis®, we provide uniforms, workplace supplies, and professional cleaning that help businesses simplify their workday and keep their teams safe, confident, and focused on what matters most. More than a provider, we are a partner in productivity, trusted to keep you running.
 
Join us and build a career supporting the people who make it all work.
 
 
Overview
 
The Vice President of Distribution Center Operations will lead the product distribution strategy and drive an economically competitive operation that delivers both best-in-class customer experience and distribution cost advantages across all facilities supporting Vestis Rental and Direct Sale customers.
 
This leader will influence and reinforce a portfolio of core values and accountability standards centered on safety, workforce engagement, customer experience, operational efficiency, and innovative solutions that support business goals. This role is responsible for deploying strategies and actionable plans that deliver measurable performance improvement.
 
This leader will also define and advance the technology roadmap for Distribution Center Operations, identifying opportunities to leverage artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, automation, advanced analytics, and other emerging technologies to improve safety, productivity, quality, service, capacity, and cost.
 
The Vice President will promote data-driven performance visibility, real-time corrective action, and strong cross-functional collaboration. This leader will work effectively with business partners to identify, address, and resolve operational issues.
 
This role will set goals and oversee key metrics related to customer fill rates, customer satisfaction, footprint utilization, inventory management, optimization and total DC cost, along with other key measures tied to Distribution Center Operations.
 
Responsibilities/Essential Functions
 

* Set and deliver the overall vision and distribution strategy for national and international distribution centers to ensure end-to-end customer needs are met at the lowest possible cost.
* Lead a high-performing team of supply chain practitioners, with direct and indirect responsibility for an organization of more than 600 employees.
* Partner with Human Resources to design and implement workforce strategies for each distribution center location, including the evolution of workforce skills needed to support increasingly automated and technology-enabled operations.
* Define objectives, establish key performance metrics, and create a regular review cadence across safety, quality, fill rate, customer satisfaction, inventory management, budget performance, and other critical operating areas.
* Implement metrics, processes, and operating routines that drive accountability and ensure results.
* Improve costs year over year through disciplined operational execution and continuous improvement.
* Drive performance improvement through the use of continuous improvement methodology.
* Build strong cross-functional partnerships to identify, escalate, and resolve operational issues and improvement opportunities.
* Set the strategic direction and oversee major projects across national and international locations, including distribution center layout changes, equipment needs, space utilization, capital expenses, major repairs, and related operational requirements.
* Manage domestic and international direct and indirect reporting teams to ensure processes and procedures are consistent across all facilities.
* Lead the annual budgeting process in partnership with DC Operations and Direct Sale Finance Teams and Sales Leadership.
* Stay current on information, technology, and trends affecting functional areas; promote innovation and make appropriate recommendations to executive leadership.
* Develop and execute a multi-year distribution technology and automation roadmap, including the evaluation and adoption of AI, robotics, material-handling automation, advanced analytics, and emerging distribution technologies where they provide measurable operational and financial value.
* Evaluate opportunities to automate manual and repetitive processes across receiving, put-away, inventory movement, picking, packing, sortation, shipping, and related distribution workflows.
* Establish business cases and success measures for major automation and technology investments, including productivity improvement, service impact, safety, capacity, labor requirements, operating cost, capital requirements, and return on investment.
* Partner with Information Technology, Engineering, Supply Chain, Finance, Human Resources, and external technology partners to successfully pilot, scale, and operationalize new distribution technologies across the network.
* Use data, predictive analytics, and AI-enabled decision support to improve demand and capacity planning, inventory positioning, workforce planning, asset utilization, operational visibility, and decision-making.
* Build a culture of innovation in which technology augments the workforce, improves safety and efficiency, and prepares the distribution organization for future operating requirements.
* Set the overall strategy for operational performance planning to drive quality standards and efficiency.
* Oversee and monitor safety and security in accordance with national and international requirements for facilities and employees. Ensure proper training and adherence to company requirements.
* Drive employment decisions and recommendations, including hiring, retention, improvement plans, transfers, promotions, corrective actions, terminations, and pay adjustments.
* Manage employee performance and support improvement through coaching, mentoring, and formal performance reviews.
* Recommend, plan, and implement employee training and skill development activities.
* Lead communication on company and departmental issues, priorities, and goals. Provide oversight of employee growth and development through weekly team meetings, regular one-on-one meetings, coaching, performance management, training, and company-sponsored learning opportunities.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities
 

* Demonstrated understanding of technical issues within a global distribution framework.
* Strong understanding of modern distribution technologies, including warehouse automation, robotics, AI, machine learning applications, advanced analytics, and automated material-handling solutions.
* Ability to translate emerging technology into practical operational use cases and measurable business outcomes rather than implementing technology for technology’s sake.
* Strong understanding of automation investment strategy, including business-case development, scalability, change management, operational readiness, and return on investment.
* Ability to lead transformation in environments where automated and traditional operations may need to coexist across different facilities.
* Strong project leadership and cross-functional leadership experience.
* Ability to think, plan, and execute strategically.
* Ability to influence and build consensus with executive leadership.
* Comfortable operating in ambiguity.
* Decisive and persuasive, with a strong sense of urgency and a proven ability to drive results.
* Strong organizational skills.
* Excellent analytical skills and technical capabilities.
* Willingness and ability to travel extensively, both nationally and internationally.

Working Environment/Safety Requirements
 
Role is based in Lawrenceville, GA.
 
Requires up to 50% travel across the U.S. and Canada.
 
Work includes distribution center, plant, and office environments, including corporate office interaction in Roswell, GA.
 
Must comply with all company safety, security, and site-specific requirements.
 
Experience/Qualifications
 

* 15 years of experience leading a large workforce in a high-volume, fast-paced global distribution or manufacturing network.
* Bachelor’s degree in business, supply chain operations, engineering, or a related field required; MBA preferred.
* Recognized thought leader and expert within business, supply chain, logistics, and/or global distribution disciplines.
* Experience developing, implementing, and delivering long-term distribution and supply chain strategies.
* Deep understanding of the work apparel business, including financials, products, services, and market dynamics.
* Technologically adept, with the ability to envision and oversee the implementation of technology-based solutions.
* Demonstrated experience developing or executing distribution automation, robotics, AI, advanced analytics, or digital transformation initiatives within complex, high-volume operations.
* Experience evaluating automation technologies and building investment recommendations based on operational benefit, scalability, capital requirements, and return on investment.
* Experience leading technology-enabled operational change at scale, including the people, process, training, and change-management requirements associated with automation.

Headquartered in Roswell, GA, Vestis® is the second largest provider in the industry with over 300,000 customer locations and approximately 20,000 teammates across North America. Vestis® is a leader in the B2B uniform and workplace supplies category. Vestis® provides clean and safe uniform services and workplace supplies to a broad range of North American customers from Fortune 500 companies to locally owned small businesses across a broad set of end markets. The Company’s comprehensive service offering includes a full-service uniform rental program, cleanroom and other specialty garment processing, floor mats, towels, linens, managed restroom services, first aid supplies and more.
 
 
Vestis® is an equal-opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, relation, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or veteran status.
 
 
Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veterans/Individuals with Disabilities
 
This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws. For further information, please review the Know Your Rights notice from the Department of Labor.
 
 
Vestis Commitment to Equal Opportunity Employment
 
If you are a job seeker with a disability and require a reasonable accommodation to apply for one of our jobs, you will find the contact information below to request the appropriate accommodation.
 
Reasonable Accommodations and the Online Application Process
 
Consistent with Vestis and Canadian Linen’s commitment to equal employment opportunity, we provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities who need assistance in applying electronically for a position with Vestis or Canadian Linen, unless doing so would impose an undue hardship. To request a reasonable accommodation for this purpose, please call 1-833-901-8823 or email us at accessibility@vestis.com.
 
Please note that this phone number is to be used solely to request an accommodation with respect to the online application process. Calls for any other reason will not be returned. Reasonable accommodation requests are considered on a case-by-case basis.
 
Thank you for your interest in an employment opportunity with Vestis, Canadian Linen and Québec Linge.

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
**DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS**

*Ritchey Livestock ID* | Fort Collins, Colorado | Full-Time, Onsite

Run the Operation. Build the Team. Shape What's Next.

**This Role Is For Builders.**

**We're looking for someone who can run a great operation today—and help build the company we'll become tomorrow.**

At Ritchey Livestock ID, we believe farmers and ranchers are the unsung heroes of our world. They work long hours, in every kind of weather, doing the essential work of feeding the rest of us. They don't ask for much in return. The least we can do is get our little part right.

For more than 60 years, we've manufactured livestock identification tags that ranchers can count on. Our products may be small, but the responsibility we feel to our customers is anything but.

We're a profitable, growing American manufacturer with a loyal nationwide customer base. We've recently completed the largest facility investment in our company's history, opening a new manufacturing operation in Fort Collins, Colorado. Now we're building the people, systems, and culture to carry Ritchey into its next chapter.

**We're looking for a hands-on Director of Operations who can lead that effort—and potentially grow into a broader executive leadership role as the company evolves.**

This is not a position for someone who wants to lead from behind a desk. You'll spend meaningful time on the production floor, working alongside your managers, solving real problems, and helping people succeed.

You'll also be expected to think beyond today's production schedule: developing leaders, building systems, improving performance, and preparing Ritchey for its next stage of growth.

**The Opportunity**

You'll lead approximately 45 people across manufacturing, engraving, shipping, and related operations, working directly with our CEO.

Your mission is twofold: **Run an exceptional operation today. Build the people, processes, and accountability that make excellence repeatable tomorrow.**

You'll own performance across safety, quality, on-time delivery, productivity, cost, and team development.

You'll be responsible for developing department managers, improving operational systems, driving continuous improvement, and building a culture where people take pride in their work and ownership of their results.

**Your First Year: Real Challenges, Real Opportunity**

We've made a major investment in our future. Now comes the work of making that investment pay off.

Here are five challenges you'll help us tackle:

* **Strengthen our new manufacturing operation.** Continue ramping up our Fort Collins facility, improving production stability, quality, capacity, and efficiency.
* **Improve scheduling and throughput.** Build better production planning and workflows across manufacturing, engraving, and shipping to improve delivery performance and reduce bottlenecks.
* **Build systems that last.** Reduce dependence on individual employees by developing practical SOPs, standardized processes, clear performance measures, and repeatable operating routines.
* **Develop our next generation of leaders.** Coach newer managers, strengthen accountability, and build employee development practices that help great people grow.
* **Drive continuous improvement.** Use Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, and practical root-cause problem-solving to reduce waste, improve productivity, and create measurable, sustainable improvements.

You'll have meaningful ownership of these challenges, the support of our leadership team, and the freedom to make a lasting impact.

**Who We're Looking For**

We're looking for a rare combination of heart, head, and hands. Someone who can lead people, build systems, solve problems, and roll up their sleeves when the work demands it.

**What you must bring:**

* **Proven People Leadership:** Demonstrated success leading teams in a manufacturing or production environment, ideally 20 or more employees, with experience developing supervisors or managers and holding people accountable.
* **Demonstrated Systems Building:** A track record of improving processes, implementing operational improvements, and building systems that continue to work without your constant involvement.
* **High Agency & Ownership:** The judgment, initiative, work ethic, and follow-through to take responsibility for results, solve difficult problems, and lead confidently in a hands-on environment.

**What we'd love to see:**

* Experience in plastic injection molding, extrusion, or related manufacturing processes.
* Practical experience applying Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other structured continuous improvement methods. Certifications are valued but not required.
* Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems, production scheduling, inventory management, purchasing, and quality systems.
* Strong financial and analytical skills, with an understanding of how operational decisions affect profitability.
* Experience developing managers, building teams, and helping an organization prepare for growth.

We value experience, but we're far more interested in what you've accomplished than the number of years on your résumé.

**Seasoned plastics professionals and exceptional leaders from other manufacturing environments are equally encouraged to apply.** What matters most is demonstrated leadership, systems thinking, operational judgment, and a willingness to keep learning.

***The Ritchey Way***

Our culture is built around one simple commitment: **DO RIGHT BY THE RANCH.**

Four core principles guide how we show up every day:

**ASK WHY. ASK WHAT IF.** — Learn the work. Make it better.

**MAKE THE SMALL THINGS COUNT.** — Bring care to the details, seen or unseen.

**NO SIDELINES.** — See it. Say it. Help solve it.

**BE GOOD TO WORK WITH.** — Carry your share. Be good company.

These aren't just words on a wall. They're the standards we hold ourselves and each other to. As our Director of Operations, you'll help bring *The Ritchey Way* to life through your leadership, your example, and the team you build.

**Why Ritchey?**

We're small enough that your ideas matter, but established and ambitious enough that your work can make a lasting difference. You'll have direct access to ownership, real authority to drive improvement, and a genuine opportunity to help shape the company's future.

**We're intentionally looking for someone with the potential to grow beyond operations.**

For the right individual who demonstrates exceptional leadership, business judgment, and results, this role could become a pathway toward broader company leadership, potentially including a future President or General Manager position.

That opportunity isn't guaranteed or tied to a timetable. It will be earned through performance, trust, and demonstrated ability to lead an increasingly complex business.

Most importantly, you'll be part of a team that takes pride in showing up every day for the farmers and ranchers who feed us.

**If you're a builder at heart, believe great people deserve great leadership, and want to create something you can be genuinely proud of, we'd love to meet you.**

**Location:** Fort Collins, Colorado — Full-Time, Onsite

**Compensation:** $130,000–$160,000 base salary, depending on experience and qualifications, plus performance-based bonus..

Pay: $130,000.00 - $160,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Paid time off
* Professional development assistance
* Relocation assistance

Application Question(s):

* Open & Honest - as a small company, we do not currently offer health benefits or a 401k. Our plan is to start to work on these things in 2027, but we prefer to meet you where we are today. Is that acceptable?
* How many years of practical experience do you have with concepts such as six sigma and lean manufacturing?

Work Location: In person

records.description:
* Team:Industrial Operations & Product Supply
* Location:Saratoga Springs
* Req ID:R53229
* Contract:Full time
* Work Pattern:Onsite

**The role**
------------

**Build our future together:**

At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We’re hiring a Sr. Director/ Executive Director of Manufacturing Operations for our new highly automated bulk/ drug substance manufacturing plant, supporting 20–30 tech transfers a year alongside commercial delivery responsibility. GMP production will run concurrently with construction and CQV for 3–5 years. This role requires both building and operating.

 
 

This site operates on a foundation of strategy, execution, and rigor. Every function at the site owns a pyramid of metrics derived from annual goal planning that connects the site’s strategic goals to the factory floor, with performance measured back up to leadership to monitor, track, and mitigate against contingencies quantified using SMART goals in days and dollars.

 
 

The Sr. Director/ Executive Director of Manufacturing Operations owns cross-suite production performance across upstream and downstream operations in both single-use and stainless-steel suites. As the site scales to six suites, this leader is accountable for delivery of the site production plan, manufacturing cost performance, and workforce strategy, drives daily operational discipline through MDI and lean standard work, and represents manufacturing on the site Leadership Team.

 
 

**When & where:**

* Location: Saratoga Springs, New York, United States

* Work model: Monday-Friday, 8am-4:30pm
 

 

**Discover your role:**

* Own cross-suite production performance and site-wide annual batch plan attainment across all operating suites

* Lead fully integrated, operations-focused suite teams, with upstream, downstream, and support activities managed within each suite, and clear day-to-day accountability for execution, staffing, and scheduling

* Oversee these functions OpEx and CapEx budget and roadmap

* Serve as the primary responsible party for this function's alignment with the Global Center of Excellence (COE), connecting site execution back to the business-level function

* Ensure this function's metrics flow up and down through the MDI structure, connecting into the site's S&OP, AOP, and long-range planning cycles

records.description:
**Job Summary**

The Director of Manufacturing will provide strategic and operational leadership across manufacturing operations, ensuring production performance, scalability, operational excellence, cost efficiency, and quality. This role is responsible for developing manufacturing strategies, leading cross-functional teams, and aligning operations with business growth and organizational objectives.

**Responsibilities**

* Develop and execute manufacturing strategies aligned with organizational goals.
* Lead manufacturing operations, production, and operational support functions.
* Establish operational KPIs and drive accountability across manufacturing teams.
* Improve production capacity, throughput, efficiency, quality, and cost performance.
* Lead continuous improvement and operational excellence initiatives.
* Develop and implement workforce planning and organizational strategies.
* Collaborate with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, and leadership.
* Support new product introduction, process transfers, and manufacturing scale-up.
* Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, quality, and safety requirements.
* Develop management teams and succession planning.
* Identify opportunities for automation, technology implementation, and process innovation.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, or related field.
* 10+ years of manufacturing experience.
* 5+ years of senior manufacturing leadership experience.
* Proven experience managing complex manufacturing operations.
* Strong background in operational excellence, Lean, Six Sigma, or process improvement.
* Experience managing budgets, KPIs, production capacity, and large teams.
* Experience in medical devices, biotech, aerospace, electronics, or advanced manufacturing preferred.

Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

**A Day in the Life**
=====================

At Medtronic, you can begin a life-long career of exploration and innovation while helping champion healthcare access and equity for all. You'll lead with purpose, breaking down barriers to innovation in a more connected, compassionate world. We work with a sense of purpose and ownership, knowing there is a human life on the other side of every decision.
 
 
In this enterprise leadership role, the Director, Quality Center of Expertise (COE) – Design Quality will advance Design and Development excellence across Medtronic by shaping strategy, standards, governance, and enterprise capability for Design Quality and product development processes. Supporting every Medtronic Operating Unit and product category, this leader will drive consistency, strengthen Design Control execution, improve organizational capability, and help teams successfully navigate complex product development challenges.
 
 
The ideal candidate brings deep Design Quality and product development expertise, strong technical credibility, and a demonstrated track record of leading through complexity to deliver business, quality, and patient-focused outcomes. This individual will be a trusted enterprise partner who collaborates across Operating Units, Core Quality Services, and executive leadership teams to remove barriers, accelerate progress, and enable innovation while maintaining the highest standards of quality, compliance, and patient safety.
 
 
At Medtronic, we bring bold ideas forward with speed and decisiveness to put patients first in everything we do. In-person collaboration is critical to the success of this enterprise leadership role. This position requires an on-site presence a minimum of four days per week and must be based at one of the Medtronic U.S. campuses listed below. 

**Work Location**

This position will be onsite and based at one of the following Medtronic locations in the contiguous United States:

* Mounds View, MN / Minneapolis, MN (Twin Cities Campus)
* Irvine, CA / Santa Ana, CA (Orange County Campus)
* Lafayette, CO (Colorado Campus)
* Greater Boston Area (Boston, Danvers, or Mansfield, MA)
* North Haven, CT
* Memphis, TN
* Fort Worth, TX
* Jacksonville, FL
* Tempe, AZ

Travel up to 20% is required.

 

As **Director, Quality Center of Expertise (COE) – Design Quality** , you will provide enterprise leadership for Design Quality across Medtronic's global portfolio of medical technologies. You will partner with Operating Unit, Quality, Regulatory, Engineering, Product Development, and executive leaders to strengthen Design and Development practices, improve Design Control effectiveness, and enable successful execution across a diverse range of products and technologies.

You will serve as a highly credible Design Quality leader and trusted advisor, helping teams solve complex product development challenges while driving strategic initiatives that improve quality outcomes, product safety, regulatory readiness, and organizational performance.

Success in this role requires the ability to influence across a highly matrixed organization while maintaining a hands-on approach that removes barriers and accelerates execution. You will lead a small team of experts while driving enterprise-wide impact through collaboration, technical leadership, and capability building.

Responsibilities may include the following and other duties may be assigned:

 

***Lead enterprise Design Quality strategy, standards, and governance.***

* Develop and execute the enterprise Design Quality strategy, governance model, standards, and service priorities across Medtronic's global product portfolio.
* Establish and maintain enterprise Design Quality standards that enable consistent execution, regulatory readiness, and risk-based decision making.
* Own enterprise Design Quality process health, KPI visibility, and performance management mechanisms to identify trends, elevate risks, and drive timely action.
Create and lead governance mechanisms supporting critical product development programs, including escalation, issue resolution, and cross-functional decision making. 

***Drive enterprise initiatives and cross-functional partnerships that improve product development effectiveness, quality, and patient safety.***

* Partner with Operating Unit development teams to address complex design and development challenges through technical consultation, coaching, and expert guidance.
* Drive enterprise initiatives focused on improving product development effectiveness, product quality, patient safety, and risk management.
* Lead and influence strategic initiatives across the DRM Council, Productivity Workstream, Software Excellence Workstream, Global Operations & Supply Chain (GOSC), and Core Quality Services.
* Advance enterprise priorities, including Predicate Product Risk Reduction (PPRR) and other high-impact Design Quality improvement initiatives.
Partner with other Quality Centers of Excellence, including Risk Management, CAPA, and Acquisitions, to ensure alignment across critical quality processes. 

***Serve as the enterprise Design Quality expert, building capability and influencing critical decisions.***

* Serve as the enterprise subject matter expert for Design Quality, Design Controls, and Design & Development excellence.
* Build enterprise Design Quality capability through coaching, mentoring, talent development, and deployment of best practices.
* Influence decisions with potential enterprise-wide impact involving product safety, compliance, regulatory risk, legal exposure, business performance, and Medtronic's reputation.
Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, technical excellence, continuous improvement, and patient focus. 

 

**Must Have: Minimum Requirements**

 

**To be considered for this role, please ensure the minimum requirements are evident on your resume.**

* Bachelor's degree required and 10+ years of relevant experience in Product Development, Design Quality, Quality Engineering, Quality Systems, or related leadership roles **OR** Advanced degree with 8+ years of relevant experience in Product Development, Design Quality, Quality Engineering, Quality Systems, or related leadership roles.
* Minimum of 7 years of people leadership experience.
* Demonstrated experience leading Design Quality and Design Control activities within regulated medical device, software, combination product, or similarly regulated industries.
* Demonstrated experience leading Design & Development, Design Quality, or Product Development initiatives across multiple business units, product platforms, or enterprise functions within a complex, matrixed organization.
Experience supporting the development, design transfer, or lifecycle management of regulated medical technologies. 

 

**Nice to Have**

 

***Product development and Design Quality experience across the lifecycle.***

* Extensive experience serving on product development Core Teams through multiple phases of the product lifecycle.
* Demonstrated success leading complex product development or Design Quality challenges across diverse technologies and product categories.
Experience leading enterprise-wide quality, product development, or transformation initiatives across multiple business units. 

***Deep technical, regulatory, and digital expertise.***

* Deep expertise in Design Controls, Design Verification and Validation, Risk Management, and Design & Development processes.
* Strong knowledge of FDA regulations, QMSR, ISO 13485, EU MDR, GMP, and other global regulatory requirements.
* Experience supporting software-enabled medical technologies, digital health products, combination products, or other complex regulated technologies.
Experience leveraging analytics, AI-enabled tools, automation, and digital technologies to improve quality performance and organizational effectiveness. 

***Leadership through influence in a highly matrixed environment.***

* Proven ability to build alignment and influence decision-making among technical experts, business leaders, and executive stakeholders.
* Demonstrated success leading through influence in a highly matrixed environment while delivering large-scale organizational impact.
* Hands-on leadership style with a demonstrated ability to remove barriers, accelerate execution, and deliver measurable business outcomes.

For Baccalaureate degrees earned outside of the United States, a degree that satisfies the requirements of 8 C.F.R. § 214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A) is required.

The physical demands described within the Responsibilities section of this job description are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. For Office Roles: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to be independently mobile. The employee is also required to interact with a computer, and communicate with peers and co-workers. Contact your manager or local HR to understand the Work Conditions and Physical requirements that may be specific to each role.

At Medtronic, we are committed to fostering an environment where employees can thrive and make a meaningful impact. Apply only through official Medtronic channels. All legitimate Medtronic recruiting communications come from approved Medtronic platforms and official @medtronic.com email addresses.

 

Medtronic will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information (such as bank account or Social Security details) during early stages of the hiring process. Any such requests are not legitimate.

 

If you receive a suspicious message claiming to be from Medtronic, do not respond, click links, or open attachments.

 

If you have any questions, concerns regarding the authenticity of a communication alleged to have been made by or on behalf of Medtronic, please contact us immediately at AskHR@medtronic.com .
‌

===========================

**Medtronic offers a competitive Salary and flexible Benefits Package** 
A commitment to our employees lives at the core of our values. We recognize their contributions. They share in the success they help to create. We offer a wide range of benefits, resources, and competitive compensation plans designed to support you at every career and life stage.

Salary ranges for U.S (excl. PR) locations (USD):$184,000.00 - $276,000.00
‌ 
This position is eligible for a short-term incentive called the Medtronic Incentive Plan (MIP).The base salary range is applicable across the United States, excluding Puerto Rico and specific locations in California. The offered rate complies with federal and local regulations and may vary based on factors such as experience, certification/education, market conditions, and location. Compensation and benefits information pertains solely to candidates hired within the United States (local market compensation and benefits will apply for others).

The following benefits and additional compensation are available to those regular employees who work 20+ hours per week: Health, Dental and vision insurance , Health Savings Account , Healthcare Flexible Spending Account , Life insurance, Long-term disability leave , Dependent daycare spending account , Tuition assistance/reimbursement , and Simple Steps (global well-being program).

The following benefits and additional compensation are available to all regular employees: Incentive plans, 401(k) plan plus employer contribution and match , Short-term disability , Paid time off , Paid holidays , Employee Stock Purchase Plan , Employee Assistance Program , Non-qualified Retirement Plan Supplement (subject to IRS earning minimums) , and Capital Accumulation Plan (available to Vice Presidents and above, or subject to IRS earning minimums).

records.description:
**About Bora:**

Bora Biologics is a global biologics CDMO delivering integrated development and GMP manufacturing solutions from First‑in‑Human through licensed commercial supply. While many CDMOs are structured primarily for early clinical programs, Bora Biologics is purpose‑built for commercialization. Our inspection‑proven, bi‑coastal U.S. manufacturing platform and integrated development center provide the infrastructure, regulatory discipline, and operational precision required for sustained global market supply.

**Summary**

Reporting to the VP, Regional Head of Quality, the BBUL Site Head of Quality is responsible for developing, implementing, and overseeing a comprehensive Quality Management strategy aligned with corporate policies, client expectations, and global regulatory requirements. This role ensures products from development through commercialization are safe, effective, and fully compliant with applicable CGMP/GxP standards. As a key member of the site leadership team, the Director/Sr. Director of Quality provides strategic and operational leadership for the Quality organization, which includes Quality Assurance and Quality Control. The role partners cross-functionally with all departments to foster a strong culture of quality, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement while ensuring regulatory compliance and client satisfaction. The Director/Sr. Director also directs day-to-day quality operations, drives operational excellence and process optimization, supports execution of strategic and tactical initiatives, and ensures timely resolution of quality and compliance issues to maintain business performance and inspection readiness.

 

**Essential Functions**

*Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.*

* P rovide strategic leadership and overall accountability for the site Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring compliance with global policies, procedures, CGMP/GxP standards, and applicable regulatory requirements across the U.S. and international markets including EU.
* Partner with the Site Leadership Team (SLT) to strengthen and sustain a proactive culture of quality, escalating significant compliance risks and driving timely, effective resolution of quality issues.
* Lead and oversee regulatory inspections and audits, ensuring inspection readiness, effective agency interactions, and timely, compliant responses to observations.
* Direct all core Quality functions, including batch record review, material and product disposition, deviations and change control, document control, QC, QA oversight of all GMP functions including validation, operations, and facility activities.
* Provide leadership to ensure uninterrupted support for successful product transfers through robust quality oversight and operational excellence.
* Serve as the senior Quality leader supporting development initiatives and phased clinical programs, ensuring appropriate compliance throughout product development activities.
* Lead the Quality organization in achieving operational and strategic objectives, including budget planning and management, workforce planning, project execution, and organizational effectiveness.
* Establish and monitor key quality metrics (e.g., deviations, CAPAs, change controls, product release) to foster accountability. Evaluate system effectiveness and drive corrective action.
* Oversee quality indicators and operational efficiencies, implementing action plans to mitigate risks and streamline quality processes.
* Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing Quality organization that operates as a trusted, collaborative business partner, while driving talent development, succession planning, and employee growth.
* Establish clear, consistent, and effective communication across the Quality organization and with cross-functional stakeholders to ensure alignment on priorities, risks, and business objectives.
Perform additional responsibilities and strategic initiatives as assigned 

*The above statements are intended to describe the nature of work performed by those in this job and are not an exhaustive list of all duties. Nothing in this job description restricts managements right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time which reflects management’s assignment of essential functions.*

**Minimum Education, Experience and Skills**

Bachelor’s degree in life sciences or a related area of study

**Experience:**

* At minumum15 years of pharmaceutical industry experience with at least 10 years of Quality experience, both QC and QA in biopharma/biotech in a CGMP pharmaceutical manufacturing environment with early and late-stage products.
* 5+ years of senior leadership experience driving Quality strategy, compliance initiatives, continuous improvement and staff development.
* Extensive experience developing, implementing and improving quality systems directly related to biologics drug substance manufacturing CGMP
* Proven track record of successfully managing and leading regulatory inspections, audits, and remediation activities with global health authorities with demonstrated success in leading a company through cGMP pre-approval and post-approval inspections.
* Proven ability to build and sustain a transparent, collaborative, and quality-focused culture that promotes accountability, engagement, and operational performance.
* Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional teams and influencing organizational change within complex regulated environments.
* Demonstrated ability to develop staff at all levels.
Experience with developing and managing budgets. 

**Skills and Abilities**

* Strong working knowledge of global regulatory requirements and quality standards, including US FDA, EMA, PIC/S, and ICH guidelines.
* Demonstrated success in leading organizations through sound decision-making, strategic problem-solving, and effective communication at all levels of the business.
* Prior experience within a CDMO environment is strongly preferred
* Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders and communicate complex quality and compliance matters clearly and effectively.
* Proven ability to lead, mentor, and support teams through crisis management, organizational transformation, cultural change, and business growth initiatives.
* Highly adaptable and resilient, with the ability to perform effectively in fast-paced, high-pressure environments while maintaining focus on priorities and outcomes.
* Strong leadership capability with a demonstrated ability to empower teams, identify high-potential talent, and drive employee development and succession planning.
* Results-oriented leader with strong analytical and problem-solving skills focused on continuous improvement and operational excellence.
* Skilled at building trusted relationships and collaborating effectively with cross-functional peers, senior leadership, clients, and regulatory agencies.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced degree in biological or chemical sciences
* Experience with US FDA, China FDA, Health Canada, EMEA, PMDA, and ANVISA is preferred
* Knowledge of and experience with GLP and/or GCP regulatory inspections a plus
Strong operational excellence experience or qualification 

Base Salary Range 192000-270000

 
 

**Compensation and Benefits**

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support our employees’ wellbeing, including:

* Competitive salary and performance-based incentives
* Comprehensive health coverage including medical, dental, and vision insurance
* Retirement savings plans with employer matching contributions
* Paid time off
* Professional development opportunities
* Employee wellness programs and resources
* Employee Assistance Program and Mental Health Resources

**Core Values**

*At Bora, our values guide everything we do — from how we solve challenges to how we support our people. We lead with a solutions-first mindset, strive to do the right thing, stay proactive, and above all, respect everyone.*

Bora Pharmaceuticals is committed to providing equal employment opportunity to all applicants and employees according to all applicable equal opportunity and affirmative action laws, directives and regulations of federal, state and local governing bodies and agencies. In keeping with this commitment, Bora Pharmaceuticals will recruit, hire, train and promote persons in all job titles, without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex (including factors related to pregnancy or child birth), national origin, age, marital status, familial status, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity status with regard to public assistance, employment status, local human rights commission activity, status as a protected veteran, genetic information, atypical hereditary cellular or blood trait, or any other protected category.

records.description:
About PopUp Bagels

PopUp Bagels is not just a bagel company—we’re a cultural movement. Our stores are small, our vibes are loud, and our energy is contagious. From signature neon and iconic bullhorns to our “Not Famous but Known” mirror, we’ve reimagined not just how a bagel is created, but how it’s enjoyed: Grip, Rip and Dip! With a cult-like following, massive social presence, and unparalleled collaborations with top companies, partners and Brand Ambassadors PopUp Bagels is defining a new food lifestyle brand.

We keep things simple, but we do them really, really well. And our customers agree.

The Role

We're looking for a Regional Director to lead operations at our Nevada cream cheese production facility. This facility will play an important role in supporting PopUp's continued growth and our ability to deliver the products our customers love.

This is a senior operational leadership role responsible for overseeing the day-to-day performance of the facility, from the moment raw materials come through the door to the second finished goods ship out to shops around the country.

Here's what makes this role different from other operations roles: we're building something big, and we're building quickly. With established production facilities and operating procedures already in place, the right person for this role will know how to take proven processes, put them into practice, and continue improving them as we grow.

We're looking for a problem-solver who isn't afraid to roll up their sleeves and find solutions, a leader who earns trust on the floor just as easily as they collaborate with senior leadership, and someone who can translate operational expectations into consistent, measurable results.

This role serves as a key connection between the Nevada production facility and our broader operations leadership team. You'll have the opportunity to influence how we operate, develop our people, and contribute to the continued evolution of our production processes as PopUp expands.

If you're a driven leader who thrives in fast-moving environments, values collaboration, and takes pride in building strong teams and efficient operations, this could be the role for you.

What You'll Do:

Run the Facility. You'll provide day-to-day operational leadership and oversight across Cream Cheese and Schmear production, Warehouse, Quality Assurance, Sanitation, and Equipment Maintenance Working closely with the President of Operations and other facility leaders, you'll implement and maintain established SOPs, manage production schedules, drive throughput targets, and identify opportunities to continuously improve how we operate. You'll be responsible for addressing operational challenges, escalating significant issues when appropriate, and ensuring the facility consistently meets established performance, quality, and safety expectations.

Lead People Who Make an Impact. Building a strong team culture is at the core of this role. You'll recruit, develop, and retain a workforce that makes a genuine impact at PopUp Bagels. You'll coach and support your management team, reinforce established training programs, and identify opportunities to strengthen employee development as the operation grows. You'll create an environment where accountability and recognition go hand in hand. Our hourly workforce is the backbone of this operation, and how you show up for them defines everything.

Manage the Numbers. You'll be accountable for facility-level operational performance, including production costs, labor efficiency, waste reduction, and budget adherence. You'll partner closely with the President of Operations, Finance, and Accounting on budgeting, forecasting, and period-end reporting, and regularly communicate facility performance, challenges, and opportunities to senior leadership. You'll identify ways to improve efficiency and control costs without compromising quality, safety, or people, while supporting broader capital planning and investment decisions.

Drive Supply Chain Alignment. Work directly with our VP of Supply Chain to align production schedules with material availability. You'll oversee raw material procurement planning, inventory controls, and warehouse operations, ensuring established FIFO and food safety standards are consistently followed. You'll collaborate with Supply Chain and other production facilities to support inventory accuracy, product availability, and efficient distribution.

Lead Food Safety & Regulatory Compliance. Champion a food-safety-first culture across every part of the facility. You'll ensure consistent execution of established food safety programs and compliance with applicable FDA regulations, FSMA requirements, HACCP plans, and third-party audit standards (SQF, BRC), as applicable. You'll partner with Quality Assurance and the President of Operations to maintain rigorous in-process and finished product quality standards, address compliance concerns, and implement corrective actions when something doesn't meet the bar.

Collaborate Across the Company. You'll represent Nevada facility operations in company-wide leadership meetings and collaborate with Distribution & Logistics, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and corporate leadership. You'll translate what's happening on the floor into meaningful operational insights, communicate opportunities for improvement, and ensure company priorities and decisions are effectively implemented at the facility level.

Who You Are and What You Bring

We're looking for a leader who is genuinely:

A scrappy problem-solver. When something breaks at 7am or a key ingredient is backordered, you find a way. You're resourceful, calm under pressure, and put in the time to figure it out. You know when to make decisions, when to collaborate, and when to escalate an issue.

A trust-builder. Your team respects you because you've worked to build trust, not because of your title. You're on the floor, you know people's names, and you follow through on what you say.

A galvanizing leader. You provide clear direction, get buy-in, and bring your team along with energy and conviction. People want to work hard for you because they know you'll do the same for them.

Equally at home in a leadership meeting and a production room. You can review financial and operational performance in the morning and troubleshoot a production issue in the afternoon. You don't ask your team to do what you're not willing to do yourself.

Built for growth and continuous improvement. PopUp is growing fast, and our processes will continue to evolve. You appreciate the value of established systems and standards, but you're also comfortable identifying opportunities to make them better. You know how to balance consistency with adaptability as the business scales.

You bring:

* Bachelor's degree in Food Science, Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience. Master's degree (MBA or MS) preferred.
* 8–10+ years of progressive plant or manufacturing operations leadership experience, including demonstrated responsibility for facility performance, team leadership, and operational budgets.
* Experience leading operations in fast-paced manufacturing environments, preferably within growing or multi-site organizations.
* Proven track record of leading high-performing, cross-functional manufacturing teams.
* Prior food and beverage industry experience strongly preferred; dairy, cream cheese, spreads, or related refrigerated food production experience is a significant plus.
* Familiarity with food safety regulatory frameworks, including FSMA, HACCP, GMP, and third-party audit standards (SQF, BRC, AIB).
* Strong financial acumen, including budget management, cost analysis, labor efficiency, and operational performance reporting.
* Working knowledge of production cost drivers, manufacturing KPIs, and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Production Excellence, or equivalent).
* Demonstrated experience implementing and maintaining standardized operating procedures, production processes, and operational controls.
* Experience partnering with corporate Finance, Supply Chain, Quality Assurance, and Distribution teams.
* Availability and willingness to be on-call on weekends and off-hours to respond to facility disruptions or emergencies.
* Experience supporting capital improvement projects and operational efficiency initiatives.
* A history of building positive, rewarding workplace cultures for hourly workforces.

Physical Requirements

The following physical requirements are representative of those needed to perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made for individuals with qualifying disabilities.

* Ability to walk, stand, and move throughout a production facility for extended periods during daily floor presence and inspections.
* Must be able to work in a manufacturing environment with varying temperatures, including refrigerated dairy production and storage areas, moderate to loud noise levels, and exposure to dairy ingredients and food-grade cleaning agents.
* Occasional lifting of up to 50 pounds may be required.
* Must be able to wear required PPE, including hair nets, beard nets, gloves, and safety footwear when on the production floor.
* Ability to use standard office equipment (computer, monitor, phone, conferencing technology) for extended periods.
* Occasional travel to corporate offices, other production facilities, or external meetings (estimated up to 30%).

PopUp Bagels is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

We do not discriminate based on race, age, ancestry, creed, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, pregnancy, childbirth or related condition, unemployment status, gender identity or expression, transgender status, marital status, domestic violence or sexual violence victim status, national origin, citizenship, disability, covered veteran and/or military status, genetic information, familial status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, and local law. PopUp Bagels conducts pre-employment screenings in compliance with local, state, and federal laws, and utilizes E-Verify to confirm U.S. employment eligibility.

The duties of this position may change from time to time. PopUp Bagels reserves the right to add or delete duties and responsibilities at its discretion. This posting describes the general nature and level of work expected and is not intended to be all-inclusive.

records.title: Sr. Director, Operations
records.description:
**About Schumacher**

Schumacher & Co. is an innovative interior design company that is disrupting the $150 billion-dollar global interior design industry. We are a technological leader on the design frontier, constantly pushing boundaries and striving for excellence. With over 500+ employees and growing, we are driven by a shared belief that design transforms life. We are dedicated to the mission of helping our customers *"celebrate the feeling of home".* F. Schumacher & Co designs and produces some of the most beautiful fabrics, wallcoverings, trims, rugs, furniture, and accessories in the world. Our portfolio of products is broad, but they are united by a passion for design, a thirst for what is next, an appreciation for what's come before, a drive to make our products with enormous care and attention for detail. F. Schumacher & Co is a globally recognized company with a myriad of showrooms both domestically and internationally.

Our competitive advantage in the industry is our people. We believe that our employees are our most important assets. F. Schumacher & Co is deeply anchored in our company's core values which are as follows:

* Preserve our Start-up spirit

* Take Ownership & Accountability

* Be Solutions-Oriented

* Demonstrate Courage

* Practice Adaptability

* Embrace Collaboration

We empower our employees to live these values daily because we understand how it will positively impact the customer's journey. F. Schumacher & Co., also known as FSCO, is the parent company to many brands within our portfolio. This role leads our **Paramount Handprints manufacturing operations** — our internal product mills based in Passaic, NJ and the Brooklyn Navy Yard — which are a critical differentiator for the business, providing craft and flexibility across our portfolio.

**Role Overview**

We are seeking an experienced, hands-on **Sr. Director of Operations** to lead manufacturing operations across our two internal product mills: **one in Passaic, NJ** which produces hand screen-printed fabric and wallcoverings in Passaic, NJ, and another in the Brooklyn Navy Yard which prints digital wallcoverings, both for FS&CO and third-party customers. This individual will oversee the full manufacturing process — from receiving and inventory through order entry, craft printing, quality assurance, shipping and client communications.

This is a builder role. The ideal candidate is scrappy and entrepreneurial, comfortable operating in a hands-on, evolving environment, while also bringing rigor, standards, and consistency to a growing operation. They will balance our commitment to craftsmanship with the need for cost efficiency and anticipate that capabilities and capacity will continue to evolve over time.

This role is based full-time, on-site in Passaic, NJ, five days a week, with occasional travel to our Brooklyn Navy Yard and SoHo locations as needed. It reports to the **Head of Portfolio Development**.

 

**What You'll Do**

* **Leadership**: Lead a team of approximately 60 across both mills.

* Directly manage the Director of Production Planning, Director of Production, Shipping & Warehouse Leads, and Senior Digital Printers at each site and indirectly oversee their teams.

* Oversee the CX leader responsible for order entry and client communication.

* Build a strong, accountable culture across both sites; recruit, develop, and retain talent at all levels.

* **Manufacturing Operations**: Oversee the end-to-end manufacturing process and P&L ownership across both sites, including:

* Warehouse receiving and inventory management

* Screen engraving, color mixing, and trialing

* Production

* Quality assurance and printing

* Cutting, packing, and shipping

* **Process improvement & margin management**: Bring consistency and standardization reliability to our operations.

* Balance craftsmanship with efficiency to protect and improve margin across the mills' output

* Identify and implement process improvements that increase throughput, quality, and reliability without compromising craft.

* Develop and manage spending against budget, in conjunction with Head of Portfolio Development

* Identify cost savings opportunities across from raw materials, vendor contracts and labor

* Develop and track KPIs across capacity, production, quality, fulfillment & financial efficiency

* **Facilities, Safety & Space Planning**

* Own facilities, maintenance, and safety programs across both mills.

* Lead space planning as capacity and capabilities evolve over time.

* Identify opportunities to augment capabilities with equipment & CAPEX investment opportunities

* **Collaboration & Communication**: Serve as an internal partner and external-facing representative of the mills, building trust with cross-functional teams as well as third-party customers and vendors.

* Build and maintain strong relationships with key customers and vendors, including third-party manufacturing and supply partners; quickly step into and manage existing external relationships as you transition into the role.

* Partner proactively with Portfolio Development, Design, Procurement, Sales and other cross-functional teams to align capacity and capabilities with business needs.

* Provide proactive, transparent communication and reporting to the Head of Portfolio Development and cross-functional stakeholders

 

**What We're Looking For**

* 8+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations leadership, ideally in a craft, custom, or make-to-order production environment.

* Ability to consistently balance productivity, quality, and craftsmanship at the highest level.

* Proven experience managing large teams (50+) across multiple functions and/or sites.

* Strong track record in process improvement and bringing standards/consistency to an evolving operation.

* Strong proactive communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.

* Excellent people management skills with a demonstrated ability to build culture and develop talent.

* Scrappy, entrepreneurial, and hands-on, balanced with the ability to bring structure and rigor; comfort operating in a business where capabilities and capacity frequently evolve

* Experience with facilities, safety, and space planning oversight.
