records.description:
Description:

**THE COMPANY**

For over 40 years, Aero Simulation, Inc. (ASI) has provided quality flight training devices to the US Military. ASI has successfully built numerous training systems with a primary focus on aircrew and maintenance training systems. Our current programs include, but are not limited to, the B-1 Training Systems (Air Force), E-2D Training Systems (Navy), CH-53E Training Devices (USMC), IMOMS (Coast Guard), Navigation, Seamanship, Shiphandling Trainer – NSST (Navy). To learn more about ASI visit Programs- Aero Simulation, Inc.

ASI is a 100% employee-owned engineering and manufacturing company committed to supporting the nation’s warfighters. Being 100% employee-owned directly impacts our culture: it drives our decision-making, motivates our teams, increases our productivity, improves retention and contributes to the future success of our company. Our culture is one where we work hard for our clients and for each other – and we have fun collaborating, sharing experience and expertise, and learning along the way. We strive to deliver exceptional quality, elevate client relationships, and enrich the careers and lives of our employee-owners. As Employee-Owners, we are invested in the success and continued development of each other and the company.

In addition to the Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), we offer a flexible work environment, generous paid time off, professional development opportunities, industry competitive compensation, and superior benefits to include medical, dental, 401k and more!

ASI is a great place to build a career and grow with a company that is dedicated to quality, service and to fostering a community of support for each and every member of the team. To learn more about this opportunity, keep reading!

**POSITION SUMMARY**

ASI is seeking an experienced, results-driven Director of Production to provide strategic leadership and operational oversight of its production organization. This is a key senior leadership position responsible for ensuring the successful manufacturing, assembly, integration, and delivery of ASI's advanced simulation and military training device hardware.

Based in Tampa, Florida, and reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer (COO), the Director of Production will oversee Production Control, Material Control, and Manufacturing through functional managers and department leads. The position will also provide executive oversight of Facility Management and Workplace Safety through the Facilities Manager.

The successful candidate will bring demonstrated experience leading complex manufacturing operations, developing high-performing teams, managing production capacity and resources, and delivering technical products in demanding, schedule-driven environments.

This individual will play an important role in supporting ASI's Department of Defense, U.S. military, government agency, and defense industry programs while ensuring the organization is positioned to support new business opportunities and long-term growth.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

*Strategic Leadership & Operational Management*

* Provide strategic direction and operational leadership for Production Control, Material Control, and Manufacturing.
* Establish production priorities, performance expectations, resource requirements, and organizational objectives.
* Lead through functional managers, promoting accountability, operational discipline, and effective execution.
* Ensure production operations consistently meet contractual commitments, customer requirements, program milestones, and delivery schedules.
* Partner with executive leadership to develop operational strategies supporting current programs and future business growth.
* Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure organizational effectiveness and drive improvement.

*Production Planning & Program Execution*

* Oversee production planning, scheduling, capacity management, and resource allocation across multiple concurrent programs.
* Partner with Program Management and Engineering to translate contractual requirements and technical specifications into executable production plans.
* Ensure production readiness, including personnel, materials, equipment, facilities, documentation, and approved manufacturing processes.
* Identify and mitigate production risks that could impact cost, schedule, quality, or customer delivery.
* Support program reviews, production readiness assessments, customer meetings, and government inspections.
* Provide production estimates, labor forecasts, capacity assessments, and schedule inputs for new business proposals.

*Manufacturing & Systems Integration*

* Oversee the manufacturing and assembly of complex simulation and training device hardware.
* Ensure effective collaboration between Production and Engineering to promote manufacturability, reliability, and cost-effective designs.
* Support the integration of major simulation hardware components, including visual display systems, motion platforms, and associated subsystems.
* Ensure manufacturing activities follow approved engineering drawings, Bills of Materials (BOMs), configuration requirements, and engineering change processes.
* Drive improvements in production flow, manufacturing efficiency, product quality, and delivery performance.

*Workforce Leadership & Development*

* Lead, mentor, and develop production managers, supervisors, manufacturing engineers, technicians, assemblers, and integration personnel.
* Establish clear performance expectations and accountability standards for functional managers.
* Develop staffing and workforce plans to support current and anticipated production requirements.
* Identify workforce development needs and implement appropriate training and cross-training initiatives.
* Build organizational depth through succession planning, leadership development, and employee engagement.
* Foster a culture centered on safety, quality, teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.

*Materials Management & Supply Chain Coordination*

* Ensure effective coordination between Production and Procurement to maintain material availability and support production schedules.
* Monitor material shortages, supplier performance, inventory levels, and long-lead procurement requirements.
* Establish appropriate material priorities based on program schedules and contractual commitments.
* Ensure effective inventory management, material traceability, and control of customer-furnished and government-furnished property.
* Promote accurate material tracking and accountability through ASI's ERP system.

*Quality & Regulatory Compliance*

* Ensure production operations comply with ASI's ISO 9001:2015 Quality Management System and applicable contractual, customer, government, and regulatory requirements.
* Partner with Quality Assurance to address nonconformances, corrective actions, root-cause analysis, and process improvements.
* Maintain effective production documentation, inspection records, test results, and configuration records.
* Support government quality audits, customer surveillance activities, and acceptance inspections.
* Promote a culture of quality and adherence to approved manufacturing processes throughout the production organization.

*Budget, Cost Control & Performance*

* Develop and manage production budgets, labor forecasts, and operational resource plans.
* Monitor production costs, labor utilization, productivity, rework, and overhead.
* Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing efficiency, reduce waste, and increase production throughput.
* Evaluate production capacity and capital equipment requirements.
* Provide regular operational and financial performance reporting to the COO and executive leadership.
* Support long-term resource planning and investment strategies aligned with anticipated business growth.

*Facility Management & Workplace Safety*

* Provide executive oversight of Facility Management and Workplace Safety through the Facilities Manager.
* Establish strategic priorities for facility readiness, infrastructure reliability, maintenance, and workplace safety.
* Ensure facilities, equipment, and infrastructure adequately support current production requirements and future growth.
* Review facility performance, safety metrics, significant incidents, and corrective actions.
* Coordinate facility investment, capital requirements, and infrastructure planning with the Facilities Manager and COO.
* Promote a safe, organized, and efficient working environment.

*Continuous Improvement*

* Implement Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, 5S, and other operational excellence methodologies, as appropriate.
* Establish consistent production management practices, standard operating procedures, and performance measures.
* Identify opportunities to reduce cycle times, eliminate waste, improve first-pass yield, and increase productivity.
* Drive corrective and preventive actions to resolve recurring operational issues.
* Promote employee engagement, proactive problem-solving, and continuous

**LEADERSHIP EXPECTATIONS**

* Provides leadership and direct supervision of Group Leaders responsible for Manufacturing, Facility Management, Production Control, Workplace Safety, and Stockroom operations, establishing priorities, expectations, and accountability for operational performance, quality, efficiency, safety, and on-time delivery.
* The Director maintains oversight of these functional areas while ensuring alignment with program requirements and organizational objectives. Ensures teams have the resources, processes, equipment, capabilities, and organizational support necessary to maintain safe and efficient operations, support successful program execution, and meet production schedules and contractual commitments.

Requirements:

**EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS**

* 10–15 years of progressive experience in manufacturing, production, or operations management.
* At least 5 years of leadership experience managing production teams, functional managers, and complex manufacturing operations.
* Proven experience overseeing the manufacturing, assembly, integration, and delivery of complex technical products.
* Demonstrated ability to manage production schedules, labor resources, materials, budgets, capacity, and contractual delivery commitments.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production planning, quality management systems, and operational performance metrics.
* Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and drive accountability across multiple functional organizations.
* Excellent leadership, communication, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
* Working knowledge of facility operations, infrastructure, and workplace safety requirements.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, flight simulation, military training systems, or related industries.
* Experience supporting U.S. Department of Defense programs, military customers, or defense prime contractors.
* Experience with complex electromechanical systems and hardware/software integration.
* Familiarity with ISO 9001, Lean Manufacturing, and Six Sigma principles.
* Experience with ERP/MRP systems, production planning tools, and manufacturing performance reporting.
* Familiarity with government contracting, DoD Manufacturing Planning (MIL-HDBK-896), configuration management, and Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT).
* Experience managing multiple concurrent production programs.
* Experience providing executive oversight of facility management, infrastructure planning, capital equipment, and workplace safety functions.

*Technical and Leadership Competencies*

* Defense manufacturing and production operations.
* Mechanical and electrical assembly and integration.
* Simulation hardware manufacturing and testing.
* Production planning, scheduling, and capacity management.
* Configuration management and engineering change control.
* Quality management systems and regulatory compliance.
* Government contracting and DoD acquisition environments.
* ERP/MRP systems and material requirements planning.
* Cost accounting, labor forecasting, and operational performance metrics.
* Strategic thinking and organizational leadership.
* Cross-functional collaboration and resource allocation.
* Leadership development, team building, and change management.
* Accountability for cost, schedule, quality, and delivery performance.

*Security & Compliance Requirements*

* Must be eligible to work in the United States.
* Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government Secret-level security clearance.
* Must successfully complete applicable government security eligibility and investigation requirements.
* Must be able to work in accordance with applicable DoD security, export control, and controlled information requirements.
* Familiarity with International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Export Administration Regulations (EAR), and Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) requirements, as applicable.

**WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE**

The Director of Production will be successful by:

* Delivering production commitments on time and within established cost and quality objectives.
* Building a strong, accountable, and effective production leadership team.
* Maintaining production readiness and sufficient capacity to support current and future programs.
* Improving manufacturing efficiency, productivity, and operational performance.
* Ensuring effective coordination among Production, Engineering, Program Management, Quality, Procurement, and Facilities.
* Maintaining safe, reliable, and growth-ready production facilities.
* Positioning ASI's production organization to successfully execute new program awards and support long-term business growth.

**EDUCATION**

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, or a related technic 
al discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* The physical requirements and working conditions listed below are representative of those required on the job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential duties and responsibilities.

records.title: Director, Program Operations
records.description:
In this role, the Director of Program Operations leads a team of Operations Program Managers (OPM) and Material Program Managers (MPM) responsible for the operational elements of program execution within Mercury's PCC Manufacturing Center of Excellence. This role serves as a conduit between the line of business and operational teams, ensuring seamless coordination across engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, and growth functions.

You will be responsible for developing and executing operational program plans for critical programs, overall ownership of operational program performance, and internal communication of customer requirements affecting operational execution.

The Director of Program Operations will support proposals by providing accurate basis of cost estimates, focusing on supply chain material costs in addition to manufacturing labor costs. This work will be performed in conjunction with factory operations, supply chain, and engineering functions. Candidates must have excellent written and oral communications skills to influence across multiple functions and communicate effectively with external partners.

This role is on site at one of the following Mercury facilities: **Phoenix AZ**

**Job Responsibilities:**

* Lead, coach, and develop a team of OPMs and MPMs accountable for operational aspects of program life cycle from proposal, development, production, sustainment, & delivery.
* Serve as the primary liaison between the line of business and operations, communicating customer requirements that affect manufacturing and supply chain execution.
* Responsible for meeting the financial objectives of the business unit, including the management of Estimate at Completion (EACs) specific to operations labor and material content.
* Oversee supply chain and manufacturing milestones to ensure compliance with contract baseline.
* Monitor program risks and opportunities, including obsolescence management, reporting, and improvement actions.
* Support and present operations metrics and data through program reviews (both internal and external) to Mercury and customer leadership.
* Champion efforts to meet readiness requirements throughout an NPI stage-gate process.
* Change leader, helping to drive Mercury's strategy, structure, and values.
* Strategic thinking coupled with ROI / business case development.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree.
* Typically requires 10+ years prior relevant experience in functional areas of Supply Chain, Operations (including Production Control), Program Management, or technical Project Management.
* Strong financial acumen with experience providing input into and reviewing EACs, along with development of business cases.
* Experience in review and understanding of Statements of Work (SOW) and project requirements (technical and commercial).
* Strong analytical skills, problem‑solving capabilities, and attention to detail.
* Experience developing and mentoring high‑performing teams.
* The ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government issued security clearance is required. U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* A self-starter, capable of achieving organizational and program objectives, and able to interface with all levels of internal management and external stakeholders.
* Ability to succeed in fast paced, developmental environment.
* Excellent time management skills and the ability to assign the appropriate priorities to the many tasks that need to be performed.
* Knowledge of US Government acquisition laws and regulations (FAR).
* Proficiency in ERP/MRP business systems.
* Knowledge of Mercury-type products with surface mount technology.
* Excellent communication skills (written, verbal, and presentation), leadership abilities, and the ability to work in an IPT environment.

records.title: Sr. Manager, Reaction Injection Molding, Operations
records.description:
**What to Expect**

The Senior Manager, CyberCab Reaction Injection Mold – Operations sets the vision and strategic path for the Production Maintenance & Engineering organizations. This role leads the production, maintenance, tool & die and Engineering teams and works collaboratively with cross-functional partners to achieve Safety, People, Quality, Production/Delivery, and Cost KPI targets of the organization, as well as establishing a high-performance culture.
 
 
This role is responsible for production and resource planning for all exterior panels of CyberCab, provides coaching, mentoring, and developing leaders; launching new programs successfully; and daily tactical planning and execution to achieve the build plan and meet safety, quality, rate, and cost targets. The person in this role must be capable of guiding the team through complex issues, distilling large volumes of data to solve problems, and driving day-over-day continuous improvement.
 
 
This Senior Manager provides hands-on support, leadership, and direction to both teams on all operational, team morale, and equipment-related matters. The person in this role is responsible for building teams that work cohesively and perform at the highest level, keeping Tesla’s mission and the goals of the organization in mind. Your technical judgement and Operating discipline will drive decisions with Engineering, NPI, Programs, Quality, Materials and Upstream/Downstream shops.

 
**What You'll Do**

* Set the vision and strategic path for the Production, Maintenance & Engineering organizations within Cybercab, and lead the team to achieve Safety, People, Quality, Production, and Cost KPI targets and objectives of the organization
* Drive tactical planning to achieve the production build plan with the highest safety, quality, and yield performance
* Launch new programs and lead production ramps and product design changes successfully through resource planning, program management, and partnership with the NPI, Manufacturing Engineering, and Design Engineering teams
* Work with the team to identify production bottlenecks and achieve ramp plans by addressing availability, efficiency, and yield constraints on the line. Coach and mentor the team on data collection and analysis, complex problem solving, and driving daily improvements
* Guide the team through root cause analysis, methodical problem solving, and first-principles thinking. Maintain a culture of adherence to standardized work and compliance with documented processes and procedures so that safe practices and building products to quality specification are sustained
* Lead the maintenance team on equipment availability, preventive and predictive maintenance programs, project planning, and equipment improvements based on downtime data analysis. Establish and maintain equipment spare parts to achieve availability targets and build rates
* Be entrepreneurial and make quick decisions in ambiguous situations. Build a high-performing team, set clear expectations and goals, and manage performance effectively with clear, concise feedback loops
* Maintain a strong technical understanding of product design, intent, processes, and equipment theory of operation. Identify bottlenecks, balance the line, and work closely with the engineering team to solve problems, increase availability, and drive process improvements
* Create a comprehensive strategy for Tool & Die as well as Engineering teams for strong collaboration, same goal visions and strong partnership from dies to machine parametrization
* Work with HR and other teams to improve team morale and create an environment in which team members want to come to work and perform at the highest level

 
**What You'll Bring**

* 10–12 years of leadership and manufacturing experience, preferably in the automotive industry or a highly technical manufacturing environment
* Analytical, detail-oriented, self-driven critical thinker who communicates proactively with all employees and works well in a fast-paced, multicultural environment
* Experience with process-improvement methodologies to improve efficiency, increase yield and availability, and apply design of experiments and statistical methods
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills with strong interpersonal skills. Ability to work well under pressure, manage competing demands, juggle priorities, and meet tight deadlines with diligent follow-through
* Hands-on experience implementing lean methodologies and world-class manufacturing practices
* Ability to use structured problem-solving methods and techniques to successfully resolve production problems, such as 8D, fishbone diagrams, and 5-Why analysis
* Ability to foster close working relationships with team members, management, and cross-functional groups. Highly collaborative, with a positive impact on the team overall
* High-level leadership and decision-making skills. A strong sense of urgency and drive to succeed
* Proficiency in MS Office, Visio, CAD, SPC charts, data-analysis tools, Jira, Tableau/BI dashboards, and project-management tools as well as basic level of prompting or deep curiosity for SI learning

#### **Benefits**

Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:

* Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
* Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
* Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans, both have options with a $0 paycheck contribution
* Company Paid (Health Savings Accounts) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High-Deductible medical plan with HSA
* Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
* 401(k) with employer match, Employee Stock Purchase Plans, and other financial benefits
* Company paid Basic Life, AD&D
* Short-term and long-term disability insurance (90 day waiting period)
* Employee Assistance Program
* Sick and Vacation time (Flex time for salary positions, Accrued hours for Hourly positions), and Paid Holidays
* Back-up childcare and parenting support resources
* Voluntary benefits to include: critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, theft & legal services, and pet insurance
* Weight Loss and Tobacco Cessation Programs
* Tesla Babies program
* Commuter benefits
* Employee discounts and perks program
* Earned Wage Access: Real-time pay access paid daily, subject to eligibility and schedule (applicable for below Sr. Managers levels)

 
 
Tesla is an Equal Opportunity / Affirmative Action employer committed to diversity in the workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, gender identity or any other factor protected by applicable federal, state or local laws. 
 
Tesla is also committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your recruiter know if you need an accommodation at any point during the interview process.

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
TerraImm, Inc. is seeking a dynamic, results-driven Director of Operations & Sales Growth to lead our sales organization, accelerate revenue growth, and strengthen overall business operations.
 
This is a key leadership opportunity for an experienced professional with a proven track record of building successful sales teams, developing effective sales strategies, and delivering measurable business results.

We are looking for a leader who knows how to motivate a team, establish accountability, identify opportunities for growth, and turn ambitious business objectives into actionable strategies.
 
The ideal candidate combines strong sales leadership, operational expertise, and a hands-on management approach.

 

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Sales Leadership & Revenue Growth**

* Lead, develop, and manage the sales organization with a primary focus on increasing revenue, improving conversion rates, and achieving aggressive growth objectives.
* Develop and execute comprehensive sales strategies designed to expand market reach, increase customer acquisition, and drive sustainable business growth.
* Establish clear sales goals, individual performance expectations, and measurable revenue targets.
* Coach, mentor, and motivate sales professionals to improve performance, strengthen sales techniques, and consistently achieve established goals.
* Evaluate sales performance, identify areas for improvement, and implement targeted training and development initiatives.
* Oversee sales pipeline management, lead distribution, prospect follow-up, appointment setting, and closing strategies.
* Implement effective sales processes and accountability measures to ensure consistent execution across the sales team.
* Identify opportunities to expand sales channels, improve lead generation, and strengthen customer acquisition strategies.
* Partner with marketing leadership to align campaigns, lead generation efforts, and sales objectives.

**Sales Performance, KPIs & Accountability**

* Develop, monitor, and report on key sales performance indicators, including:
 + Outbound calls and customer contacts
 + Qualified prospects and appointments scheduled
 + Estimates and proposals delivered
 + Lead-to-appointment conversion rates
 + Appointment-to-estimate conversion rates
 + Estimate-to-close conversion rates
 + Closed sales and revenue generated

**Operational Leadership & Business Efficiency**

* Develop and implement operational strategies, policies, and procedures that support business growth and scalability.
* Identify inefficiencies, streamline workflows, and implement solutions that improve productivity and service delivery.
* Establish and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs) to improve consistency, accountability, and operational effectiveness.
* Ensure the organization's operational infrastructure can support increased sales volume and business expansion.

**Team Development & Organizational Growth**

* Recruit, develop, and retain high-performing sales professionals and operational leaders.
* Build a performance-driven culture that encourages ownership, teamwork, accountability, and professional growth.
* Lead by example through active involvement, strong communication, and a commitment to measurable results.

**Financial Performance & Executive Collaboration**

* Work closely with executive leadership and Finance & Administration to establish revenue objectives, operational budgets, and financial performance goals.
* Identify business risks and implement solutions that support sustainable growth.
* Support compliance with company policies and applicable regulatory requirements, coordinating immigration-related matters with appropriate legal professionals.

 

**Qualifications & Requirements:**

* Proven track record of leading sales teams and achieving measurable revenue growth.
* Demonstrated success in developing and executing sales strategies, improving conversion rates, and increasing team productivity.
* Strong experience with sales pipeline management, CRM systems, forecasting, and performance reporting.
* Proven ability to coach, motivate, and develop sales professionals while maintaining high performance expectations.
* Experience establishing and monitoring sales KPIs, revenue targets, and individual performance metrics.
* Strong operational management skills, including process improvement, workflow optimization, and organizational development.
* Excellent leadership, communication, analytical, and decision-making skills.
* Ability to balance strategic planning with hands-on execution in a fast-paced, growth-oriented environment.
* Experience in immigration services, professional services, consulting, or related industries is preferred but not required.
* Bilingual proficiency in English and Spanish is preferred but not required.

 

The ideal candidate is a confident, proactive leader who knows how to set expectations, develop talent, measure performance, and deliver results. You understand that successful sales leadership requires more than setting goals. It requires coaching, accountability, consistent execution, and the ability to turn opportunities into revenue. You are equally comfortable analyzing performance reports, developing growth strategies, coaching a sales representative, or working alongside executive leadership to solve operational challenges.

records.title: Head of NA Operations, Professional Lines & Canada

postedPay.title: Head of NA Operations, Professional Lines & Canada

records.description:
This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance. We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture. As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

We are seeking an accomplished operations leader to lead the operational strategy, performance and transformation agenda supporting our North America Professional Lines & Canada businesses. 
This is a senior leadership role supporting specialty insurance businesses with more than $1 billion in annual revenue and significant ambitions for continued growth. The Head of Operations will partner closely with senior Underwriting leaders to build operational capabilities that enable profitable growth, increase underwriting capacity, strengthen service and controls, and improve how we work. 
The successful candidate will combine strong commercial and insurance knowledge with operational expertise and a passion for transformation. They will be equally comfortable shaping strategy with senior leaders and working with teams to understand challenges, simplify processes and turn opportunities into measurable results.

**What You'll Do** 
 

* Serve as a trusted strategic partner to senior Professional Lines & Canadian Underwriting leaders.
* Translate business strategy, portfolio priorities and growth ambitions into operational priorities and capabilities.
* Build strong relationships across Underwriting and Operations to identify opportunities to improve productivity, responsiveness and the underwriting experience.
* Balance enterprise standards with the specific requirements of individual underwriting businesses.

Lead Operational Performance 

* Lead a large underwriting support organization with accountability for service, quality, productivity, capacity and operational performance.
* Establish clear performance measures and service standards across the underwriting lifecycle.
* Use data and business insight to identify root causes, resolve performance issues and continuously improve results.
* Maintain a strong operational control environment with clear ownership and accountability.

Transform How We Work 

* Lead the development and implementation of scalable target operating models that simplify work, reduce unnecessary handoffs and create underwriting capacity.
* Evaluate processes end to end and identify opportunities to improve speed, accuracy, consistency and service.
* Build compelling cases for change based on data, business impact and measurable outcomes.
* Ensure transformation initiatives move beyond implementation to deliver sustainable improvements in business performance.

Harness Technology, Data & AI 

* Partner with Technology, Data and business leaders to modernize underwriting workflows and operating practices.
* Identify and implement practical opportunities to use workflow, automation and AI to increase underwriting capacity, improve service and strengthen operational controls.
* Ensure technology investments translate into measurable business value, colleague adoption and sustainable operating improvements.

Build a High-Performing Organization 

* Build and develop a high-performing Operations organization characterized by strong business partnership, accountability, curiosity and disciplined execution.
* Develop leaders, strengthen succession pipelines and build commercial, insurance and operational capability across the team.
* Foster an inclusive environment where colleagues are encouraged to challenge existing ways of working, solve problems and improve the business.
* Align workforce and capacity plans with business demand, service expectations and anticipated growth.
* Use productivity and performance insights to guide organization design, resource allocation and investment decisions.

**What You'll Bring**

* 10+ years of progressive experience within commercial P&C insurance, including significant experience in Underwriting Operations, Underwriting Support or a closely related function.
* Significant leadership experience, including responsibility for managers and large or geographically distributed teams.
* Strong understanding of the end-to-end underwriting lifecycle and the operational capabilities required to support a specialty insurance business.
* Demonstrated success partnering with senior Underwriting and business leaders and translating strategy into execution.
* Proven experience designing and implementing operating models and leading complex operational transformation.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with demonstrated experience using data to identify root causes and improve business performance.
* Experience applying technology, workflow, automation and data to improve underwriting or operational outcomes.
* Strong understanding of operational controls, service management and continuous improvement.
* A track record of leading change from concept through implementation and delivering measurable results.
* Strong commercial judgment and exceptional stakeholder-management and communication skills.
* A collaborative, hands-on leadership style, with the confidence to challenge constructively and create accountability for outcomes.
* Experience managing budgets, resources and workforce plans.
* Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree or relevant insurance qualification preferred.

What Success Looks Like 
The successful candidate will help create a more scalable, responsive and technology-enabled operating model that: 

* Increases underwriting capacity and allows underwriters to focus more of their time on underwriting, portfolio management, broker relationships and profitable growth.
* Delivers measurable improvements in service, productivity, quality and operational control.
* Supports continued business growth without proportionate increases in cost or operational complexity.
* Converts technology, automation and AI investments into meaningful business outcomes.
* Builds a strong leadership bench and a high-performing Operations organization with clear accountability for results.

This is an opportunity to play a significant leadership role in shaping how Operations enables the next phase of growth in our North America Professional Lines & Canada businesses.

**Role Factors**

The role requires you to be in office 3 days per week. Travel may be included.

 

**What We Offer**

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $180,000 - $235,000. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location.

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more. Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is Exempt for FLSA purposes.

**This posting is for an existing vacancy.**

records.description:
The Director of Operations leads all day-to-day operations at Innova's M3 facility in Mexicali, Mexico, including production, maintenance, purchasing, shipping and receiving, and site safety. Working closely with the site leadership team, this role ensures production goals, quality standards, cost targets, and customer delivery commitments are met. The Director builds and develops a strong local team, drives continuous improvement, and serves as the key link between the Mexicali plant and Innova's U.S. leadership, Finance, Quality, and Sales teams. The ideal candidate is based in the San Diego area, is fully bilingual in English and Spanish, and has proven experience leading manufacturing operations in Mexico.

 

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Champion and uphold the company's values, mission, and quality policy in all activities.

* Adhere to and help enforce company policies, procedures, and internal control standards.

* Ensure compliance with all applicable Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, including ISO 9001 and ISO 13485, as applicable to this role.

* Follow all safety rules and PPE requirements, and promptly report hazards, incidents, and near-misses.

* Lead all operations at the M3 facility, including production, maintenance, purchasing, and shipping and receiving, to meet production goals, quality standards, and customer delivery commitments.

* Direct and develop the site leadership team, including hiring, training, performance management, and succession planning.

* Oversee production planning and scheduling to balance capacity, labor, and materials with customer demand.

* Establish operational KPIs and monitor productivity, efficiency, scrap, cost, and on-time delivery, taking corrective action as needed.

* Oversee the site safety program and ensure compliance with applicable Mexican health, safety, and environmental regulations (e.g., STPS and NOM standards), fostering a strong culture of safety.

* Develop and manage the site operating budget, labor plan, and capital expenditure requests.

* Oversee equipment maintenance and facility upkeep to maximize uptime and maintain a safe, organized plant.

* Drive lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives to reduce waste, improve throughput, and lower costs.

* Coordinate with logistics and customs partners to support cross-border shipments, materials flow, and import/export requirements.

* Partner with Human Resources on workforce planning, employee relations, and compliance with Mexican labor law.

* Serve as the primary liaison between the Mexicali plant and Innova's U.S. leadership, Quality, Finance, and Sales, providing regular operational and financial reporting.

* Perform other related duties as required.

 

**EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE**

* Bachelor's degree in Operations Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field, required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.

* Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, including at least 5 years in a leadership role, required.

* Experience leading manufacturing operations in Mexico (maquiladora or similar cross-border environment) strongly preferred.

* Experience with plastics manufacturing processes (e.g., injection molding, thermoforming, CNC machining) preferred.

* Lean Manufacturing or Six Sigma certification preferred.

 

**SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS**

* Fully bilingual in English and Spanish (written and verbal) required.

* Proven leadership skills, with the ability to build, motivate, and develop a high-performing team.

* Extensive knowledge of manufacturing operations, production planning, and plant management.

* Strong working knowledge of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.

* Financial acumen, with the ability to develop budgets, manage costs, and interpret financial data.

* Working knowledge of Mexican labor, safety, and environmental regulations.

* Working knowledge of quality system requirements under ISO 9001 and ISO 13485, as applicable to this role.

* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and ERP/MRP systems.

* Valid passport and ability to cross the U.S.–Mexico border regularly.

 

**TRAINING & COMPETENCY REQUIREMENTS**

* Complete new-hire orientation and role-specific on-the-job training prior to performing unsupervised work.

* Complete Quality Management System (QMS) training applicable to this role, including quality policy awareness and the consequences of nonconformance to product or process requirements.

* Complete safety training applicable to this role (e.g., PPE use, lockout/tagout, forklift certification).

* Maintain competency through periodic refresher or retraining as required by department procedures and applicable regulatory requirements.

 

**WORK ENVIRONMENT**

* Office setting.

* Manufacturing floor environment.

* Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety glasses.

 

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.

* Mobility to navigate the production floor to conduct inspections and oversight.

 

**EXPECTED HOURS OF WORK**

* This is a full-time exempt position, required to work Monday through Friday. Occasional weekend availability may be required based on business needs.

 

**TRAVEL**

* Regular cross-border travel between San Diego, CA and the M3 facility in Mexicali, with on-site presence required a minimum of 4 days per week.

* Occasional travel to other Innova facilities, customers, and suppliers, up to 10%.

records.title: Head of NA Operations, U.S. Wholesale & Lower Middle Market

postedPay.title: Head of NA Operations, U.S. Wholesale & Lower Middle Market

records.description:
This is your opportunity to join AXIS Capital – a trusted global provider of specialty lines insurance and reinsurance. We stand apart for our outstanding client service, intelligent risk taking and superior risk adjusted returns for our shareholders. We also proudly maintain an entrepreneurial, disciplined and ethical corporate culture. As a member of AXIS, you join a team that is among the best in the industry.

At AXIS, we believe that we are only as strong as our people. We strive to create an inclusive and welcoming culture where employees of all backgrounds and from all walks of life feel comfortable and empowered to be themselves. This means that we bring our whole selves to work.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any protected characteristic, including age, color, disability, ethnicity, gender identity, marital status, national origin, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any basis prohibited by the laws that govern its operations.

We are seeking an accomplished operations leader to lead the operational strategy, performance and transformation agenda supporting our U.S. Wholesale and Lower Middle Market businesses.

This is a senior leadership role supporting specialty insurance businesses with more than $1 billion in annual revenue and significant ambitions for continued growth. The Head of Operations will partner closely with senior Underwriting leaders to build operational capabilities that enable profitable growth, increase underwriting capacity, strengthen service and controls, and improve how we work.

The successful candidate will combine strong commercial and insurance knowledge with operational expertise and a passion for transformation. They will be equally comfortable shaping strategy with senior leaders and working with teams to understand challenges, simplify processes and turn opportunities into measurable results.

**What You'll Do**

* Serve as a trusted strategic partner to senior Wholesale and Lower Middle Market Underwriting leaders.
* Translate business strategy, portfolio priorities and growth ambitions into operational priorities and capabilities.
* Build strong relationships across Underwriting and Operations to identify opportunities to improve productivity, responsiveness and the underwriting experience.
* Balance enterprise standards with the specific requirements of individual underwriting businesses.

Lead Operational Performance 

* Lead a large underwriting support organization with accountability for service, quality, productivity, capacity and operational performance.
* Establish clear performance measures and service standards across the underwriting lifecycle.
* Use data and business insight to identify root causes, resolve performance issues and continuously improve results.
* Maintain a strong operational control environment with clear ownership and accountability.

Transform How We Work 

* Lead the development and implementation of scalable target operating models that simplify work, reduce unnecessary handoffs and create underwriting capacity.
* Evaluate processes end to end and identify opportunities to improve speed, accuracy, consistency and service.
* Build compelling cases for change based on data, business impact and measurable outcomes.
* Ensure transformation initiatives move beyond implementation to deliver sustainable improvements in business performance.

Harness Technology, Data & AI 

* Partner with Technology, Data and business leaders to modernize underwriting workflows and operating practices.
* Identify and implement practical opportunities to use workflow, automation and AI to increase underwriting capacity, improve service and strengthen operational controls.
* Ensure technology investments translate into measurable business value, colleague adoption and sustainable operating improvements.

Build a High-Performing Organization 

* Build and develop a high-performing Operations organization characterized by strong business partnership, accountability, curiosity and disciplined execution.
* Develop leaders, strengthen succession pipelines and build commercial, insurance and operational capability across the team.
* Foster an inclusive environment where colleagues are encouraged to challenge existing ways of working, solve problems and improve the business.
* Align workforce and capacity plans with business demand, service expectations and anticipated growth.
* Use productivity and performance insights to guide organization design, resource allocation and investment decisions.

**What You'll Bring**

* 10+ years of progressive experience within commercial P&C insurance, including significant experience in Underwriting Operations, Underwriting Support or a closely related function.
* Significant leadership experience, including responsibility for managers and large or geographically distributed teams.
* Strong understanding of the end-to-end underwriting lifecycle and the operational capabilities required to support a specialty insurance business.
* Demonstrated success partnering with senior Underwriting and business leaders and translating strategy into execution.
* Proven experience designing and implementing operating models and leading complex operational transformation.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with demonstrated experience using data to identify root causes and improve business performance.
* Experience applying technology, workflow, automation and data to improve underwriting or operational outcomes.
* Strong understanding of operational controls, service management and continuous improvement.
* A track record of leading change from concept through implementation and delivering measurable results.
* Strong commercial judgment and exceptional stakeholder-management and communication skills.
* A collaborative, hands-on leadership style, with the confidence to challenge constructively and create accountability for outcomes.
* Experience managing budgets, resources and workforce plans.
* Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree or relevant insurance qualification preferred.

**What Success Looks Like** 
The successful candidate will help create a more scalable, responsive and technology-enabled operating model that: 

* Increases underwriting capacity and allows underwriters to focus more of their time on underwriting, portfolio management, broker relationships and profitable growth.
* Delivers measurable improvements in service, productivity, quality and operational control.
* Supports continued business growth without proportionate increases in cost or operational complexity.
* Converts technology, automation and AI investments into meaningful business outcomes.
* Builds a strong leadership bench and a high-performing Operations organization with clear accountability for results.

This is an opportunity to play a significant leadership role in shaping how Operations enables the next phase of growth in our U.S. Wholesale and Lower Middle Market businesses.

**Role Factors**

The role requires you to be in office 3 days per week. Travel may be included.

 

**What We Offer**

For this position, we currently expect to offer a base salary in the range of $180,000 - $235,000. Your salary offer will be based on an assessment of a variety of factors including your specific experience and work location.

In addition, you will be offered competitive target incentive compensation, with awards based on overall corporate and individual performance. On top of this, you will be eligible for a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes medical plans for you and your family, health and wellness programs, retirement plans, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation, and much more. Where this role is based in the United States of America, this role is Exempt for FLSA purposes.

**This posting is for an existing vacancy.**

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
**Job Overview**

The Director of Operations leads business operations and operations management, turning strategic plans into clear priorities and effective execution. You’ll guide executive-level teams, manage budgets and financial performance, and strengthen processes across the organization. This role calls for confident leadership, sound judgment, and a practical, data-driven approach to change and growth.

**Responsibilities**

* Lead operational excellence initiatives, process improvement, and operational analysis to improve business performance.
* Direct strategic planning, project management, and program management, aligning work with organizational priorities.
* Oversee executive-level budget management, financial management, budgeting, forecasting, and profit and loss analysis.
* Manage business development and business development management, identifying opportunities and coordinating execution.
* Lead change management, including large-scale organizational change, and communicate plans and progress clearly to executives. Your impact: Clear priorities and disciplined execution help teams deliver reliable operations and better serve customers.

**Qualifications**

* Demonstrated experience in operations management, business management, strategic management, and operational management.
* Experience in senior leadership, executive leadership, executive-level team management, management, and supervising experience.
* Strong budget management, financial management, forecasting, and profit and loss analysis skills.
* Proven ability to lead process improvement, project management, business development, and organizational change.
* Excellent verbal communication with executives and a record of data-driven decision making and strategic planning.

Pay: $45.00 - $95.00 per hour

Expected hours: 40.0 per week

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Flexible schedule
* Parental leave
* Retirement plan
* Tuition reimbursement

Work Location: Hybrid remote in North Chicago, IL 60064

records.title: Director - Service Operations
records.description:
As the **Director of Service Operations** at Lumos, you'll play a critical leadership role in delivering reliable fiber connectivity and an exceptional customer experience across our growing markets. You'll lead and develop regional operations teams, oversee service installations and maintenance, and drive the performance, safety, and efficiency of our field operations.

This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact as Lumos continues to expand, combining strategic leadership with hands-on operational expertise to strengthen service delivery, improve processes, and build high-performing teams that support our customers and continued growth.

This is a remote position supporting Service Operations across the Midwest region, with a preference for candidates located within a Lumos market in **Ohio, Indiana, or Kentucky**. Regional travel is required.

**Why Lumos:**

Lumos is transforming the future of connectivity by building one of the nation's fastest-growing 100% Fiber Optic networks. Through T-Fiber, our joint venture with T-Mobile, we're working toward a shared goal of connecting 12 to 15 million homes by 2030 while expanding access to reliable, high-speed internet in the communities we serve.

Here, you'll find more than a job, you'll have the opportunity to make an impact, take ownership of your work, and help shape how we grow. We move quickly, collaborate across teams, and believe the best ideas come from people who are curious, solutions-oriented, and ready to build what's next.

**What You'll Do:**

* Lead, coach, and develop regional Service Operations managers and teams, fostering accountability, collaboration, and a strong customer-first culture.
* Oversee service installations, maintenance, and field operations across assigned markets, ensuring consistent quality, safety, and operational performance.
* Establish and monitor KPIs, SLAs, and customer experience metrics to drive efficiency, service reliability, and continuous improvement.
* Develop and execute operational strategies that support market expansion, service delivery objectives, and long-term business growth.
* Manage department budgets, resources, and operational projects to ensure effective planning, execution, and cost management.
* Oversee vendor and contractor performance, including negotiations, service expectations, and accountability for operational results.
* Serve as a key escalation point for complex customer and operational challenges, driving timely resolution and improvements to the customer experience.
* Partner across Network Operations, Engineering, Construction, Customer Care, and other teams to improve workflows, strengthen service delivery, and support business objectives.
* Establish and maintain operational policies, procedures, and safety standards while identifying opportunities to improve processes and scale operations.

**What You'll Bring:**

* 7+ years of experience in telecommunications service operations, field operations, or a related area.
* Proven experience leading geographically dispersed teams, developing managers, and driving operational performance across multiple markets.
* Strong understanding of telecommunications service installation, maintenance, network operations, and customer service delivery.
* Experience managing operational budgets, vendor relationships, contractor performance, and service-level agreements.
* Ability to analyze KPIs, operational performance, and customer satisfaction metrics to identify trends and drive improvements.
* Strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and operational software platforms, with the ability to adapt to new systems and technologies.
* A proactive, solutions-oriented approach with the ability to work independently and lead effectively in a fast-paced environment.

**What Makes You a Great Fit:**

* High school diploma or equivalent.
* Bachelor's degree in business, telecommunications, engineering, or a related field.
* Direct experience in the fiber broadband or FTTH industry, including distributed and centralized split network architectures.
* Knowledge of central office infrastructure, network equipment, and telecommunications facilities.
* Experience improving customer satisfaction, NPS scores, and operational efficiency across multiple markets.
* A track record of developing high-performing teams, improving operational processes, and supporting growth in a scaling organization.
* A collaborative, hands-on leadership style with the ability to balance strategic priorities with day-to-day operational execution.

**Physical Requirements:**

* Frequently operates a computer, phone, and standard office tools.
* Ability to travel to properties and regional offices as needed.
* Near-constant use of sight, speech, hearing, comprehension, and reasoning.
* Must be able to sit or remain in a stationary position for extended periods.

**Benefits & Perks:**

Our commitment to communities includes recruiting and rewarding the Lumos team members who are working together to build a brighter tomorrow.

We have:

* Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage.
* Competitive compensation packages, including bonus options for eligible positions.
* Paid Time Off & Paid Holidays.
* Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) and Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs).
* 100% employer-paid life and disability insurance.
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP) with access to professional support for life's challenges.
* 401K plan w/ up to 5% employer contribution and a self-directed brokerage option.
* Wellness program offering education and cash incentives for gym attendance and nutrition programs.
* Employee referral bonuses.
* Discounts on Lumos Fiber Internet for employees who live in our service areas.
* Discounts on T-Mobile wireless service and select features for lines.

**Applicant Eligibility Notice:** 
Applicants must be at least eighteen (18) years of age at the time of application.

**At Lumos we recruit, hire, employ, train, promote, and compensate individuals based on job-related qualifications and abilities. We have a longstanding policy of providing a work environment that respects the dignity and worth of each individual and is free from all forms of employment discrimination, including harassment, because of race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws. We will provide reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals** **with disabilities or based on a sincerely held religious belief, in accordance with applicable laws.**

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
**U C Coatings Director of Operations**

**Reports to** President

**Location** Based at a U-C Coatings facility; Buffalo, NY or Kenosha, WI preferred

**Travel** Approximately 25-35%, including regular travel to all four sites and 3PL partners

**Scope** Buffalo, Kenosha, Seattle and Portland manufacturing sites; 3PLs; supply chain and sourcing; customer service

**Position summary**

U-C Coatings manufactures specialty coatings, wood protection and repair products for industrial and consumer markets. The **Director of Operations** leads the people, processes and resources that turn customer demand into safe, reliable production and accurate, timely delivery.

Reporting to the President, this leader is accountable for operating performance across four sites and the supporting supply chain, sourcing, logistics and customer service functions. The role requires regular time on the production floor, strong financial judgment, and the ability to develop capable site and functional leaders in a lean organization.

**Manufacturing and site leadership**

* Lead site leaders in Buffalo, NY, Kenosha, WI, Seattle, WA, and Portland, OR; establish clear responsibilities, operating standards and performance expectations across the network.
* Translate demand into production, staffing and capacity plans; improve batch scheduling, filling, packaging, labor productivity and equipment utilization.
* Improve yield, reduce scrap and rework, and address recurring downtime through preventive maintenance, root cause analysis and practical process improvements.
* Evaluate production allocation, interplant transfers, capital investments and facility changes to improve service, cost and available capacity.

**Supply chain and sourcing**

* Own procurement and supplier performance for raw materials, packaging, purchased products and operating supplies; negotiate pricing, terms and service commitments.
* Lead monthly demand and supply planning with Sales and Finance; align forecasts, purchasing and production with service goals and working capital requirements.
* Set replenishment and inventory policies by item and site; improve inventory accuracy, reduce excess and obsolete stock, and prevent material shortages.
* Develop qualified alternate sources and continuity plans for critical inputs; coordinate supplier and material changes with Technical and Quality before implementation.

**Logistics and third party warehousing**

* Manage 3PL contracts, service standards and performance reviews, including inventory reconciliation, order accuracy, shipping performance, claims and invoice audits.
* Control inbound, outbound, parcel, LTL and interplant freight costs; improve packaging, carrier selection and routing while meeting customer requirements.

**Customer Service**

* Lead Customer Service from order receipt through fulfillment; improve order entry accuracy, acknowledgments, delivery commitments and response times.
* Connect Customer Service, Sales, planning, plants and 3PLs so customers receive reliable commitments and proactive updates on shortages or delays.
* Resolve escalated service issues, returns and credits with Sales, Finance and Technical; use complaint and shipping error trends to eliminate repeat failures.

**Safety quality and compliance**

* Hold site leaders accountable for safe operations, training, inspections, incident reporting and timely corrective action; maintain clear escalation and stop-work authority.
* Partner with internal specialists and outside advisers to meet applicable workplace safety, environmental, storage, waste and shipping requirements at each site.
* Ensure operating teams follow approved formulations, batch records, quality checks, labeling and lot traceability; support product launches and process changes with Technical and Quality.

**Financial management and people leadership**

* Own operating budgets and explain labor, material, freight and overhead variances with Finance; deliver verified savings and capital projects with clear returns.
* Coach and evaluate site and functional leaders; build staffing, cross-training and succession plans, and address performance issues promptly with HR support.
* Run weekly site and consolidated scorecard reviews covering service, cost, quality, inventory and people; assign owners and deadlines and verify corrective actions.

**Qualifications**

* Ten or more years of progressive manufacturing operations experience, including at least five years leading managers or major operating functions.
* Demonstrated success leading multiple manufacturing sites or a comparably complex manufacturing and distribution network; ability to lead dispersed teams.
* Practical experience with procurement, inventory planning, logistics, outsourced warehousing and customer fulfillment; strong cost and financial analysis skills.
* Experience with ERP and MRP systems, Excel, operating scorecards and continuous improvement; ability to turn data into decisions and sustained results.
* Bachelor's degree in operations, supply chain, engineering, business or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. Coatings, chemicals, adhesives, sealants or other batch manufacturing experience is strongly preferred.

**Measures of success**

Accountable measures include safety controls; on-time, in-full delivery; labor efficiency; yield and cost of poor quality; inventory accuracy and turns; supplier and 3PL performance; freight costs; order accuracy; and leadership development. Agree on targets with the CEO after validating baselines.

**Initial priorities and working environment**

Within 90 days, assess the sites and key partners, validate scorecards, and agree on an improvement plan with owners, deadlines and financial impact. Work includes office, plant and warehouse activities, required PPE (company-provided), regular travel and occasional support outside business hours. Essential duties may be performed with reasonable accommodation.

**COMPANY DESCRIPTION:**

U-C Coatings is a leading manufacturer and supplier of premium wood protection products. For more than 50 years, our products have been used in a variety of industries, including hardwood and softwood logging and lumber production, wood products, manufacturing, woodworking, and wood decking markets.

Our products are used worldwide to protect, conserve, and enhance forest resources. Our goal is to help our customers achieve more with less waste and provide the highest level of protection for their products.

**ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:**

This role is an in-person role located within the company’s Kenosha, WI location. There is a moderate noise level within the work environment. Compliance with applicable Company policies including maintaining a drug-free workplace and adhering to all safety policies and procedures is required.

**DISCLAIMERS:**

UC Coatings, LLC reserves the right to revise, change or modify the duties and responsibilities of this position at any time to meet business needs. This job description may not list all duties for this position. This job description is not a contract of employment, and all UC Coatings, LLC employment unless otherwise disclosed is “at will” and either the incumbent or UC Coatings, LLC may terminate employment at any time for any reason.

UC Coatings, LLC is an Equal opportunity, inclusive employer and will consider all applicants for employment with the Company based on merit, competence, and qualifications without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, or any other category protected by federal, state, or local law.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Education:

* Bachelor's (Required)

Experience:

* Operations management: 5 years (Required)

Willingness to travel:

* 50% (Preferred)

Work Location: In person

records.title: Director of Production
records.description:
MHI Ship Repair & Services is a major marine repair and conversion contractor serving the U.S. Navy, Military Sealift Command, Maritime Administration and Commercial ship owners and operators worldwide. Our shipyard is conveniently located in the Mid-Atlantic region at the port of Hampton Roads, Norfolk Virginia.

**JOB SUMMARY:** Manages the operations of all production trades to include Facilities and Gas Free. Responsible for ensuring that all projects are manned with competent, properly trained and certified personnel, and the work efforts are coordinated and executed in a cost-effective manner, safely, and on time. Provides leadership and guidance to Shop Superintendants and oversees the maintenance and improvement of all shop equipment and development of shop procedures.

**SUPERVISES:** All Shop Superintendents

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Primary oversight of all production departments to include Facilities and Gas Free. Responsible for making strategic and tactical decisions related to certain aspects of MHI's production business to include operation non-Program work
* Responsible for ensuring that all projects are manned with competent, properly trained and certified personnel, and that work efforts are prioritized, coordinated and efforts integrated between departments and executed safely, in a cost-effective manner and on time.
* Ensures performance is within the guidelines of the contracts, delivery orders are received and that all contractual requirements are within the scope of work for the specific market and are met for U.S. Navy, Government, private shipyard, and commercial projects.
* Holds daily production meetings with all trades and Project Managers. Communicate with all department heads to ensure that any manning, scheduling, tooling, and material issues are identified and resolved.
* Attend all SRA Production Meetings.
* Walks through all in plant vessels daily verifying all work in progress and identifying and resolving any issues as they arise.
* Provides leadership and guidance to Shop Superintendants and oversees the maintenance and improvement of all shop equipment and development of shop procedures.
* Reviews and proofreads specs.

**ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Estimating as requested.
* May on occasion be required to manage a project.
* Performs other related duties as assigned by supervisor.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

* College education and 15 years progressive experience in the maritime industry. (Apprenticeship and practical experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.) Prior management experience a must.
* Ability to estimate.
* Basic knowledge of all skilled trades, and ability to manage effectively.
* Ability to communicate effectively as a leader.

MHI Ship Repair & Services offers competitive wages and an excellent benefit package.

Affirmative Action/EOE Employer of protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.

records.title: Regional Director of Operations
records.description:
**Regional Director of Operations (LNHA) – Iowa**
=================================================

**Company:** EMY Healthcare 
**Location:** Cedar Rapids–Des Moines, Iowa Region 
**Position Type:** Full-Time 
**Work Location:** Field-Based / Multiple Skilled Nursing Facilities 
**Travel:** Regular Regional Travel Required

### **About EMY Healthcare**

EMY Healthcare is a growing healthcare organization dedicated to providing exceptional skilled nursing, rehabilitation, and long-term care services throughout the Midwest. We are committed to delivering quality care, supporting our employees, and building strong, successful facilities through hands-on leadership and operational excellence.

As we continue expanding throughout Iowa, we are seeking an experienced, motivated, and results-driven **Regional Director of Operations (LNHA)** to oversee multiple skilled nursing facilities across the Cedar Rapids–Des Moines region.

### **Position Overview**

The Regional Director of Operations will provide operational leadership, oversight, and support to approximately 5–6 skilled nursing facilities located throughout the Cedar Rapids–Des Moines corridor, with the majority of facilities concentrated in the Cedar Rapids area.

**This position requires an active Licensed Nursing Home Administrator (LNHA) license and significant skilled nursing operational experience.**

This is a hands-on, field-based leadership position requiring regular travel between facilities. Candidates may reside in the Cedar Rapids, Iowa City, Des Moines, or surrounding areas, provided they are willing and able to travel regularly throughout the assigned region.

The ideal candidate will have a proven background in skilled nursing operations, a strong understanding of regulatory compliance and financial performance, and demonstrated success leading administrators, improving facility performance, and driving operational results.

We are looking for a leader who is proactive, organized, accountable, and comfortable working independently while collaborating closely with corporate and regional leadership.

### **Key Responsibilities**

**Operational Leadership & Facility Oversight**

* Provide direct operational oversight and support to approximately 5–6 skilled nursing facilities.
* Lead, mentor, and hold facility administrators accountable for operational, clinical, and financial performance.
* Conduct regular on-site visits to evaluate operations, identify opportunities for improvement, and provide hands-on support.
* Establish clear performance expectations and ensure consistent execution of company policies and operational standards.
* Assist facilities in resolving operational challenges and implementing sustainable improvements.
* Support administrator recruitment, onboarding, development, and retention.

**Financial Performance & Census Development**

* Oversee facility financial performance, including budgets, labor management, operating expenses, and profitability.
* Review financial statements, operational reports, and key performance indicators to identify trends and improvement opportunities.
* Work with administrators to develop and implement strategies to improve census, payer mix, and revenue.
* Monitor staffing levels, overtime, agency utilization, and labor costs while maintaining appropriate resident care.
* Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency and financial performance without compromising quality of care.

**Regulatory Compliance & Quality Improvement**

* Ensure facilities maintain compliance with applicable federal and state regulations.
* Partner with clinical leadership to support survey readiness, quality improvement initiatives, and corrective action plans.
* Assist administrators in addressing survey deficiencies, regulatory concerns, and operational risks.
* Promote a culture of accountability, resident-centered care, and continuous improvement.
* Support facilities through surveys, audits, and other regulatory activities as needed.

**Leadership & Collaboration**

* Work closely with facility administrators, Directors of Nursing, regional clinical leadership, and corporate departments.
* Conduct regular operational meetings and follow up on action plans and performance objectives.
* Provide guidance and support during leadership transitions, operational challenges, and facility improvement initiatives.
* Communicate regularly with executive leadership regarding facility performance, challenges, and opportunities.
* Help implement company-wide initiatives and best practices across assigned facilities.

### **Qualifications**

**Required:**

* **Current, active Licensed Nursing Home Administrator (LNHA) license. Iowa licensure preferred; candidates licensed in another state must be eligible to obtain Iowa licensure.**
* Significant experience in skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care operations.
* Previous experience as a Nursing Home Administrator, Regional Director of Operations, or comparable skilled nursing operational leadership role.
* Strong understanding of nursing home operations, regulatory compliance, financial management, staffing, and census development.
* Demonstrated ability to lead teams, improve operational performance, and hold facility leadership accountable.
* Strong analytical, organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to manage multiple facilities and competing priorities.
* **Willingness and ability to travel regularly throughout the Cedar Rapids–Des Moines region.**
* Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.

**Preferred:**

* Previous multi-facility or regional operations experience.
* Proven success improving facility financial performance, census, quality measures, and operational efficiency.
* Experience with facility turnarounds, acquisitions, or operational transitions.
* Familiarity with PointClickCare and skilled nursing operational reporting systems.
* Knowledge of Iowa nursing home regulations and survey processes.

### **What We Offer**

* Competitive compensation based on experience.
* Health insurance and employee benefits.
* 401(k) with company match.
* Travel reimbursement.
* Opportunities for professional growth and advancement.
* Supportive corporate and regional leadership.
* Opportunity to make a meaningful impact across multiple facilities within a growing healthcare organization.

### **Work Location & Travel Requirements**

**This is a regional, field-based position covering skilled nursing facilities between Des Moines and Cedar Rapids, Iowa, with the majority of facilities concentrated in the Cedar Rapids area.**

* Candidates may reside anywhere within reasonable traveling distance of the assigned facilities.
* Regular, in-person facility visits are an essential part of the position.
* The role requires flexibility to travel throughout the assigned region based on operational needs.
* Administrative responsibilities may be completed from home when not traveling or visiting facilities.
* Travel expenses will be reimbursed in accordance with company policy.
