records.title: Senior Director, Strategy & Operations, Point of Care, Remote
records.description:
Working in the Office of the Chief Medical Officer and reporting to the VP of Point of Care & Risk Stratification, the Senior Director of Strategy & Operations, Point of Care, will lead day-to-day operations, partnerships, go-to-market efforts, and wraparound support services to maximize the impact of Aledade’s value-based care insights to our partner practices. 
The team is looking for a high-output generalist with a strong business analyst toolkit, looking to rapidly take ownership of complex content with high visibility, working across multiple stakeholders. Candidates that thrive managing multiple deadlines on tight timelines and learning content quickly are best positioned to succeed; successful team members in the same function primarily have backgrounds in consulting and generalist healthcare strategy & operations roles.
To start, the role will focus on 1) scaling the deployment of our point of care tools and 2) broadening and deepening the insights available in our point of care tools, to maximize the impact of Aledade’s insights on our patients’ health outcomes and partner practices’ success in their value-based care contracts. 
At the end of their first year, a successful leader in the role will own end-to-end accountability for 1) proactive identification, development, and execution of Point of Care deployment improvement opportunities, including field, practice, and clinician education, deployment automation and monitoring, and go to market approach and materials, 2) strategic relationship building and partnership with Aledade’s payer partners to advance point of care tool adoption and impact, 3) goal setting, metric identification and development, and impact evaluation for our point of care tools, 4) identification, evaluation, contracting, and cross-functional execution of net new vendor and external partnerships that support insight delivery and impact.
Additionally, this role will 1) provide direction and expert guidance to junior team members owning individual initiatives, including incentive and adoption programs, educational efforts, hotspotting, monitoring, and alerting development, practice and user-level prioritization and triage, and 2) coordinate with cross-functional product, analytics, technology, performance, care programs, and other senior leaders across Aledade to advance point of care tool adoption and impact.
The role is expected to start as a senior individual contributor, but is expected to grow into a people manager in the near term.

Primary Duties: 
In collaboration with cross-functional product, analytics, technology, performance, care programs, and other senior leaders across Aledade:
Own single-threaded accountability for proactive identification, development, and execution of Point of Care deployment improvement opportunities, including field, practice, and clinician education, deployment automation and monitoring, and go to market approach and materials
Lead strategic relationship building and partnership with Aledade’s payer partners to advance point of care tool adoption and impact
Drive goal setting, metric identification and development, and impact evaluation for our point of care tools
In support of maximizing insight delivery and impact, lead the evaluation, contracting, and cross-functional execution of net new vendor and external partnerships
Direct and support other Transformation team members’ ideation and execution of strategic initiatives related to point of care deployment and impact
Minimum Qualifications: 
Bachelor’s Degree required, preferably in Economics, Business, Healthcare, or a related field
12+ years of progressive professional experience, or 7+ years progressive professional experience with a Master’s Degree, strongly preferred
6+ years of experience in healthcare
2+ years of experience in value-based care
Preferred Qualifications: 
Advanced exploration of emerging AI tools, with additional preference given to individuals that have demonstrated ability building, scaling, and/or teaching AI tooling to broader teams
Expert Excel skills required, including the ability to work with large, complex, & often incomplete data sets; conduct one-off complex analyses quickly; and utilize Index / Match, XLOOKUP, FILTER, and other advanced formulas
Advanced PPT skills required, including storyboarding skills, ability to translate complex analyses and concepts into engaging slides, and ability to draft executive-level materials with limited direction
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, as well as the ability to build strong relationships and work with individuals at all levels of the organization, tailoring communication style as appropriate based on audience
Excellent project management skills, including proven track record leading complex, cross-functional initiatives in health care operations settings
Strong strategic planning and analytical skills
Strong “business analyst” toolkit, including abilities to independently prioritize, solve problems via hypothesis-driven analytical methods, manage across multiple responsibilities and projects, execute with attention to detail, and overcome ambiguity
Poise, confidence, and maturity interacting with key stakeholders, including senior leaders
Commitment to confidentiality and discretion in appropriately handling sensitive information is required
Physical Requirements:
Sitting for prolonged periods of time. Extensive use of computers and keyboard. Occasional walking and lifting may be required.
Who We Are:
Aledade PBC, a public benefit corporation, exists to empower the most transformational part of our health care landscape - independent primary care. We were founded in 2014, and since then, we've become the largest network of independent primary care in the country - helping practices, health centers and clinics deliver better care to their patients and thrive in value-based care. Additionally, by creating value-based contracts across a wide variety of health plans, we aim to flip the script on the traditional fee-for-service model. Our work strengthens continuity of care, aligns incentives and ensures primary care physicians are paid for what they do best - keeping patients healthy. If you want to help create a health care system that is good for patients, good for practices and good for society - and if you're eager to join a collaborative, inclusive and remote-first culture - you've come to the right place.
 
What Does This Mean for You?
At Aledade PBC, you will be part of a creative culture that is driven by a passion for tackling complex issues with respect, open-mindedness and a desire to learn. You will collaborate with team members who bring a wide range of experiences, interests, backgrounds, beliefs and achievements to their work - and who are all united by a shared passion for public health and a commitment to the Aledade mission.
 
In addition to time off to support work-life balance and enjoyment, we offer the following comprehensive benefits package designed for the overall well-being of our team members:
 
Flexible work schedules and the ability to work remotely are available for many roles
Health, dental and vision insurance paid up to 80% for employees, dependents and domestic partners
Robust time-off plan (21 days of PTO in your first year)
Two paid volunteer days and 11 paid holidays
12 weeks paid parental leave for all new parents
Six weeks paid sabbatical after six years of service
Educational Assistant Program and Clinical Employee Reimbursement Program
401(k) with up to 4% match
Stock options
And much more!
 
At Aledade PBC, we don’t just accept differences, we celebrate them! We strive to attract, develop and retain highly qualified individuals representing the diverse communities where we live and work. Aledade is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. Employment policies and decisions at Aledade are based on merit, qualifications, performance and business needs. All qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth or medical conditions related to pregnancy or childbirth), gender identity or expression, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, legally protected genetic information, marital status, veteran status, or sexual orientation.

records.title: Plant Manager
records.description:
CAMS is looking for a Plant Manager at the Kings Mountain Energy Center in Kings Mountain, NC. The incumbent will have 19 direct and indirect employees. The Plant Manager is responsible for the safe, reliable, compliant, and financially responsible operation and maintenance of the Kings Mountain Energy Center.
Kings Mountain Energy Center is a 475MW natural gas-fired combined-cycle power plant. The facility features an advanced 276MW Mitsubishi M501GAC gas turbine, a Vogt Power heat recovery steam generator (HRSG), a 225MW Toshiba steam turbine generator, and a Thermal Engineering International surface condenser.
The position provides overall leadership for plant operations, maintenance, engineering support, environmental and regulatory compliance, administration, workforce development, budgeting, outage execution, and continuous improvement. The Plant Manager serves as the primary site representative to CAMS leadership, facility ownership and asset management, and is accountable for developing a high-performing organization that maximizes plant availability, reliability, efficiency, and long-term asset value. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong leadership, sound technical and business judgment, and the ability to manage a complex combined-cycle generating facility in a competitive power-market environment.                          

Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Provide overall leadership and direction for the safe, reliable, environmentally compliant, and cost-effective operation and maintenance of the facility.
Establish and maintain a strong safety culture in which employees and contractors actively identify hazards, stop unsafe work, and demonstrate personal ownership of safety performance.
Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local environmental permits, laws, regulations, NERC requirements, OSHA requirements, company policies, and facility procedures.
Lead and develop the plant management team and workforce, including recruiting, coaching, performance management, succession planning, qualification programs, and workforce development.
Maintain effective working relationships with facility ownership, Asset Management, CAMS leadership, regulatory agencies, the system operator, utilities, OEMs, contractors, and other key stakeholders.
Develop and execute annual operating plans, O&M budgets, capital plans, forecasts, and long-term maintenance strategies consistent with owner objectives and contractual requirements.
Monitor plant financial performance and control expenditures while ensuring that short-term budget objectives do not create unacceptable safety, environmental, reliability, or long-term asset risk.
Direct plant operations to achieve availability, reliability, heat-rate, start-reliability, capacity, and other performance objectives while meeting dispatch and commercial obligations.
Provide leadership for maintenance strategies, preventive and predictive maintenance, corrective-maintenance backlog management, equipment reliability, root-cause analysis, and elimination of recurring failures.
Direct planning and execution of combustion turbine, steam turbine, HRSG, generator, electrical, and balance-of-plant outages and major maintenance activities, including scope, budget, schedule, contractor performance, quality, and risk management.
Develop and maintain multi-year outage, major-maintenance, and capital improvement plans based on equipment condition, OEM recommendations, operating profile, commercial requirements, and risk.
Identify significant plant risks and provide CAMS leadership and ownership with timely information, alternatives, consequences, and clear recommendations for decision-making.
Ensure appropriate critical-spares strategy, inventory controls, long-lead component planning, and equipment-obsolescence management.
Oversee plant engineering and technical support activities, including equipment modifications, controls and logic changes, performance monitoring, capital projects, and technical problem solving.
Ensure plant procedures, drawings, technical documentation, training materials, emergency plans, and operating records are accurate and maintained.
Oversee administration of applicable plant contracts and agreements and ensure operational compliance with owner requirements, O&M obligations, OEM/LTSA requirements, fuel and utility agreements, and other commercial commitments.
Maintain effective communication with Asset Management and ownership, including prompt escalation of significant safety, environmental, operational, equipment, financial, contractual, or regulatory events.
Lead emergency response and business-continuity activities and ensure the facility is prepared for severe weather, grid emergencies, fuel interruptions, cyber events, and major equipment failures.
Promote a culture of accountability, teamwork, continuous improvement, and open communication across Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Compliance, and Administration.
Identify and implement opportunities to improve plant performance, reduce operating risk, optimize costs, and increase long-term asset value.
Support CAMS fleet initiatives, peer reviews, lessons learned, workforce-development efforts, and cross-facility technical support as requested.
Other duties as assigned.
  Qualifications and Skills
10+ years of progressively responsible experience in power generation operations and maintenance, including significant leadership experience in a power plant environment.
Prior Plant Manager, Operations Manager, Maintenance Manager, or comparable senior power-generation leadership experience strongly preferred.
Demonstrated knowledge of combined-cycle power plant operations, maintenance, reliability, and major equipment systems. Experience with combustion turbines, steam turbines, HRSGs, generators, electrical systems, and balance-of-plant equipment is preferred.
Experience with Mitsubishi M501GAC combustion turbines is preferred.
Demonstrated experience planning and executing major outages, managing contractors and OEMs, controlling outage scope and cost, and resolving emergent technical issues.
Working knowledge of environmental, health and safety, and electric-generation regulatory requirements applicable to power plant operations.
Demonstrated experience developing and managing O&M budgets, forecasts, capital projects, and long-term maintenance plans.
Proven ability to lead, coach, develop, and hold accountable a multidisciplinary workforce.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, decision-making, planning, and organizational skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with employees, executives, owners, regulators, contractors, and technical personnel.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field preferred. Significant relevant power-generation leadership experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and familiarity with computerized maintenance management systems, plant historians, performance-monitoring systems, and other power-plant business systems.
Ability to respond to plant emergencies and significant operating events outside normal business hours as required.
Other Desirable Skills
Demonstrates visible leadership and a strong personal commitment to safety and environmental compliance.
Balances technical, operational, financial, and commercial considerations when making decisions.
Communicates significant risks and problems early and avoids surprises for ownership and senior leadership.
Demonstrates strong customer service skills and the ability to build trusted relationships with facility ownership and Asset Management.
Effectively prioritizes competing demands in a fast-changing operating environment.
Develop people and create clear succession paths for key positions.
Demonstrates a high degree of integrity, accountability, sound judgment, and ownership mentality.
Ability to represent the facility and CAMS professionally with owners, regulators, industry organizations, and external stakeholders
Applicants must possess a valid driver's license and maintain a clean driving record, as this position requires occasional travel for company business. Candidates should be comfortable operating a vehicle as part of their job responsibilities and must meet any applicable company and insurance requirements.
CAMS offers a variety of excellent benefits. Full-time employees are offered the following: medical, dental, vision, LTD, STD, and Life insurance plans. You can even select additional “al la carte” benefits to meet all your needs. You can also enroll in our 401k, flex spending accounts for medical and childcare needs, and participate in our employee referral and tuition reimbursement programs.
Qualified Applicants must be legally authorized for employment in the United States. Qualified Applicants will not require employer sponsored work authorization now or in the future for employment in the United States.
We believe in transparency and providing candidates with important information to make informed decisions. The salary range for this position will be commensurate with experience, qualifications, and location. Actual compensation will be determined based on several factors, including but not limited to skills, experience, and relevant qualifications.
This range represents the base salary and does not include other forms of compensation, such as bonuses, benefits, or equity, which may be offered in addition to the base pay. The company reserves the right to modify.

records.title: Director, MSAT/External Manufacturing Management
records.description:
OPPORTUNITY
Mammoth Biosciences is seeking a Director, Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) to lead the scale-up of our lipid nanoparticle (LNP) drug product process from Phase 1 into Phase 2 and toward late stage readiness. This leader will own the technical path from the current clinical process to a well-characterized, scalable process that is ready for process performance qualification (PPQ).
All manufacturing and analytical work is performed at external contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) and contract testing labs. The Director will be Mammoth's technical owner of the process at those partners, ensuring that development, technology transfer, process characterization and PPQ are executed in line with current regulatory guidance and industry best practice.
This is a build role. Initially the Director will deliver through external resources (CDMOs, consultants and contract staff), then grow an internal MSAT team in stages as program milestones are met. The role reports to the Head of CMC and works closely with Process Development, Analytical Development, Quality, Regulatory CMC, Supply Chain and Program Management.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Process scale-up and technology transfer
Lead scale-up of the Phase 1 LNP process (nucleic acid payload formulation, mixing, buffer exchange/TFF, sterile filtration and fill) to Phase 2 and late-stage clinical scale
Define the scale-up strategy, including equipment selection, mixing platform scalability, scale-down model development and comparability between process versions
Plan and execute technology transfers of processes and methods between Mammoth, development partners and GMP CDMOs, including transfer protocols, gap assessments and engineering runs
Own the technical risk assessments (e.g., FMEA) that drive scale-up and characterization priorities
Process characterization and PPQ readiness
Build the control strategy using a QbD approach: define CQAs and CPPs, link material attributes to product quality, and set proven acceptable ranges
Design and oversee process characterization studies (DoE, qualified scale-down models, hold times, mixing and filtration studies) that support the control strategy and regulatory filings
Lead PPQ planning and execution: validation master plan inputs, PPQ protocols and reports, acceptance criteria, sampling plans and the transition to continued process verification
Partner with Analytical Development to make sure methods are phase-appropriate, validated on time and fit to support characterization and PPQ
External manufacturing and CDMO management
Serve as Mammoth's technical lead and person-in-plant at CDMOs and contract labs for development, engineering and GMP campaigns
Lead selection, qualification and oversight of CDMO partners for drug product manufacturing, fill-finish operations and drug product testing, including technical due diligence, capacity and capability assessment, and scale-up fit
Provide technical oversight for engineering and GMP runs at external partners
Develop scalable, phase-appropriate aseptic drug product processes at CDMOs, including fill-finish operations, cryogenic handling (as applicable) and cold-chain compatibility
Assess and implement suitable container-closure systems (vials, syringes) that meet regulatory and operational requirements
Accountable for review and approval of batch records in accordance with regulatory guidelines; review campaign plans, deviations, investigations, CAPAs and change controls in partnership with Quality
Manage partner timelines, budgets, deliverables and quality in collaboration with internal stakeholders; drive technical decisions and escalate issues early
Project manage external stakeholders and high-profile partner meetings (up to 10% of time)
Contribute to technical sections of quality agreements, statements of work and budgets
Regulatory and cross-functional support
Author and review CMC sections for IND/IMPD/CTA amendments, end-of-Phase 2 and later filings (Module 3 process description, process development history, process validation)
Support regulatory interactions and inspections with process knowledge and data
Provide manufacturing input to program plans, timelines and supply forecasts
Team and resource leadership
In the early phase, deliver through external resources: CDMO technical teams, consultants and contract MSAT staff
Build the internal MSAT function in stages tied to milestones, including hiring plans, roles and the balance of internal and outsourced work
Set up MSAT systems and practices: tech transfer templates, process knowledge management, data trending and lifecycle documentation
REEQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
PhD in chemical engineering, pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry or a related field with 10+ years of industry experience, or MS with 14+ or BS with 16+ years of experience
6+ years in MSAT, process development or technical operations for parenteral drug products, including at least 3 years in a leadership role
Hands-on experience scaling up LNP or comparable complex parenteral processes (liposomes, nanoparticles, nucleic acid formulations) from early clinical to late-stage scale
Led at least one process characterization and PPQ campaign through completion, with working command of ICH Q8–Q12 and FDA/EMA process validation expectations
Extensive experience managing CDMOs and contract labs as the sponsor's technical lead, including tech transfer, person-in-plant oversight, deviations and change control
Experience with fill-finish operations, aseptic processing and external manufacturing oversight
Strong working knowledge of cryogenic storage and cold-chain management for LNP drug products
Track record of authoring CMC regulatory sections and supporting agency interactions
Ability to influence and direct external partners without line authority, and to make sound technical calls under timeline pressure
Ability for frequent domestic and international travel to CDMO and contract lab sites, estimated at up to [30–40]% and peaking during engineering, characterization and PPQ campaigns
Must be able to travel internationally on short notice and hold, or be able to obtain, a valid passport and any visas needed for partner sites
Ability to commit to extended on-site presence at CDMOs (person-in-plant) during critical campaigns, sometimes across time zones.
Based in the San Francisco Bay Area preferred, with ability to work onsite at our Brisbane, CA location; hybrid or remote arrangements are available
Ability to work Pacific Time Zone hours if not located on the West Coast
Ability to travel to Mammoth’s Brisbane, CA HQ regularly if not local
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
Direct experience with mRNA/LNP or gene editing drug products
Experience with impingement jet or microfluidic mixing scale-up, TFF and sterile filtration of LNPs
Experience with commercial process validation and BLA/MAA preparation

records.title: Director of Quality
records.description:
Company Overview
ACS (Allen Control Systems) is a defense technology company building precision robotic systems for the United States and its allies. Founded by two former U.S. Navy electrical engineers with deep experience in robotics and software, ACS brings together AI, computer vision, precision motion, and advanced hardware to solve complex defense challenges across land, air, and maritime environments.

Our flagship product, Bullfrog, is an autonomous precision weapon system that transforms existing weapons into highly accurate counter-drone systems — giving warfighters a scalable, cost-effective response to one of the fastest-growing threats on the modern battlefield. Bullfrog is deployed with U.S. forces, and ACS works with organizations throughout the U.S. military and national security community.

Following a $200 million Series B at a $2.2 billion valuation, ACS is rapidly expanding manufacturing, accelerating Bullfrog deployments, and developing the next generation of autonomous battlefield systems. This is an opportunity to join a proven, fast-moving team and help scale technology with direct, real-world impact on national security.

ACS is headquartered in Austin, Texas, with additional operations in Alexandria, Virginia; Mountain View, California; and Huntsville, Alabama. For more information, visit allencontrolsystems.com http://allencontrolsystems.com.




Position Overview
We're looking for a Director of Quality to build our quality function from the ground up — including our path toward ISO 9001 — and lead it for the long haul. This role sets the multi-year quality strategy while staying grounded in what's really happening on the floor, in the supply base, and with customers. Our hardware matters; defects here aren't abstract metrics. Our core philosophy is quality at the source: quality can't be inspected in after the fact, it has to be built right the first time. QA is the backstop, not the primary defense — an escape that reaches the customer is a production failure, not a QA failure.
We want a pragmatic leader who favors simple, practical problem-solving (5 Whys, direct observation) over paperwork-heavy processes, and who will build a genuine partnership with Supply Chain and supplier quality engineers to catch issues at the source rather than at receiving.

What You'll Do:

Strategic & Long-Range Leadership
• Own the long-range quality strategy, translating business goals into a multi-year plan for systems, staffing, and capability.
• Architect our Quality Management System — including our path toward ISO 9001 — from the ground up, building processes that are clear and simple, not just audit-ready.
• Own the audit calendar as the QMS matures, treating findings as strategic input, not a checkbox.
• Set and report quality KPIs (defect rates, first-pass yield, complaints, supplier performance); a data point is noise, a trend is a signal.
• Put every requirement, gate, and approval on trial — if no one can name who owns it and why it exists, that's the signal to cut it, not preserve it.

Ground Truth & Root Cause
• Get out onto the floor, into supplier facilities, and in front of customers regularly — not just working from what's reported up the chain.
• Personally lead or coach RCCA using practical, lightweight tools (5 Whys, direct observation) instead of heavy formal methodologies when they aren't warranted.
• Move with urgency: default to “why can't this be fixed today,” not “when can we fit this in.”

Supply Chain & Supplier Quality
• Build a close partnership with Supply Chain and supplier quality engineers, treating supplier quality as a shared mission.
• Drive supplier qualification, scorecards, and joint problem-solving to resolve issues at the source.
• Serve as the primary quality point of contact for DCMA surveillance, audits, and findings.

Stakeholder Relationships
• Partner especially closely with Engineering and Manufacturing — closing the loop between field/production issues and design decisions, and keeping quality and throughput goals aligned.
• Own key external customer relationships on quality matters, building credibility through transparency and follow-through.

Team & Culture
• Manage, mentor, and develop the quality team with a bias toward action and practical problem-solving.
• Keep the QMS lean — every process should exist because it supports a real decision, not because it looks good on paper.
• Own customer complaints and non-conformances through to true root cause and permanent corrective action.

What You'll Need:
• 8+ years in quality leadership, ideally in manufacturing, hardware, or defense/aerospace.
• Experience building or scaling a QMS; ISO 9001 experience strongly preferred (we are not yet certified — you'll help drive us there).
• A track record of practical, tool-light RCCA (5 Whys, direct observation) over heavyweight, paperwork-driven processes.
• Experience partnering closely with Supply Chain and supplier quality engineers.
• Comfort operating at both strategic altitude and on the floor — this is a hands-on role, not a desk job.
• Strong communication skills and the ability to influence engineering, manufacturing, and executive leadership alike.

What We Offer

 - Competitive salary

 - ACS Equity Package

 - Health, Dental, and Vision Insurance

 - Paid Time Off

Allen Control Systems prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.



The Role

We're hiring our first Sr. Manager of Production Planning & Scheduling to own the factory side execution. Where our S&OP function decides where and whether we can build across the network, you own how and when it actually gets built on the floor. You'll own discrete operational scheduling, job sequencing and priority, and the daily/weekly rhythm that ensures on-time delivery (OTD) and sets the factory up for success.

This role reports to our Operations leadership and drives a consistent scheduling methodology across the network, while partnering closely with each site General Manager on execution. Your scheduling and planning team members will support the sites day-to-day (dotted-line to the GM) while you own the standards, methodology, and rigor centrally.

This is a builder and owner role. While the team is built out, you'll be hands-on developing the scheduling methodologies, communication rigor, and visual management that don't exist yet, and turning them into standard work. You'll be the person the floor, Program Management, and leadership rely on for a clear, credible answer to "what are we running, in what order, and are we going to hit the date?"

You'll partner tightly with the S&OP function, translating network-level allocation and capacity plans into an executable factory schedule — and feeding real execution signal back up to highlight and drive capacity improvements.

What You'll Do:

Own Production Scheduling & Execution

· Own discrete production scheduling and job sequencing across work centers to maximize on-time delivery and throughput.

· Own work order release to the floor and control what work is released and when.

· Set and manage priority and milestone dates, establish clear, transparent rules for what runs when, and make the trade-off calls when priorities conflict.

· Own data integrity for schedules and dates in the system, and maintain and drive accurate MRP schedules so plans, priorities, and downstream commitments can be trusted.

· Build the daily/weekly scheduling cadence and standard work that keeps the floor aligned, from shift-level execution to weekly look-ahead.

· Translate S&OP network allocation and capacity plans into an executable, sequenced factory schedule.

· Partner closely with the site General Manager to align on priorities, sequencing, and daily execution serving as the GM's right hand for turning the plan into on-time output.

· Establish the system and cadence for tracking work order progress through the floor, monitors status against milestone dates, surfaces at risk jobs early, and drives rapid recovery on exceptions.

Drive OTD & Factory Performance

 - Own on time delivery as a primary metric track it, root cause misses, and close the gaps.

 - Ensure the factory is set up for success: materials, tooling, capacity, and priorities aligned ahead of the work, not discovered at the machine.

 - Highlight and drive capacity improvements — surface constraints and bottlenecks from real execution data and partner with Operations and Engineering to resolve them.

 - Feed execution signal (actual cycle times, constraints, attainment) back to S&OP to sharpen capacity models and sellable-capacity commitments.

Build Methodology, Rigor & Visibility

 - Develop the scheduling methodologies and logic from the ground up, sequencing rules, buffering, prioritization frameworks and codify them as standard work applied consistently across sites.

 - Establish communication rigor: the meeting cadence, escalation paths, and reporting that keep the floor, the GMs, and leadership on the same page.

 - Build the visual management schedules, boards, dashboards, and status views that make factory status, priorities, and risks obvious at a glance.

 - Establish key scheduling metrics: OTD, schedule adherence, past due, work center utilization, and cycle time performance.

People Leadership

 - Lead, coach, and develop a team of production planners and schedulers as the function scales, including team members embedded at and dotted lined to the sites.

 - Build organizational capability through talent development, standard work, training, and performance management.

 - Foster a culture of accountability, urgency, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications

· Proven experience in production planning, scheduling, or shop floor operations management in a discrete manufacturing environment.

· Deep understanding of production scheduling, sequencing, priority management, master scheduling, capacity/constraint analysis, and OTD drivers.

· Hands on experience with scheduling/ERP/MES systems and strong analytical and data visualization skills.

· Experience leading teams and developing planning/scheduling talent.

· Strong communication and facilitation skills, with the ability to drive urgency and accountability on the floor.

· ERP/MRP expertise work order lifecycle, MRP mechanics, and maintaining schedule/date data integrity at scale.

Education & Experience Requirements

 - Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations Management, Business, Engineering, Finance, or related discipline preferred.

 - 5+ years of progressive experience in production planning, scheduling, or manufacturing operations.

Role Summary

The Director, Forward Deployed Engineering leads the technical arm of Hadrian's Customer Programs motion. You sit inside Build Engineering and partner directly with the Customer Programs team, owning the manufacturing scoping of new customer engagements: translating what a customer wants into what Hadrian will actually commit to and build.

This role works directly with customers every day. For many of them, you and your team are the face of Hadrian engineering, so how you show up in the room matters as much as the technical answer. The work starts with discovery. Before anything is proposed, you and your team get inside the customer's operation: observing how work actually flows, mapping their processes and constraints, and interviewing the people closest to the problem until you understand what they need, which is often different from what they first ask for.

From there, you shape a solution that maximizes what the customer gets out of the engagement and builds toward where Hadrian is headed. The craft is steering to the answer where the customer's best outcome and Hadrian's direction reinforce each other: high impact, low effort, and built on what we already do well rather than new obligations we then have to invent our way out of.

The intent behind housing this role in Build Engineering is clean accountability: your team scopes what we commit to, and Build Engineering delivers it. That means the commitments you shape have to be grounded in first-principles engineering judgment and a real understanding of the factory, not optimism. You evaluate and understand before you propose or promise.


Key Responsibilities

 - Represent Hadrian with customers day to day: Own the technical relationship with customer engineering, program, and leadership teams. Run working sessions, present findings and recommendations, handle hard questions and pushback in the room, and follow up with clear, accurate written communication. Every interaction should leave the customer more confident in Hadrian.

 - Discover before you design: Embed with customers to observe their operations, map processes, constraints, and pain points, and interview stakeholders from the shop floor to program leadership. Build a clear, evidence-based picture of the real need before any solution is on the table.

 - Shape the solution: Fold what you learn into a solution that maximizes customer output and moves Hadrian toward what we are building. Hold an accurate picture of current capability and roadmap, and steer each engagement to the point where those two goals reinforce each other, favoring existing capabilities over new obligations.

 - Partner with Customer Programs: Operate on a dotted line to Customer Programs as their forward deployed engineering arm, bringing technical judgment into every engagement from first conversation through commitment.

 - Lead the forward deployed engineering team: Build, manage, and develop a technical team that engages directly with customers during new program scoping. Set the standard for how the team runs discovery, evaluates opportunities, and communicates with customers in a technical, credible, low-ego way.

 - Scope new customer engagements: Own the manufacturing scoping of new engagements: review requirements, drawings, specifications, tolerances, materials, and volumes, and define a manufacturing solution that Hadrian can commit to with confidence.

 - Evaluate before you promise: Bring a first-principles engineering mindset to every engagement. Understand the problem and the constraints before proposing or committing to a solution, so that what we sign up for is real and deliverable.

 - Hand off cleanly to Build Engineering: Ensure every commitment is scoped so that the Build Engineering organization can deliver it: clear product definition, make-vs-buy posture, process capability requirements, and a manufacturing plan that stands up to execution.

 - Drive leverage, not one-offs: Recognize recurring customer patterns and turn them into repeatable scoping approaches and reusable solution templates, so the function scales with the business instead of scaling headcount linearly.

Saronic is seeking a Business Development Manager to lead growth initiatives across the U.S. Special Operations community. records.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.

About the Role:

We are seeking a Head of Manufacturing Engineering to lead the development and scale-up of our manufacturing systems for high-volume small unmanned aircraft production. This leader will own the manufacturing engineering organization responsible for translating product designs into robust, automated, production-ready manufacturing systems capable of operating reliably at scale.

A major focus of this role will be factory automation, controls engineering, equipment development, and manufacturing systems architecture. You will build and lead a multidisciplinary organization spanning manufacturing engineering, automation and controls, equipment engineering, process development, and production industrialization.

The ideal candidate has experience scaling complex electromechanical products from early production into high-rate manufacturing, with a strong understanding of how automation, controls, data, equipment design, and process engineering come together to create a world-class production system.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can establish the long-term manufacturing strategy while also driving execution on the factory floor.



How You’ll Make an Impact:

 - Build, lead, and develop a high-performing Manufacturing Engineering organization supporting production from new product introduction through high-volume manufacturing.

 - Define the manufacturing engineering strategy, technical roadmap, organizational structure, and capabilities required to support significant production growth.

 - Partner closely with Design Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Test Engineering, and Product teams to ensure products are designed for manufacturability, automation, testability, and scale.

 - Establish manufacturing standards, design reviews, equipment specifications, process qualification methodologies, and production-readiness criteria.

 - Lead the architecture, development, deployment, and lifecycle management of automated manufacturing equipment and production systems.

 - Build strong internal capabilities in controls engineering, PLC programming, industrial robotics, motion control, machine vision, industrial networking, sensors, servo systems, safety systems, and automated material handling.

 - Establish controls and automation standards that enable equipment to be deployed, supported, replicated, and scaled rapidly across production.

 - Develop strategies for balancing manual, semi-automated, and fully automated manufacturing based on production rate, process capability, economics, and product maturity.

 - Establish disciplined equipment development processes including requirements definition, design reviews, FAT/SAT, commissioning, process validation, and production acceptance.

 - Partner with external automation integrators and equipment suppliers while developing critical automation and controls capabilities internally.

 - Build a highly instrumented manufacturing environment where equipment and processes generate actionable production data.

 - Partner with software and data teams to connect manufacturing equipment with MES, traceability, quality, and factory data systems.

 - Develop automated collection and analysis of process parameters, equipment states, cycle times, downtime, quality results, and genealogy.

 - Use manufacturing data to identify process drift, predict failures, improve yield, and accelerate root-cause analysis.



What Makes You a Good Fit:

 - 12+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, automation engineering, controls engineering, equipment engineering, or related disciplines.

 - 5+ years of experience leading engineering organizations responsible for manufacturing systems or factory automation.

 - Demonstrated experience scaling complex electromechanical products into high-volume production.

 - Experience in aerospace, automotive, robotics, industrial automation, electronics, battery, semiconductor, or another highly engineered manufacturing environment; aerospace experience strongly preferred.

 - Deep understanding of manufacturing automation and controls, including several of the following:
   
   - PLC and industrial controls architectures
   
   - Robotics and robotic cells
   
   - Servo and motion-control systems
   
   - Machine vision
   
   - Industrial networking and communications
   
   - Sensors and instrumentation
   
   - Automated test and inspection
   
   - Machine safety systems
   
   - SCADA/HMI systems
   
   - Manufacturing equipment software

 - Experience developing custom production equipment from concept through production deployment.

 - Experience developing capital equipment strategies and managing significant CapEx programs.

 - Strong understanding of DFM/DFA and the ability to influence product architecture to enable manufacturing scale and automation.

 - Experience operating in environments requiring rigorous configuration management, traceability, process control, and quality systems.

 - Demonstrated ability to recruit, develop, and lead multidisciplinary technical organizations.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to move between factory-level strategy and detailed engineering problems.

 - Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Controls Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related technical field.

 - Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions.



Preferred Qualifications

 - Experience scaling aerospace or similarly complex hardware from low-rate initial production to hundreds or thousands of units per month.

 - Experience building an automation and controls engineering function from the ground up.

 - Experience designing manufacturing systems for products combining mechanical assemblies, electronics, motors, sensors, batteries, composites, or other complex electromechanical technologies.

 - Familiarity with aerospace manufacturing and quality frameworks such as AS9100.

 - Experience with MES, equipment connectivity, manufacturing data infrastructure, and Industry 4.0 architectures.

 - Experience with automated inspection, machine vision, robotic assembly, dispensing, fastening, material handling, or automated test systems.

 - Experience developing standardized automation platforms that can be replicated across multiple production lines or factories.

 - Experience working in fast-growth hardware organizations where product design and manufacturing systems evolve simultaneously.

 - Master's degree in an engineering discipline or equivalent technical experience.

postedPay.title: VP of Mission Assurance & Quality (MA&Q)
postedPay.text: This is a full time, exempt position, based out of our Saratoga office.  The target base pay for this position is $190,000- $225,000annually.  The total compensation packaged will be determined by various factors such as your relevant job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

records.description:
Ready to make connectivity from space universally accessible, secure and actionable? Then you’ve come to the right place!

E-Space is bridging Earth and space to enable hyper-scaled deployments of Internet of Things (IoT) solutions and services. We are building a highly-advanced low Earth orbit (LEO) space system that will fundamentally change the design, economics, manufacturing and service delivery associated with traditional satellite and terrestrial IoT systems.

We’re intentional, we’re unapologetically curious and we’re 100% committed to innovate space-based communications and deliver actionable intelligence that will expand global economies, protect space and our planet and enhance our overall quality of life. 


The VP, Mission Assurance & Quality (MA&Q) holds the independent oversight authority that ensures every spacecraft is safe, reliable, and qualified before it launches. This role is structurally independent of all other VP organizations - the authority to halt work, reject deliverables, and withhold qualification sign-off cannot be overridden by any VP. Only the CTO can override an MA&Q determination, and that override is documented with the MA&Q position on record regardless of outcome.
 
Independence is the defining feature of this role. MA&Q does not build hardware, does not own schedule, and does not report to any VP who does. This structural separation is deliberate - quality and safety decisions must never be compromised by production pressure, schedule urgency, or cost targets.
 
The VP, MA&Q must be willing to halt a production line, delay a gate review, or withhold qualification sign-off when the evidence demands it - and hold that position under pressure from peers and the CTO alike.

What you’ll be doing:
Mission Assurance
Own the FMEA/FMECA from initial build through qualification -zero unmitigated single-point failures is a CDR entry criterion
Chair the Failure Review Board (FRB) -convene, lead root cause investigation, assess extent of condition, and close with verified corrective action
Define mission success criteria and own fault tree analysis
Safety
Implement and own the system safety program per MIL-STD-882 or program-equivalent standard
Lead hazard analysis (PHA, SHA) and maintain the hazard tracking log through every gate
Manage propulsion, battery, high-voltage, and deployment safety; provide range safety interface for launch operations
Quality Assurance
Exercise independent inspection authority across all program phases
Hold sole NCR disposition authority -Use-As-Is and Repair require MA&Q concurrence regardless of phase
Enforce workmanship standards per IPC-A-610 Class 3; conduct process audits and first article inspections
Issue Standing Disposition Authorizations (SDAs) for recurring Tier 2/3 NCRs; Tier 1 Critical NCRs trigger CTO notification within 4 hours
Reliability Engineering
Own quantitative reliability model per MIL-HDBK-217 or equivalent; track MTBF/MTTR targets against the constellation availability model
Lead reliability growth tracking, redundancy analysis, and reliability predictions correlated with test data at QR
Parts Engineering & Radiation
Maintain the Preferred Parts List (PPL) - sole authority to add or remove parts; no part may fly without PPL approval
Enforce derating compliance at CDR and manage lot acceptance testing
Specify the mission radiation environment (TID, SEE, displacement damage) and track radiation margins for all flight parts
Configuration Management
Chair the production CCB and administer the ECO/ECN process
Maintain as-built configuration records from the MES; execute FCA and PCA before Phase Close Gate
Provide as-built conformance report to the CTO
What you bring to this role:
15+ years of progressive mission assurance, quality engineering, or reliability engineering on flight programs; at least one spacecraft program carried from system requirements through on-orbit operations
Demonstrated record of exercising halt/reject authority or withholding qualification sign-off against schedule and cost pressure you must describe a specific instance. This is the most important qualification for the role
Direct accountability for a flight program's FMEA/FMECA from initial build through qualification, including enforcing zero-unmitigated-SPOF at CDR
Experience designing, implementing, and running a tiered NCR classification and disposition system at production rate, including Use-As-Is and Repair disposition authority
Direct experience chairing or co-chairing a spacecraft Qualification Review and making the independent go/no-go determination
Familiarity with PPL management, derating analysis, lot acceptance testing, and radiation qualification requirements (TID, SEE)
Demonstrated record of building multi-discipline assurance teams spanning all seven functions
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Aerospace, Systems, Electrical Engineering, or related field — or equivalent verifiable experience
Bonus Points for the Following
Direct experience with constellation programs and fleet-wide conformance reporting
Familiarity with SAP (Special Access Program) assurance requirements
Prior experience as CCB chair in a high-rate production environment
Familiarity with CMMI or AS9100 quality management systems in a space or defense manufacturing environment
Range safety certification or prior direct range safety interface experience
Additional Requirements
This is a fast-paced, high-impact environment - flexibility to occasionally work extended hours or weekends during critical periods is expected.
This is a full time, exempt position, based out of our Saratoga office.  The target base pay for this position is $190,000- $225,000annually.  The total compensation packaged will be determined by various factors such as your relevant job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.  
 
We are redefining how satellites are designed, manufactured and used—so we’re looking for candidates with passion, deep knowledge and direct experience on LEO satellite component development, design and in-orbit activities. If that’s your experience – then we’ll be immediately wow-ed.
 
This role requires access to controlled technical data. Under U.S. law (ITAR/EAR), we can only consider U.S. persons (U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, and individuals granted asylum or refugee status). 
 
E-Space is not currently able to provide employment sponsorship for candidates who do not hold work authorization for the location of this role.


Why E-Space is right for you:

As a member of our team, you will play a crucial role in driving our success.  Our team members have a strong sense of dedication and responsibility; this includes a strong commitment to our mission to create an entirely new suite of global capabilities to improve lives, business efficiencies and build a smarter planet. This means that there will be times when extra hours, including nights and weekends, may be needed to meet critical deadlines and mission goals.  In return, we offer a dynamic work environment with opportunities for professional growth and development and the chance to make a meaningful impact in a high-growth industry.  

We want you to make the most of your journey at E-Space. That’s why we support and invest in the physical, emotional and financial well-being of our team members and their families. Some of what you can expect when working at E-Space:

•  An opportunity to really make a difference
•  Sustainability at our core
•  Fair and honest workplace
•  Innovative thinking is encouraged
•  Competitive salaries
•  Continuous learning and development
•  Health and wellness care options
•  Financial solutions for the future 
•  Optional legal services (US only)
•  Paid holidays
•  Paid time off

records.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD


At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Bedrock's technology is scaling rapidly —over the next twelve months, we will rapidly scale our machine count, partners, and sites while also adding net-new machine types and a next-generation platform.  

The Head of Operations Planning & Special Projects owns aligning cross-functionally on an integrated machine plan across types, generations, product lines, partners, sites in order to develop Operational headcount and material plans; ultimately, giving the business a clear view of what's required and by when. 

You'll own the integrated machine plan, scenario planning, cross-functional alignment when constraints arise, building headcount scaling factors and plans, and standing up our early Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process. Reporting to the VP of Operations, you'll be a critical thought partner to the VP and each Operations Lead.


WHAT YOU'LL DO


INTEGRATED PLANNING

 - Own the integrated operations plan covering requirements across all product lines, machines, field headcount, and material readiness.

 - Identify constraints in the plan and build scenarios that drive resolution or acceptable alternatives.

 - Partner with each Operations leader to surface optimizations, risks, and constraints, and develop paths to mitigation.

 - Support senior leadership and board-level decisions with clear, rigorous analysis.

 - Partner with the VP of Operations to define team OKRs, the mechanisms to track them, and routine reporting on critical initiatives.

 - Contribute to the long-term forecast, integrating priorities across multiple teams.

 - Help align data collection needs with operational optimizations to strengthen our data pipelines.


S&OP PROCESS IMPLEMENTATION

 - Partner with Commercial, Finance, Supply Chain, Engineering, and Operations to build stage-appropriate S&OP processes that tee up critical business decisions, surface constraints, and evaluate alternatives.

 - Own the monthly S&OP cycle end to end: forecast development, demand review inputs, forecast analysis, supply plan integration, pre-meeting coordination, and reporting.

 - Forecast demand, assess whether projected supply can meet it, and define key performance metrics such as forecast accuracy and fulfillment rate.

 - Serve as the bridge between business strategy, engineering build plans, finance, and supply chain execution.


PRODUCTION PLANNING COORDINATION

 - Own phase-in / phase-out planning for new machine types, product lines, partners and sites, and hardware generations — including availability, supply constraints, retrofits, and partner transitions.

 - Track lead times and drive alignment on critical decision timelines and order dates.

 - Work with Operations leaders to plan labor availability, using key ratios and operational planning drivers.

 - Partner with Supply Chain and Contract Manufacturing to plan production capacity against demand, consolidate risks, and drive prioritization when supply is constrained.


OPERATIONS INSIGHTS & ANALYTICS

 - Own the development of core operational metrics and routine reporting.

 - Run operational review cadences that drive accountability and bring key insights to the business.

 - Support continuous improvement across Operations through process and data.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - A single, trusted integrated plan that the business uses to make decisions about machines, people, and materials.

 - Constraints surfaced early, with clear scenarios and recommendations — not surprises.

 - A functioning monthly S&OP cadence with consistent participation and clear decisions.

 - Core operational metrics defined, tracked, and reviewed on a regular rhythm.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR


REQUIRED

 - 8–10 years in operations, planning, or program leadership, including 5+ years working with cross-functional teams distributed across sites or regions.

 - Demonstrated ability to influence leaders — aligning cross-functional stakeholders, driving difficult decisions, and managing risk through rapid growth.

 - Track record implementing S&OP or supply-and-demand processes that bring clarity to requirements, decisions, and success criteria.

 - Experience planning and managing hourly / field workforce headcount.

 - Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills; able to turn data into operational decisions.

 - Strong written and verbal communication, including with executives.


PREFERRED

 - Familiarity with autonomy, heavy machinery, and/or the construction industry.

 - Experience standing up supply-and-demand review processes that clarify timelines, requirements, decisions, risks, and solutions.

 - Continuous improvement, Lean, or Six Sigma experience, including standing up an improvement program.


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

As Bedrock scales, the hardest problems are increasingly about coordination: getting the right machines, people, and parts to the right sites at the right time. This role builds the planning backbone that lets every Operations team — and the company — make faster, better decisions with confidence.

Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer

We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic.

Reasonable Accommodations

We want our hiring process to be accessible to everyone. If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, please let your recruiter know so we can support you.

records.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.




ABOUT THIS ROLE



The Director, Commercial Operations will be the operational backbone of Crusoe's Energy Development Group. This person owns the analytical frameworks, pipeline processes, and team capabilities that allow Crusoe to evaluate and advance land and power opportunities at speed and at scale. From complex financial modeling and market analysis to pipeline integrity and board-level reporting, this role ensures the BD team operates with precision and strategic clarity.

This is a leadership-first, analytically grounded role. The ideal candidate brings deep experience in energy project finance or development, a track record of building and mentoring high-performing analyst teams, and the process orientation to continuously raise the quality bar on how Crusoe evaluates and advances opportunities. You will work closely with senior leadership across Energy Development, Real Estate, Finance, Cloud, Energy Innovation, Design / Engineering, Pre-Construction, and Construction teams and will be a key contributor to the operational health of Crusoe's project pipeline.




WHAT YOU'LL BE WORKING ON



 - Overseeing a team of Energy Development Analysts, setting the standard for analytical rigor, process discipline, and professional growth

 - Owning the development and refinement of economic models that underpin power origination and data center site pricing decisions

 - Driving continuous improvement of due diligence workflows, pipeline management processes, and reporting mechanisms across the Energy Development team

 - Overseeing the integrity and accuracy of Crusoe's data center opportunity pipeline, ensuring leadership has a reliable, real-time view of the project portfolio

 - Supervising the creation of board-level presentations, project approval materials, and executive communications that translate analytical complexity into clear strategic recommendations

 - Tracking and synthesizing hyperscaler activity, regulatory developments, and domestic energy infrastructure trends to surface actionable intelligence for the team

 - Supporting cross-functional collaboration between Energy Development and the Real Estate, Finance, Cloud, Energy Innovation, Design / Engineering, Pre-Construction, and Construction teams to move projects efficiently through the development pipeline






CORE RESPONSIBILITIES



Lead and enable the Energy Development Analyst team

 - Provide hands-on guidance on financial modeling, market analysis, and project evaluation

Drive analytical quality and strategic relevance

 - Oversee the development of detailed economic models for new large-scale land and power opportunities and data center site power pricing

 - Ensure analyses of energy development potential and economics are accurate, rigorous, and decision-ready

 - Guide the team in leveraging internal data analytics tools and external market intelligence to identify and vet opportunities

Own pipeline management and process improvement

 - Drive continuous improvement of business operations processes within the Energy Development team, including project management, due diligence workflows, and reporting mechanisms

 - Maintain the integrity of Crusoe's data center opportunity pipeline, ensuring data accuracy and timely updates

 - Develop and implement best practices for tracking key pipeline metrics and project statuses

Deliver executive-ready reporting and communications

 - Supervise the creation and delivery of board-level presentations, project approval materials, and ad hoc reports for senior management

 - Ensure all communications clearly articulate analytical findings, strategic implications, and support for business decisions

Support cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder engagement

 - Facilitate effective communication between the Energy Development team and the Real Estate, Finance, Cloud, Energy Innovation, Design / Engineering, Pre-Construction, and Construction teams

 - Support the team in communications with external stakeholders including developers, IPPs, and potential partners

Monitor market and regulatory intelligence

 - Oversee tracking and analysis of hyperscaler and co-located data center activity, regulatory changes in the energy sector, and domestic energy infrastructure investments

 - Ensure the team synthesizes this information to identify potential impacts and opportunities for Crusoe




QUALIFICATIONS

Required

 - 7+ years of progressive experience in consulting, project finance, investment banking, private equity, energy development, or business operations, with significant focus on the energy sector (renewables, conventional power, or oil & gas)

 - 3+ years of experience in a managerial or team leadership role, with a demonstrated ability to mentor and develop direct reports

 - Deep understanding of energy markets, project economics, and financial modeling

 - Exceptional analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills

 - Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Google Suite; experience with pipeline management systems

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to distill complex analytical and commercial content into clear, executive-ready recommendations

 - Demonstrated ability to build and improve operational processes in a fast-moving, high-ambiguity environment

 - Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field



Preferred

 - MBA or relevant advanced degree

 - Experience with data center infrastructure, HPC, or large-scale power-consuming industries

 - Familiarity with power purchase agreements, offtake structures, and the commercial frameworks that govern energy project development

 - Experience with or strong aptitude for leveraging AI-based tools to drive analytical efficiency and output quality

 - Ability to travel domestically as required (estimated <20%)



Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location



Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $180,000 -$220,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.
