Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. records.title: VP Production, Connected Warfare
records.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE ROLE 
The Vice President, Production, Connected Warfare provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for all production activities within Anduril's Connected Warfare organization. Connected Warfare builds the compute, comms, and infrastructure products that modern defense programs rely on a business growing toward multi-billion-dollar scale, producing integrated hardware and software products at real volume. Encompassing production planning, supply chain, manufacturing engineering, and manufacturing operations, this role will be responsible for production across multiple business lines and multiple facilities. The VP orchestrates a portfolio of production programs, making resource allocation tradeoffs, and setting the Connected Warfare production strategy. This executive is responsible for driving operational excellence and production efficiency in the near term and building the production capabilities necessary to support Connected Warfare's and the company's long-term business objectives . 


 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 

 
 Establish and provide strategic and operational leadership across multiple production facilities - ensuring consistency in quality, cost, and delivery performance across geographies

 Lead and build the production capabilities of a portfolio of products, balancing investment, capacity, and talent allocation across product lines and production programs

 Partner with R&D, sales, and engineering teams to lead new product introduction efforts across multiple emerging product lines, developing from scratch the production lines and processes necessary to meet our customers’ requirements

 Drive division-level production strategy including facility footprint decisions, make-vs-buy analyses, capital deployment planning, and workforce sizing aligned to multi-year business forecasts. 

 Establish the operational excellence framework and continuous improvement culture across the division, leveraging lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or similar methodologies to reduce costs, improve yields, and increase throughput

 Establish and monitor KPIs across safety, quality, delivery, schedule, and cost to ensure performance targets are met across multiple production sites, including international expansions

 Build and develop a high-performing production organization through talent development and a strong culture of accountability

 Support capital planning, budgeting, and resource allocation for production functions across the division

 Ensure compliance with all regulatory, environmental, health, and safety requirements

 Lead capacity planning and footprint strategy, including evaluation of new facilities and/or manufacturing technologies

 Serve as a member of the division's senior leadership team, contributing to division and corporate strategic planning; represent the production organization in executive, customer, and investor contexts as appropriate

 Collaborate in a matrix environment with strong relationships and influence ability across multiple stakeholders across the business

 Lead workforce and location strategy, including labor market analysis, site selection criteria, and workforce sizing, to support new line stand-ups and geographic expansion

 
 QUALIFICATIONS 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Operations Management, or a related field; MBA or advanced degree preferred

 15+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, with at least 7-10 years in a senior or executive role overseeing organizations of 500+ employees; experience in a high- or hyper-growth environment

 Proven track record of leading large, complex manufacturing operations across multiple sites or locations

 Experience managing simultaneous product ramps across multiple facilities and scaling international manufacturing operations required

 Experience across all 5 pillars of production: production planning, supply chain, manufacturing engineering, operations, and quality

 Demonstrated ability to set and scale an operational excellence framework across a division, with deep expertise in lean manufacturing and continuous improvement

 Prior experience managing large budgets in the hundreds of millions of dollars and capital programs

 Excellent leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills

 Experience in regulated industries (e.g., defense, automotive, aerospace, medical devices) a plus

 Direct P&L ownership in a production environment with demonstrated ability to manage financial performance at division scale

 Executive presence and sophisticated communication skills; proven ability to influence C-suite stakeholders, represent the production function externally, and shape corporate-level strategy

 
  
 US Salary Range
 $252,000 — $382,000 USD 


 The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:   

  

 Benefits 

 At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.  For more information, Explore Our Benefits . 

  

 
 Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams 

 Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.



 
 To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

 
 
 No Financial Requests:  Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.



 Please always verify communications: 
 
 Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

 Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . 

 


 
 Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:  If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.



 
 What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:  Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to  contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.



 


  

 Data Privacy 

 To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ .   

  

 By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

records.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Director of Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) to join our team.

 Position Description 

 Oklo Isotopes is building scalable U.S. radioisotope production capabilities in facilities dedicated to producing essential isotopes for healthcare, space, industry, research, and defense applications. Oklo’s isotope operations include the production and processing of medically and industrially important radioisotopes using advanced radiochemical processes, hot cells, gloveboxes, and specialized nuclear facilities.

 We are seeking a Director of Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls (CMC) to lead the radiochemistry and CMC organization supporting Oklo’s isotope production programs, initially focused on Lu-177 production and Am-241 and Ra-226 processing for medical, industrial, and other applications.

 The Director will lead radiochemical process development and control, technology transfer, analytical strategy, process optimization, troubleshooting, validation support, and process lifecycle management, while building and managing a multidisciplinary radiochemistry team.

 The successful candidate will develop rigorous, scalable processes from development through commissioning and routine manufacturing. The role requires deep radiochemistry and isotope-processing expertise, strong technical and team leadership, and experience in nuclear, radiological, quality, and cGMP environments.

 The Director will collaborate across Manufacturing, Facility Operations, Quality, Regulatory, Radiation Safety, Engineering, and Supply Chain to establish safe, compliant, reliable, and scalable isotope production.

 This is a on-site position located in Austin, Texas.

 Specific responsibilities may include: 

 
 Lead the CMC and radiochemistry organization for isotope process development, implementation, technical support, and lifecycle management.

 Lead Lu-177 production and Am-241 and Ra-226 processing, including dissolution, separation, purification, recovery, impurity control, characterization, and waste minimization.

 Establish the technical basis for manufacturing processes, including process flows, material balances, critical parameters, operating ranges, specifications, and controls.

 Lead development, scale-up, optimization, and implementation of radiochemical processes in hot cells, gloveboxes, and laboratory or remote systems.

 Lead technology transfer and manufacturing readiness, including processes, equipment, analytics, procedures, training, and documentation.

 Establish and maintain the cGMP technical framework, including process characterization, validation, continued verification, change control, deviations, investigations, and continuous improvement.

 Own the analytical strategy for products, intermediates, impurities, waste streams, and process performance.

 Serve as the senior technical authority for process troubleshooting and optimization, focused on yield, purity, recovery, reliability, cycle time, waste, dose, and capacity.

 Support equipment design, commissioning, qualification, startup, and operational readiness with Manufacturing, Operations, Engineering, Quality, Radiation Safety, Regulatory, and Supply Chain.

 Build, mentor, and manage the radiochemistry team; establish technical standards, procedures, training, and documentation; and promote safety, quality, rigor, and operational excellence.

 Support regulatory activities, audits, inspections, and development of new isotope products, processes, technologies, and capabilities.

 
 Minimum Qualifications: 

 
 Masters in Radiochemistry, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, or a closely related technical discipline.

 10+ years of progressively responsible experience in radiochemistry, isotope production, radiochemical processing, nuclear chemical operations, pharmaceutical/radiopharmaceutical manufacturing, or a closely related field.

 Experience with cGMP manufacturing (US and EU requirements), particularly radiopharmaceuticals, medical isotopes, APIs, radioactive starting materials, or other regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing.

 Experience with CMC development, process characterization, technology transfer, process validation, continued process verification, and manufacturing science and technology (MS&T).

 Direct experience with Lu-177 production, lanthanide separations, target dissolution, radionuclide purification, or medical-isotope manufacturing.

 Demonstrated experience leading technical teams responsible for complex chemical, radiochemical, or manufacturing processes.

 Strong technical background in radiochemical separations, purification, radioactive-material handling, analytical chemistry, and process development.

 Demonstrated experience translating laboratory or development processes into reliable manufacturing operations.

 Experience with process development, scale-up, process optimization, technology transfer, troubleshooting, and technical lifecycle management.

 Experience working in highly regulated environments requiring disciplined procedures, documentation, configuration control, and quality systems.

 Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical investigations and make sound decisions using scientific and engineering data.

 Experience developing technical procedures, specifications, reports, process documentation, and training materials.

 Strong leadership, communication, technical writing, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

 Demonstrated ability to collaborate across Manufacturing, Operations, Engineering, Quality, Regulatory, Radiation Safety, and other multidisciplinary organizations.

 Experience with various regulatory regimes affecting isotope production and processing (FDA, NRC, DOE, etc.) regulatory frameworks relevant to radioactive-material and isotope manufacturing.

 
 Bonus Qualifications: 

 
 Passionate about unleashing beneficial isotopes and building domestic isotope-production capabilities.

 A strong technical leader who can maintain scientific rigor while moving programs rapidly toward manufacturing.

 Committed to nuclear safety culture, product quality, procedural compliance, and operational excellence.

 Capable of moving comfortably between detailed radiochemical problems and broader program and organizational decisions.

 Able to develop people and build a high-performing technical organization.

 Comfortable making decisions in technically complex environments where complete information may not always be available.

 Effective at translating scientific development into practical, repeatable manufacturing processes.

 Collaborative and able to work across Manufacturing, Facility Operations, Quality, Regulatory, Engineering, Radiation Safety, and Supply Chain.

 Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment.

 Willing to challenge established approaches and develop novel solutions to difficult isotope-production problems.

 An excellent technical communicator capable of communicating complex chemistry and manufacturing issues clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.

 Detail-oriented and disciplined about technical documentation, configuration control, quality, and follow-through.

 Able to balance near-term production needs with long-term process robustness and manufacturing scalability.

 
 Who you are: 

 A startup person : You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

 Motivated : You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

 A team-player : Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

 An excellent communicator : We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

 Creative : Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

 Detail-oriented : This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

  

 About Oklo travel requirements: 

 Oklo requires remote employees to travel to headquarters (Santa Clara, CA) twice a quarter annually, based on business or team needs, including attendance at team meetings, off-sites, and other company events or gatherings. For the first two weeks of onboarding, employees are required to be in person at headquarters in Santa Clara, CA.

  

 About Oklo compensation: 

 Salary: $170,000-$250,000

 Oklo offers flexible time off, equity, bonuses, competitive pay, 401(k), health insurance (with employer contribution), HSA, FSA, flexible work hours, wellness credits, and other benefits.

 This position may involve access to information subject to U.S. export control laws. Only applicants who meet the definition of a U.S. person under applicable laws may be eligible.

 
 About Oklo Inc.: Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories.

 #CHOP: Oklo’s Values 
 Collaboration : We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes.
 Humility : We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition.
 Ownership : We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through  to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy.
 Pathfinding : We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity.
 Candidates should be aware that employment may be contingent upon successful completion of a drug screening, and employees may be subject to drug testing at any time in accordance with company policy and applicable laws. 

 Recruitment Fraud Disclaimer 

 Oklo is aware of recent recruitment fraud attempts targeting job seekers. Please be cautious of anyone claiming to represent Oklo who does not contact you from an official Oklo email address. 

 All legitimate communications from our recruiting team— including application updates, interview requests, and job offers — will come exclusively from an @oklo.com email. Oklo will never ask for sensitive personal information, payments, or account credentials during the hiring process. 

 If you receive suspicious outreach or have concerns about the authenticity of any communication claiming to be from Oklo, please contact us through the official channels listed on our website.

Thank you for your interest in Oklo! We are searching for a Plant Manager to join our team.

 This position will be on-site at the Aurora facility at Idaho National Laboratory in Idaho. 

 Position Description 

 Oklo is developing its Aurora powerhouse at Idaho National Laboratory. The Plant Manager will coordinate the people, infrastructure, work processes, and site interfaces needed to support safe and effective facility readiness and operations.

 The Plant Manager is responsible for day-to-day facility operations and the safe, reliable, and efficient execution of maintenance, work control, logistics, and administrative activities. The manager coordinates with accountable program owners for industrial and nuclear safety, radiation protection, security, environmental requirements, and emergency preparedness. This role provides leadership across multidisciplinary teams working in a highly regulated environment.

 The Plant Manager will oversee facility readiness, site infrastructure, maintenance coordination, contractor activities, logistics, and facility support functions. The role will establish practical processes, resolve site issues, support readiness, and improve facility performance as the Aurora program advances.

 The Plant Manager will work closely with Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, Radiation Protection, Safety, Security, Emergency Preparedness, Quality, site services, contractors, program leadership, and Idaho National Laboratory organizations.

 Specific responsibilities may include: 

 
 Lead and coordinate day-to-day on-site facility operations in accordance with approved procedures, site requirements, and applicable regulatory expectations.

 Promote operational discipline, procedural compliance, safety culture, accountability, and continuous improvement across facility activities.

records.title: Director of Site Operations
records.description:
About the Company 

 We are a renewable energy and ocean technology company committed to rapidly developing and deploying technologies that will ensure a sustainable future for Earth by unlocking the vast energy potential of its oceans. Our focus is on capturing civilizational levels of ultra-low-cost renewable energy for applications including computing and affordable renewable fuels delivered to shore.

 The company is a public benefit corporation headquartered in Portland, Oregon, and backed by leading venture capitalists, philanthropic investors, university endowments, and private investment offices. We operate as an idea meritocracy in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis.

 Our staff have worked at organizations such as SpaceX, Blue Origin, Boeing, Tesla, Apple, Virgin Orbit, Astra, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, New Relic, Bridgewater, Raytheon, Disney Imagineering, and the US Army and Air Force, as well as research universities, startups, and small companies across a range of industries.

 About the Job 

 Our core technology is the node, a device that produces energy in the ocean’s harshest conditions for years at a time without human maintenance or intervention.

 We are seeking a Director of Site Operations to lead the day-to-day operational performance of Panthalassa’s regional facilities and build the systems that will support their growth. The Director will have direct responsibility for our headquarter and R&D campus, our Portland headquarters and primary hub for R&D, engineering, prototyping, and business operations, while leading Site Operations Managers at our other locations. Each site should have clear operational ownership, consistent support, and a leader who understands what is happening on the ground.

 You will set and sustain a high standard for how our sites are maintained, organized, and made ready for work. You will make sure that standard is reflected in daily conditions and practices across locations, and that site leaders address issues promptly and consistently. You will use sound judgment when site conditions or practices create safety, reliability, or operational concerns, working with the relevant functional leaders to resolve them and prevent recurrence.

 You will build the operating model behind that performance: clear roles and decision paths, useful site routines, responsive services, effective vendor relationships, and ways to identify and resolve recurring problems. You will keep a close view of site needs and emerging constraints, then turn what you learn into practical improvements that make operations more consistent and responsive as Panthalassa grows.

 This role connects functional expertise to local execution. You will work closely with Facilities Engineering, Workplace Experience, EHS, Security, Real Estate, IT, Capital Delivery, Manufacturing, R&D, and other teams to understand upcoming needs, coordinate work that affects a site, and ensure local priorities and constraints are addressed. Those teams retain ownership of their technical and professional standards; Site Operations ensures their work comes together effectively at each location.

 This is a systems-building and leadership role. You will remain closely involved in Banfield while building and developing Site Operations Managers who can lead their locations with clear accountability. Your success will show in sites that are consistently well-run, responsive to the people who use them, and ready to support Panthalassa’s changing work.

 Candidates should have strong interpersonal skills and be able to thrive in a creative, scrappy, and collaborative environment in which the best ideas change the company’s direction on a regular basis.

 Responsibilities 

 Regional Site Operations Leadership 

 
 Lead Site Operations across Panthalassa’s regional facilities, with direct responsibility for the corporate campus and leader and mentorship of Site Operations Managers at other locations.

 Hire, develop, and manage a high-performing Site Operations team with clear ownership, priorities, and expectations.

 Establish consistent operating standards, service levels, and expectations across sites while accounting for the unique needs of each location.

 Maintain visibility into major activities, constraints, and risks across the regional portfolio and ensure resources are aligned with business priorities.

 Serve as the escalation point for significant site issues, operational conflicts, and service gaps.

 Maintain hands-on involvement at the main corporate campus facilities while developing a regional operating model that does not depend on the Director personally solving every problem.

 
 Cross-Functional Operations & Planning 

 
 Serve as a senior operational partner to Engineering, Manufacturing, R&D, Facilities Engineering, EHS, Security, IT, Real Estate, and other functions.

 Build strong relationships with functional leaders to understand upcoming work, growth plans, and operational requirements.

 Ensure Site Operations Managers are coordinating activities, shared resources, projects, moves, outages, deliveries, and other work that may affect multiple teams.

 Identify operational impacts and resource constraints before they affect execution and bring together the appropriate teams to resolve them.

 Translate company growth and changing operational requirements into site capabilities, staffing, services, and infrastructure needs.

 
 Systems & Operational Excellence 

 
 Build scalable systems, processes, and operating standards that make Panthalassa facilities high-performing, consistent, and turnkey.

 Develop common operating rhythms, escalation paths, service models, and KPIs across sites.

 Identify recurring operational friction and drive solutions that address root causes rather than repeated one-off fixes.

 Implement tools, automation, vendors, and processes that improve visibility, coordination, service quality, and efficiency.

 Establish mechanisms for sharing best practices and lessons learned between sites.

 Continuously evaluate whether current operating systems can support the next stage of company growth and evolve them before they become constraints.

 
 Site Services, Vendors & Resources 

 
 Own the strategy for the vendors and services that support site operations, including janitorial, PPE, uniforms/laundry, furniture, waste, workplace supplies, fleet, logistics, and other shared services.

 Establish regional vendor strategies and standards while supporting Site Operations Managers in local execution.

 Develop scalable inventory, procurement, and replenishment strategies for operational supplies and shared resources.

 Ensure workplace readiness along with Workplace Experience on space planning, employee accommodations, furniture, and team moves.

 Partner with EHS, Security, Facilities Engineering, Real Estate, and property management on safety, security, utilities, wastewater, landlord, and other site requirements.

 
 Budget, Team & Growth Planning 

 
 Develop and own the regional Site Operations budget, including annual planning, forecasting, and ongoing management.

 Establish site-level budgets and accountability while maintaining visibility into regional spending and future requirements.

 Build business cases for staffing, vendors, tools, services, and operational investments.

 Develop staffing and service models that scale with headcount, facility growth, and increasing operational complexity.

 Identify opportunities to improve cost and operational efficiency without compromising safety, reliability, service quality, or employee productivity.

 
 Required Qualifications 

 
 8+ years of experience in site operations, facilities operations, industrial operations, workplace operations, or a related field, including experience leading teams.

 Experience supporting industrial, engineering, manufacturing, laboratory, R&D, or similarly complex environments.

 Demonstrated ability to build and scale operational systems, teams, processes, and service models.

 Experience managing operations across multiple facilities, sites, or complex operating environments.

 Strong systems thinking and the ability to understand how people, facilities, services, resources, and business activities interact.

 Experience managing significant operating budgets, vendors, procurement, and operational services.

 Strong people leadership with experience developing managers and building effective teams.

 Excellent cross-functional communication and the ability to influence and coordinate across technical and operational organizations.

 Strong judgment with the ability to balance immediate operational needs against long-term scalability.

 Comfortable operating at both strategic and tactical levels in a fast-changing environment.

 
 Desired Qualifications 

 
 Experience in a fast-growing startup or scale-up environment.

 Experience building a regional or multi-site operations function.

 Experience supporting headquarters, R&D campuses, manufacturing facilities, or mixed office/industrial environments.

 Familiarity with industrial safety and commercial building operations.

 Experience developing operational KPIs, service standards, and vendor strategies across multiple sites.

 Experience supporting significant facility growth, new site launches, or organizational scaling.

 
 The above qualifications are desired, not required. We encourage you to apply if you are a strong candidate with only some of the desired skills and experience listed.

 Additional Requirements 

 
 This is an on-site leadership role based primarily at the main corporate campus.

 Regular travel between Panthalassa’s regional locations is required.

 Ability to move regularly throughout office, lab, shop, and industrial environments.

 Intermittent availability outside normal business hours may be required for significant site issues or operational needs.

 Travel to vendors and test sites as needed

 Intermittently able to work longer hours and weekends to support critical needs. While we expect a lot of each other, we also offer a high degree of autonomy and work-life balance, including flexible PTO and flexible working hours.

 
 Compensation and Benefits 

 If hired for this full-time role, you will receive:

 
 Cash compensation of $190,000–$225,000.

 Equity in the company. We’re all owners and if we’re successful, this equity should be far and away the most valuable component of your compensation.

 A benefits package that helps you take care of yourself and your family, including:
 
 Flexible paid time off

 Health insurance (the company pays 100% of gold-level PPO plan for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents)

 Dental insurance (the company pays 100% for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents)

 Vision insurance (the company pays 100% for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents)

 Disability insurance (the company pays 100% for a policy to provide long-term financial support if you become disabled)

 Ability to contribute to tax-advantaged accounts, including 401(k), health FSA, and dependent care FSA

 


 Relocation assistance to facilitate your move to Portland (if needed).

 
 Location 

 This is an on-site position. Our offices, lab, and shop are located in Portland, Oregon.

The Director will have direct responsibility for our headquarter and R&D campus, our Portland headquarters and primary hub for R&D, engineering, prototyping, and business operations, while leading Site Operations Managers at our other locations.
Each site should have clear operational ownership, consistent support, and a leader who understands what is happening on the ground.

records.description:
Position Summary 

 The Director of Analytical Development & Quality Control will provide strategic and operational leadership for analytical development, characterization, method validation, transfer, and quality control activities supporting a growing pipeline of small molecule Oral Solid Dose (OSD) and parenteral Drug Product programs.  The incumbent will have deep experience in analytical activities required to support early-stage to late-stage oral solid dose and parenteral drug products. Additional experience in antibody/ADC manufacturing-focused analytical activities is desirable. This individual will be responsible for operating in a 100% outsourced environment to establish and manage phase-appropriate analytical strategies from preclinical through commercialization, overseeing external analytical operations, and ensuring compliance with global regulatory expectations and GMP requirements for assigned programs.

 As a key member of the Technical Operations team, the Director will collaborate cross-functionally with Medicinal Chemistry, Toxicology, Clinical Pharmacology, Drug Substance, Drug Product, ADC production, Regulatory Affairs, Quality Assurance, and external CDMOs/CRO/consultants to advance programs efficiently through development milestones while building scalable analytical and quality control capabilities for a rapidly growing organization.

  

 Key Responsibilities 

 Analytical Development Leadership 

 
 Lead, develop and execute phase-appropriate analytical method development and testing strategies and activities supporting Drug Product development, with an emphasis on small-molecule OSD and large-molecule parenteral Drug Product analytical method development and testing for assigned programs, including:

 
 Phase-appropriate small molecule oral solid dose drug product method development and testing (tablets, capsules, gelcaps)

 Phase-appropriate method development supporting antibody manufacture, ADC conjugation, and parenteral drug product manufacture.

 
 Provide technical oversight for development, qualification, validation, and lifecycle management of analytical methods.

 Ensure analytical methods support process development, formulation development, manufacturing, release testing, and regulatory submissions.

 Depending on experience, incumbent may serve as the company's analytical subject matter expert for ADC development.

 
 Support characterization of monoclonal antibodies, cytotoxic payloads, linkers, conjugates, and related impurities.

 Guide implementation and interpretation of advanced analytical techniques such as:  HPLC, UPLC, LC-MS, HRMS, SEC, CE-SDS, icIEF, HIC, ELISA, and bioassays.

 Collaborate with external CDMOs and internal process development teams to define CQAs and control strategies for ADC products.

 
 
 Quality Control Oversight 

 
 Establish and lead QC strategies across clinical manufacturing operations for assigned programs.

 Oversee external GMP testing activities including raw materials, IPCs, release testing and stability programs.

 Ensure timely release and disposition support for clinical materials.

 Manage investigations involving OOS, OOT, deviations, and laboratory events.

 
 Regulatory and Quality Support 

 
 Author and review analytical sections of regulatory submissions including: INDs, IMPDs, BLAs, NDAs, and CTAs for assigned programs.

 Ensure analytical approaches align with ICH, FDA, EMA, and other global regulatory expectations.

 Support establishment of specifications and analytical control strategies throughout the product lifecycle.

 May participate in regulatory agency interactions and inspections.

 Ensure compliance with cGMP, GLP, GCP, and data integrity requirements.

 Partner closely with Quality Assurance to maintain inspection readiness.

 Support audits of contract testing laboratories and manufacturing partners.

 
 External Partner Management 

 
 Manage relationships with contract laboratories and CDMOs.

 Oversee method transfers, validation activities, and technical governance of external laboratories.

 Establish performance metrics and ensure delivery against development and manufacturing timelines.

 Evaluate/implement new technologies/outsourced capabilities as needed.

 
  

 Required Qualifications 

 Education 

 
 Ph.D./MS in Analytical Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Chemical Engineering, or related scientific discipline preferred.

 
 Experience 

 
 12+ years (Ph.D.)15+ years (MS) of progressive pharmaceutical or biotechnology analytical development experience.

  Demonstrated deep experience in analytical development activities supporting Drug Product development and manufacturing with emphases on oral solid dose, parenteral, and pediatric formulations.

 Proven track record advancing products from early development through late-stage clinical development and/or commercialization.

 Demonstrated success working with CDMOs and global development partners.

 Additional experience in development and implementation of analytical methods to support antibody/ADC manufacturing is preferred.

 
 Technical Expertise 

 Strong working knowledge of:

 
 Analytical method development and validation

 Stability programs and specification setting

 Quality control laboratory operations

 GMP analytical testing

 Oral solid dose characterization and phase-appropriate method development, including discriminatory dissolution method development

 ADC analytical characterization

 Experience with Biologics testing methodologies preferred

 ICH Q1, Q2, Q3, Q6, Q7, Q8, Q9, Q10, and Q14 guidance

 Regulatory submissions and health authority interactions

 
 Leadership Competencies 

 
 Strategic thinker with strong business and scientific acumen.

 Excellent project management and organizational skills.

 Strong communication and influence skills across scientific, quality, regulatory, and program teams

 Ability to travel (20%) to CDMO domestic and international sites.

 Fluency with standard computer software packages (MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Project), iStability, and JMP (or similar statistical tools).

 High level of personal integrity, commitment to excellence and to our patients.

 Experience in developing and commercializing drugs for oncology is preferred.

 
 This position is classified as exempt. The anticipated annual base salary range for candidates who will work in Watertown is $193,877 to $232,875. The final base salary offered to the successful candidate will be dependent upon several factors that may include but are not limited to the type and length of experience within the job, and other factors. Treeline Biosciences is a multi-state employer, and this salary range may not reflect positions that work in other cities or states. 

   

 Recruitment fraud statement 

 Please be aware of recruitment fraud and related job scams, where scammers present themselves as recruiters but are seeking to steal money or personal information. Keep the following in mind to protect yourself: 

 
 Treeline Biosciences will never ask for money from you as part of our recruitment process. Do not provide bank details or pay somebody for the promise of a job at Treeline. 

 We do not conduct interviews through RingCentral, Skype or Telegram. 

 Our job openings are first posted to treeline.bio/careers. If you locate a listing for a Treeline job on another site, please ensure it is also posted on our careers website. 

 You can find more information about job scams at consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams. 

 To report job scams, head to ReportFraud.ftc.gov. 

 Notice to Search Firms/Third-Party Recruitment Agencies (Recruiters)

 The Human Resources team manages the recruitment and employment process for Treeline Biosciences. To protect the interests of all parties involved, Treeline Biosciences will only accept resumes from a recruiter if an executed search agreement directed to the particular position or positions is in place at the start of the recruitment effort. Unsolicited resumes sent to Treeline Biosciences from recruiters do not constitute any type of relationship between the recruiter and Treeline Biosciences and do not obligate Treeline Biosciences in any way to pay fees should we hire from those resumes. Recruiters are requested not to contact or present candidates directly to our hiring manager or employees.

records.title: Head of Company Operations
records.description:
About Tutor
We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.
Tutor Intelligence is changing that.
Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.
Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.
Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

The Role
Tutor is hiring a Head of Company Operations to lead cross-functional operations at the leading robotics research and deployment company. The scope is massive and new: every domain of our work, from research and engineering to manufacturing, solutions, sales, and finance, through a period of rapid commercial growth as we take Cassie and Sonny into new workflows, sites, and markets. You will own how the company operates: one clear plan the whole company works toward, and the execution and change it takes to get there.
Strategic intent at Tutor comes from everywhere: the founders, the leaders of each function, and the people closest to the work. You will pull it together into one coherent plan with goals the whole company believes in, keep it current as priorities shift, and make sure it gets done. When something gets stuck between teams, you make the call and drive it to resolution. When the company needs a big change, like entering a new market, standing up a new site, or reshaping how teams work, you make the case and lead it through.
You report to the CEO, sit on the leadership team, and own the operating plan we take to our board. You work as a peer to the leaders who run each function: you set goals with each of them, own the scorecard the company runs on, and have a formal say in how those leaders are evaluated. We are looking for an operator who has owned company outcomes at a scaling company: someone who has run the operating rhythm, understands how revenue and finance fit together, and is as comfortable on the factory floor as in a board planning meeting.
What you'll own
Own the plan: Continuously pull together what the founders, functional leaders, and teams are working on and seeing into one coherent plan, with company and team OKRs that leaders agree to, believe in, and execute against
Make sure it happens: Own execution against the plan across every function, from product launches and production ramps to fleet growth and hiring, and catch slips early enough to recover
Fix what's stuck: Take the highest-stakes problems that span functions, drive them to resolution, and hand each one back to the team that owns it with a fix so it does not come back
Make the calls between functions: Own the operating tradeoffs across functions, from sequencing to resourcing within the plan, so decisions get made where the work happens
Lead big changes: See where the company needs to change to hit bigger goals, make the case, and lead it through, whether that's entering a new market, standing up a new site, integrating an acquisition, or reshaping how teams work
Run the operating rhythm: Own the planning cycle and the annual operating plan with Finance, and the business reviews and scorecard the leadership team works from
Build the data and tools: Over time, build one trusted source for company metrics and the tooling that runs the operating rhythm, working with our internal tooling engineers
Requirements
You have owned the operating rhythm and its outcomes at a scaling company: quarterly planning, business reviews, scorecards, and the annual plan alongside Finance
You have held a director- or VP-level operating role at a company scaling past ~150 people
You understand how revenue and finance work: pipeline and forecast, bookings and revenue, budgets and actuals, unit economics, and how a sales forecast becomes a build plan and a hiring plan
You have taken scattered, shifting direction and turned it into goals a leadership team signed up for and hit
You have led peers and their teams through hard cross-functional work, and earned their trust
You have led a major company change end to end, such as a launch, an integration, or a reorg, and handled the people side well
You can follow a technical problem well enough to unblock it and know who should make the call, without being an engineer
You are fluent with data: you define good metrics, read SQL and dashboards, and notice when numbers disagree
You have a bias to action and high intensity, and you lead from where the work happens, from the factory floor to a customer site
You make operating calls with confidence, own the results, and know which questions belong with the CEO
Helpful, but not required:
Experience at a company that builds physical products: hardware, robotics, manufacturing, or field operations
Experience building something from scratch, as a founder or as the first person in a function
Experience building analytics, business operations, or internal tooling
What success looks like
The company and each function start the quarter with clear, measurable goals that leaders agree to; changes in direction are made explicitly, with owners and plans updated.
Commitments across product launches, production ramps, fleet growth, and hiring are tracked throughout the quarter; risks surface early with recovery plans.
Cross-functional operating decisions are made promptly within the plan, with only true strategy questions escalated to the CEO.
The highest-priority cross-functional problems are resolved with a clear functional owner and a system fix, so the same fires are less likely to return.
Leaders use one trusted scorecard to run business reviews, and planning cycles land on time with less manual effort spent assembling status.
Major changes land on plan, with clear communication and the people affected treated well.
Why Tutor?
Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.
Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.
Benefits
We take care of our team so they can do their best work. At Tutor, you’ll get:
Fully employer-covered health insurance, so you’re protected without the premium.
A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future.
Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year.
As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.
Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

records.title: Head of Technical Operations (Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Field)

postedPay.title: Head of Technical Operations (Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Field)

records.description:
About Tutor
We believe robots should be the next chapter in making physical labor safer and more affordable. But, nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t have a single robot. Tutor Intelligence is changing that.
We build robots that go straight into real factories and warehouses, to do real work, with real impact. Our robot Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Our robot Sonny does handwork, using two arms to achieve human-like dexterity in picking and packing. Every robot learns on the job, and each one we deploy makes the next one more capable, more affordable, and faster to put to work.
Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, we do it all in-house: the robotics hardware, the machine learning, and the field deployment and service. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.
Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.
Why Tutor?
Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.
Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.
The Role
Tutor is hiring a Head of Technical Operations. This person owns manufacturing, supply chain, quality, field service, and robot operations, and reports to the CTO.
We build hundreds of robots a year today and need to build a lot more. You will own how we get there, including the teams, the suppliers, and the facilities, and you will work closely with engineering along the way.
We want someone who has already run production at scale and knows what goes wrong.

Requirements
You have run manufacturing or operations at a company that builds complex hardware in volume
You have built an operations function and hired the people who run it
You have been responsible for a fleet of products in the field, including service and support
You can set targets and hire well
You are comfortable on a factory floor
Nice to haves
Robotics, or other products that combine hardware and software
Experience with contract manufacturers
Experience with quality systems
Benefits
Fully employer-covered health insurance , so you’re protected without the premium.
A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future.
Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year.
Compensation
The base salary range for this role is $250,000 to $350,000, depending on experience.
As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.
Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

records.title: Vice President of Quality
records.description:
We are partnering with a leading global prestige beauty and skincare company to identify a
**Vice President of Quality**
to lead its North American Quality organization.

This is a high-impact executive leadership opportunity for a commercially minded quality professional who can connect quality, regulatory compliance, manufacturing excellence, and business performance within a complex, global organization.

The successful candidate will oversee Quality across North American manufacturing and distribution operations, providing leadership to a network of internal manufacturing operations and external manufacturing partners across multiple continents.

**About The Opportunity**

Reporting into senior global leadership, the Vice President of Quality will lead an organization of approximately 100 professionals, with four Directors reporting directly into the role.

The scope encompasses contract manufacturing quality, factory quality (QA, QC, laboratories, and Quality Management Systems), and quality assurance across North America, while providing technical quality leadership and guidance to teams in Canada and Brazil.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Lead the North American Quality organization:**
 Provide strategic direction and leadership across manufacturing, quality assurance, quality control, laboratories, and quality systems.
* **Act as the business voice of Quality:**
 Partner with commercial, brand, manufacturing, and executive stakeholders to translate quality and regulatory requirements into sound business decisions.
* **Drive regulatory and compliance excellence:**
 Ensure alignment between global quality standards and US regulatory requirements, particularly FDA OTC regulations and Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP).
* **Oversee contract manufacturing quality:**
 Provide quality leadership and oversight across a network of approximately 30–40 contract manufacturing partners, including key strategic suppliers.
* **Strengthen organizational capabilities:**
 Develop a technically strong team, promote greater autonomy, build leadership capabilities, and establish succession depth.
* **Partner with manufacturing leadership:**
 Work closely with plant and operational leaders to balance quality expectations with production demands, providing constructive challenge and driving continuous improvement.
* **Lead through influence:**
 Build strong relationships across a global, multicultural, and matrixed organization, including teams and stakeholders outside of the direct reporting structure.
* **Prepare the organization for future growth:**
 Build the organizational structure, capabilities, and relationships necessary to support a potentially broader international Quality remit.

**Ideal Candidate Profile**

* Extensive leadership experience in Quality within beauty, personal care, consumer health, or complex consumer goods manufacturing environments.
* Strong hands-on experience with
 **FDA OTC regulations and GMP requirements**
 .
* Proven experience leading large, multi-layered Quality organizations and developing senior leadership teams.
* Experience overseeing contract manufacturers, external manufacturing partners, and complex supplier networks.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing quality, QA, QC, laboratory operations, and Quality Management Systems.
* Commercially oriented leadership approach, with the ability to translate technical and regulatory considerations into practical business decisions.
* Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders and operate effectively within global, matrixed organizations.
* Experience balancing quality standards, operational performance, and business priorities.
* Conversational French is considered a strong advantage.

records.title: Vice President of Continuous Improvement & Lean

postedPay.title: Vice President of Continuous Improvement & Lean

records.description:
Eaton’s Electrical Sector America’s business is curretly hiring for a VP of Continuous Improvement & Lean. This role can be based at Eaton’s Cleveland or Pittsburgh office. Relocation within hiring country is offered. 50 percent travel is anticipated.
 
 
Reporting directly to the SVP of Operations, Electrical Sector – Americas (ESA), the VP of CI & Lean is the senior executive accountable for the vision, strategy, and results of the Eaton Continuous Improvement System (ECIS) across the $16B ESA business, spanning 60 manufacturing sites and 14 divisions. This role sets the multi-year Lean transformation agenda, builds continuous improvement into the sector's strategic and annual profit plans, and holds the business accountable for measurable improvement in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and growth.
 
 
The VP leads and develops the ESA CI team, defines the sector-wide operating model, standards, and governance the team deploys, and serves as a strategic advisor to the ESA leadership team. Rather than leading deployment within a division, this role directs CI resources to the highest-value opportunities, owns the sector's CI talent pipeline, and shapes a Lean leadership culture at the executive level. The VP also represents ESA in enterprise CI forums, partnering with Corporate CI & Quality to align standards and scale best practices across Eaton.
 
 
**Job Responsibilities**

* Defines the multi-year ESA Lean and continuous improvement vision, strategy, and roadmap, and integrates it into the sector's strategic plan and annual profit plan.
* Owns the ECIS operating model for ESA: sets the standards, maturity expectations, and governance that the CI team deploys across divisions, functions, and sites.
* Leads, coaches, and develops the ESA CI team; sets objectives, allocates CI resources, and holds the team accountable for results.
* Chairs the Divisional CI Council across all ESA divisions and leads sector-level performance reviews, establishing the operating cadence that links CI results to business performance.
* Accountable for the ESA cost-out and productivity commitments delivered through CI; builds the sector project pipeline and validates financial impact.
* Serves as strategic advisor to the SVP of Operations and the ESA leadership team, prioritizing the transformation initiatives with the greatest business value.
* Sponsors large-scale, cross-divisional transformations (e.g., footprint changes, acquisition integrations, and Lean in office and transactional processes).
* Builds the sector CI talent strategy: capability standards, certification pathways (e.g., ASCEND X, PME), succession planning, and rotation of high-potential leaders through CI roles.
* Coaches ESA executives on Lean leadership behaviors and role-models a culture of accountability and continuous improvement from the top.
* Sets sector maturity targets and owns the EBSA and OpA assessment strategy; reviews results with leadership and directs closure of systemic gaps.
* Represents ESA in enterprise CI forums; partners with Corporate CI & Quality to shape Eaton-wide standards and scale proven practices across sectors.
* Manages the ESA CI function budget and champions digital and data analytics tools that accelerate improvement.

**Qualifications**
Required Qualifications:
 
 

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline from an accredited institution.
* Minimum 15 years of progressive experience in Continuous Improvement, Quality, or Operations
* Minimum 5 years leading leaders (managers or directors) at a multi-site, division, or business-unit level
* Proven track record leading Lean transformations that delivered measurable financial results, preferably in a multi-division manufacturing environment
* Professional experience in a global matrixed organization
* Eaton will not consider applicants for employment immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master's degree or MBA preferred

**Position Success Criteria**

* Expert-level command of Lean and Six Sigma; Master Black Belt or Black Belt certification required
* Experience designing, governing, and maturing a business operating system and maturity model at scale
* Strong business and financial acumen: builds cost-out and productivity plans, quantifies impact, and ties CI results to the P&L
* Experience designing CI talent, certification, and capability programs across a large, multi-site organization
* Applies Lean to both manufacturing and office/transactional processes
* Executive presence; a trusted advisor who influences, challenges, and aligns senior executives
* Proven ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing teams of senior CI leaders
* Strategic thinker who turns vision into multi-year roadmaps and leads change at scale
* Excellent communication at every level, from the shop floor to the executive leadership team

The expected annual salary range for this role is $203000 - $297000 a year. This position is also eligible for a variable incentive program.
 
 
Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.
 
 
All positions may require participation in video and in-person interviews as part of the hiring process. All candidates will be evaluated based on job-related competencies, and all candidates’ privacy rights and data security will be protected in accordance with applicable laws.
 
 
We are committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of an applicant's race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, marital status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by law.
 
 
Eaton believes in second chance employment. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction history will be considered regardless of their arrest or conviction history, consistent with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act and other local laws.
 
 
You do not need to disclose your conviction history or participate in a background check until a conditional job offer is made to you. After making a conditional offer and running a background check, if Eaton is concerned about conviction that is directly related to the job, you will be given the chance to explain the circumstances surrounding the conviction, provide mitigating evidence, or challenge the accuracy of the background report.
 
 
To request a disability-related reasonable accommodation to assist you in your job search, application, or interview process, please call us at 1-800-836-6345 to discuss your specific need. Only accommodation requests will be accepted by this phone number.
 
 
We know that good benefit programs are important to employees and their families. Eaton provides various Health and Welfare benefits as well as Retirement benefits, and several programs that provide for paid and unpaid time away from work. Click here for more detail: Eaton Benefits Overview. Please note that specific programs and options available to an employee may depend on eligibility factors such as geographic location, date of hire, and the applicability of collective bargaining agreements.

records.title: Vice President of Manufacturing
records.description:
**Company Overview**

A well-established, rapidly growing manufacturing organization with a strong national presence is seeking an accomplished executive to lead its manufacturing and production operations. The company is entering an exciting phase of expansion, investing in leadership, technology, automation, and operational infrastructure to support its ambitious long-term growth objectives.

**Position Overview**

The Vice President of Manufacturing will provide strategic and operational leadership across a complex, high-volume manufacturing environment, overseeing approximately 900 employees across multiple production functions.

Reporting directly to the EVP of Operations, this executive will be responsible for developing and executing a long-term manufacturing strategy, optimizing production performance, implementing automation, and building scalable processes to support continued growth.

This is a highly visible executive leadership opportunity with significant influence over the organization's operational future.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead large-scale manufacturing and production operations, overseeing approximately 900 employees.
* Develop and execute a 1–3 year manufacturing strategy focused on growth, scalability, efficiency, and automation.
* Drive continuous improvement across manufacturing processes, production operations, and facility performance.
* Establish consistent standards for safety, quality, productivity, labor efficiency, cost, and on-time delivery.
* Identify opportunities to implement advanced manufacturing technologies, automation, and equipment improvements.
* Optimize production flow, capacity planning, labor utilization, and manufacturing processes.
* Oversee manufacturing budgets, financial performance, cost controls, and operational profitability.
* Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing leadership team, strengthening accountability and succession planning.
* Implement standardized operating procedures, performance metrics, and operational best practices.
* Partner with executive leadership to align manufacturing capabilities with business growth objectives.
* Proactively identify operational risks and ensure compliance with safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements.

**Ideal Candidate Qualifications**

* 10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including significant senior-level operational responsibility.
* Strong background in wood products manufacturing required; cabinetry or related manufacturing experience highly preferred.
* Proven experience leading large-scale, high-volume manufacturing operations across multiple departments or facilities.
* Demonstrated ability to lead and develop Directors, Managers, and large production teams.
* Strong technical knowledge of manufacturing equipment, CNC machinery, automated production systems, production flow, and process optimization.
* Proven success improving operational efficiency, production output, quality, safety, and cost performance.
* Experience implementing lean manufacturing principles, continuous improvement initiatives, and scalable operating systems.
* Strong financial acumen, including budget management, operational cost controls, and P&L responsibility.
* Strategic thinker capable of developing long-term manufacturing plans while remaining actively engaged in day-to-day operations.
* Exceptional leadership, communication, coaching, and cross-functional collaboration skills.

**Why This Opportunity?**

* Executive-level opportunity with significant influence over a rapidly expanding organization.
* Lead a large-scale manufacturing operation with approximately 900 employees.
* Drive meaningful transformation through automation, technology, and operational improvements.
* Build and develop a strong leadership team while shaping the future of manufacturing operations.
* Join an ambitious organization investing in infrastructure, operational excellence, and long-term growth.

**Compensation:**
$300,000+ executive compensation package, commensurate with experience.

records.title: VP - Test, Technology and Operations
records.description:
**Job Description**
**onsemi**
is seeking a Vice President to lead the centralized Test, Technology, and Operations (TTO) Engineering organization across Allen (TX), Bangalore, Czech Republic, and Philippines. This role is responsible for driving the test, technology, and operations strategy and execution for design for test (DFT), test automation, automated test equipment (ATE) and reliability hardware, new product introduction (NPI), COGs, factory transfers, quality and EFARs, and sustaining activities.
 
 
As the VP, Test, Technology, and Operations, you will oversee a centralized engineering organization with a charter focused on enabling scalable, reliable, and cost-effective product execution from development through sustaining. This leader will drive test strategy, operational discipline, quality improvement, and cross-functional alignment across the full TTO Engineering scope.
 
 
The ideal candidate brings acute leadership experience in test engineering, new product development, product and process quality, factory transfer execution, and global organizational leadership. This role requires a proactive, strategic leader who can maintain continuity through organizational transition, strengthen technical capability, and build an execution-focused culture across a distributed global team.
 
 
Key Function:
 
 

* Lead the centralized TTO Engineering organization across Allen, Bangalore, Czech Republic, and Philippines, ensuring alignment to test, technology, operations, cost, quality, and execution priorities.
* Own the strategy and execution for DFT, test automation, ATE and reliability hardware, NPI readiness, COGs improvement, factory transfers, quality and EFARs, and sustaining support.
* Maintain a clear centralized charter, reporting structure, and operating model while driving technical competency, execution discipline, and continuous improvement across the organization.

**Responsibilities**
Responsibilities:
 
 

* Define and drive the overall TTO Engineering strategy across design for test, test automation, ATE and reliability hardware, NPI, COGs, factory transfers, quality and EFARs, and sustaining.
* Lead centralized test technology development and standardization to improve execution efficiency, test coverage, final test yield, product quality, and cost performance.
* Drive DFT and test automation strategy to enable scalable, manufacturable, and cost-effective new product introductions.
* Oversee ATE and reliability hardware strategy, capability planning, deployment readiness, and sustaining support across product lifecycles.
* Partner with product, manufacturing, quality, and operations teams to execute factory transfers, resolve quality issues, and accelerate EFAR closure.
* Drive COGs improvement initiatives through test cost reduction, yield enhancement, process optimization, and disciplined operational execution.
* Ensure sustaining support for released products, including test coverage, reliability needs, customer issue resolution, and continuous quality improvement.
* Build and develop a high-performing global engineering organization with strong technical competency, clear accountability, and effective cross-functional collaboration.

**Qualifications**
Qualification:
 
 

* Degree in Electrical Engineering or an equivalent engineering discipline.
* 20+ years of direct leadership experience in product and test engineering.

Preferred Qualification:
 
 

* Very strong executive-level leadership
* Experience building teams and developing talent.
* Able to work effectively across functional organizations at senior levels of management.
* Strong problem-solving methodology.
* Extremely proactive with a strategic mindset.
* Effective communication skills

**About Us**
**onsemi**
(Nasdaq: ON) is driving disruptive innovations to help build a better future. With a focus on automotive and industrial end-markets, the company is accelerating change in megatrends such as vehicle electrification and safety, sustainable energy grids, industrial automation, and 5G and cloud infrastructure. With a highly differentiated and innovative product portfolio, onsemi creates intelligent power and sensing technologies that solve the world’s most complex challenges and leads the way in creating a safer, cleaner, and smarter world.
 
 
**More details about our company benefits can be found here:**
https://www.onsemi.com/careers/career-benefits
 
 
**About The Team**
We are committed to sourcing, attracting, and hiring high-performance innovators, while providing all candidates a positive recruitment experience that builds our brand as a great place to work.
 
 
**onsemi**
is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, gender identity, gender expression, or any other protected category under applicable federal, state, or local laws.
 
 
If you are an individual with a disability and require a reasonable accommodation to complete any part of the application process, or are limited in the ability or unable to access or use this online application process and need an alternative method for applying, you may contact Talent.acquisition@onsemi.com for assistance.
